TextVicārasāgara — a Hindi Advaita-Vedānta prakaraṇa by Sādhu Niścaladāsa
Sanskrit + ṭippaṇīŚrī Vāsudeva Brahmendra Sarasvatī Svāmī — Sanskrit translation AND the ṭippaṇī (footnotes) are his
EditionFirst Edition, 1964 · Bhāratī Vijayam Press, Madras
Published byŚrī Vāsudeva Brahmendra Sarasvatī Svāmī Library Committee (grantha-koṣālaya-pālaka-samiti), Māyūram
EditorsBrahmaśrī P. Pañcāpageśa Śāstrī and Varahur Kalyāṇasundara Śāstrī
Dedicated toJagadguru Śaṅkarācārya of Śrī Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha — Śrī Candraśekharendra Sarasvatī (the Paramācārya)
By the command (śrīpāda-ādeśa) of the Kāñcī Paramācārya, Śrī Vāsudeva Brahmendra Sarasvatī Svāmī — who lived some twenty-five years continuously at Māyūra-kṣetra teaching dharma and brahma-vidyā and founded a library of Veda-śāstra-itihāsa-purāṇa — rendered Sādhu Niścaladāsa's Hindi Vicārasāgara into very simple Sanskrit and adorned it with his own ṭippaṇī; it was printed and published by his library committee (scan p5).
Dedicatory verse to Śrī Candraśekharendra Sarasvatī, the Kāñcī Paramācārya (editorial front-matter, not the original text)
संचारपूतानि दिगन्तराणि कुर्वन् विवृण्वन्निगमार्थतत्त्वम् ।
संशोधयन्सर्वजनान्तरङ्गं त्वं स्मारयस्यादिजगद्गुरु नः ॥
अविरतं परकार्यकृतां सतां मधुरिमातिशयेन वचोऽमृतम् ।
अपि च मानसमम्बुनिधिर्यशो विमलशारदचन्द्रचन्द्रिका ॥
Hallowing the far quarters of the earth by your travels, unfolding the true essence of the Vedas, and purifying the innermost being of all people — you, O foremost world-teacher (ādi-jagadguru), call [the first Śaṅkara] to our remembrance.
Among the holy who labour unceasingly for others’ good, your speech is nectar by its surpassing sweetness, your mind a fathomless ocean, and your fame the moonlight of the spotless autumn moon.

ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारनियमो नास्ति पूर्वपीठिका उत्तममध्यमकनिष्ठानामधिकारिणां त्रयाणामित्थं गुरूपदेशश्रवणादिभिर्निःसंशयं अयमात्मैव ब्रह्म इत्यत्युत्तमं ज्ञानं बभूव ।
There is no fixed rule of conduct for a knower of truth — Introduction: In this way, through hearing the *guru*'s instruction and the rest, the supreme, doubt-free knowledge that 'this *ātman* alone is *Brahman*' arose among all three classes of eligible seekers: superior, middling, and lower.
त्रयाणामप्येतेषां गुरूपदेशे समानेऽपि, ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कार उत्तमस्य तत्त्वदृष्टेरेवाभूत् ।
Although the *guru*'s instruction was identical for all three, direct realisation of *Brahman* occurred immediately only for Tattvadṛṣṭi, the superior seeker.
वृक्षस्य शुष्कानि पर्णानि पतितानि यथा वायुनेतस्तत उह्यन्ते तथा प्रारब्धकर्मशेषवशात् नाना कर्म कुर्वत् ज्ञानिनः शरीरमपि इतस्ततो नीयमानमिव प्रतिभाति ।
Just as dry leaves fallen from a tree are blown hither and thither by the wind, so too the body of the *jñānin*, performing diverse actions under the momentum of remaining *prārabdha-karma*, appears as if driven here and there.
ज्ञानी हि कदाचिद्रथवाजिगजाद्यारूढः सन् वनारामादीन् पश्यति ।
Indeed, sometimes the *jñānin*, mounted on chariots, horses, elephants, and the like, views forests and gardens.
कदाचिद्विनापि पादरक्षां सञ्चरति ।
At other times he wanders about even without footwear.
तस्य शयनासनादिकमप्यव्यवस्थितमेव ।
His sleeping, sitting, and other routines are entirely without fixed rule.
तस्य कदाचिद्भोगभोजनाद्युत्तममेव भवति ।
Sometimes his food, comforts, and living arrangements turn out to be of the most exquisite quality.
कदाचिदनशन एव गिरिगुहायां वसञ्छिलातले शयानो रजनीमतिवाहयति ।
At other times, remaining completely without food, he spends the night dwelling in a mountain cave and sleeping on a bare rock slab.
कदाचित्सहस्रशस्तं पुरुषाः प्रणमन्ति ।
Sometimes people bow before him in thousands.
कदाचिदयमुभयलोकभ्रष्ट इति कर्मिभिर्निन्द्यते ।
At other times he is reviled by ritualists saying, 'This man has fallen from both worlds.'
ये तावत्तं पूजयन्ति ते तस्य सुकृतं प्राप्नुवन्ति ।
Those who honour and revere him acquire his meritorious karma.
ये तु तं दोषदृष्ट्या पश्यन्ति ते तस्य पापमश्नुवन्ति ।
Whereas those who view him with a fault-finding gaze partake of his sins.
इत्थं ज्ञानिदेहस्यानियतो व्यवहारः ।
In this manner, the outward conduct of the *jñānin*'s body has no set pattern.
तत्त्वविदो भ्रमसंशयादयो नैव सम्भवन्ति ।
For the knower of reality, error, doubt, and the like are utterly impossible.
कदाचित्कुत्रचिदपि नैवास्ति किञ्चित्कर्तव्यं तस्य ।
There is never any duty whatsoever left for him anywhere.
यतः समग्रतया तस्य भेदभ्रमभयादयो नष्टाः ।
For all notions of duality, delusion, fear, and the like have been wholly destroyed for him.
सर्वोत्तमवेदप्रमाणजनितस्वप्रकाशाद्वितीयप्रत्यग्ब्रह्मात्मापरोक्षसाक्षात्कारवान्ह्यसौ ।
Indeed, he possesses direct, immediate realisation of the self-luminous, non-dual, innermost *Brahman*-*ātman*, born of the supreme *pramāṇa* of the *Vedas*.
ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारानियमाक्षेपः॥ ४६५–४८३ ॥

ज्ञानिना समाधेः शरीरस्थितिनिर्वाहकाच्चातिरिक्ते कार्ये न प्रवृत्तियुक्तेन भाव्यमित्यत्राक्षेपः — ज्ञानिनोऽपि व्यवहारे नियमोऽस्तीति केचिद्वदन्ति ।
Here the objection that an enlightened knower ought not to engage in any activity other than samādhi and what sustains the body is raised: some assert that even for a jñānin there is a fixed rule regarding empirical action.
त्रिपुटीमात्रं दुःखनिदानमिति बुद्ध्वा तत्परित्यज्य ज्ञानी सदा समाधिनिष्ठो भवति ।
Realizing that the triad of knower, knowing, and known is the sole root of suffering, and having abandoned it, the knower remains ever established in samādhi.
यदा व्यवहारः सम्भवति तदापि सोऽपि अशनायापिपासादिप्रयोज्यभिक्षाशनजलपानादिशरीरस्थितिकारणेष्वेव ।
Even when worldly transaction takes place, that too is confined exclusively to the means of bodily maintenance, such as eating begged food and drinking water impelled by hunger, thirst, and the like.
नान्यत्र ।
Never anywhere else.
न च स विस्मरति कदाचिदपि समाधिम् ।1,2,1,2,1,2,3,4,5
Nor does he ever forget samādhi.
टिप्पणी
1.
जीवन्मुक्तिलक्षणं प्रपञ्चप्रतीतिपूर्वकं प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मचैतन्यनिष्ठत्वम् ।
The definition of jīvanmukti is being established in the inner consciousness that is Brahman even while the appearance of the phenomenal world continues.
1.
सन्न्यासिन एव ज्ञाने मुख्याधिकार इति वदन्तः शङ्करानन्दप्रभृतयः ।
Śaṅkarānanda and others assert that only a renunciant has the primary qualification for knowledge.
2.
विदेहमुक्तिलक्षणं प्रपञ्चप्रतीतिशून्यत्वे सति प्रत्यक्चैतन्यात्मना वर्तनम् ।
The definition of videhamukti is abiding as the inner consciousness-Self while there is complete absence of the cognition of the world.
सुखम् ।
It is bliss itself.
ततोऽधिकसुखाभावात् ।
Because there is no bliss superior to that.
दुःखहेतुत्वेन त्रिपुट्या उद्विजते ।
The wise person recoils from the triad (knower, knowing, known) because it is a cause of sorrow.
अतः समाध्यर्थमेव ज्ञानी भूयो भूयो यतते ।
Therefore, the jñānin strives again and again only for samādhi.
यस्तु समाधिसुखं भ्रमतो बाह्यसुखासक्त्या त्यजति स श्वगर्दभप्रेतसम एव ।
However, he who, out of delusion, abandons the bliss of samādhi due to attachment to external pleasures is indeed equal to a dog, a donkey, or a ghost.
गौडपादमाण्डूक्यकारिकायां समाधिप्रकारः सप्रपञ्चं प्रपञ्चितः ।
In the Gauḍapāda Kārikā on the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad, the nature and method of samādhi have been elaborated in full detail.
इत्थं ज्ञानी प्रपञ्चविक्षेपभ्रमं तुच्छीकृत्य सकलसुखसागरीभूतस्वरूपानन्दात्मनैवावतिष्ठते ।
Thus, the jñānin, making insignificant the delusion of worldly distraction, abides solely as the essential *ānanda* of the Self which is an ocean of all happiness.
अष्टाङ्गमन्तरेण च समाधिसुखं न लभ्यते ।
And without the eightfold yoga, the bliss of samādhi is not attained.
समाधिसुखकारणत्वादष्टाङ्गस्य ।
Because the eightfold yoga is the means to the bliss of samādhi.
असाधारणं कारणमन्तरेण च नैव कार्यमुत्पद्यते ।
And without the specific cause, an effect is never produced.
अतस्तान्युच्यन्ते श‍ृणु - (१-२) प्रत्येकं पञ्च पञ्च यमनियमौ ।
Therefore they are spoken of, listen: (1-2) Yama and Niyama, five each.
(३) अनेकविधान्यासनानि ।
(3) Postures of diverse kinds.
(४) अनेकविधाः प्राणायामाः ।
(4) Various types of breath control (prāṇāyāma).
(५) अनेकविधाः प्रत्याहाराः ।
(5) Various kinds of sense withdrawal (pratyāhāra).
(६) धारणा ।
(6) Concentration (dhāraṇā).
(७) ध्यानम् ।
(7) Meditation (dhyāna).
(८) समाधिः सविकल्पकः ।
(8) Savikalpaka-samādhi.
सम्यगस्मिन्नष्टाङ्गे साधिते, सुकरः स्यान्निर्विकल्पकः समाधिः ।
When this eightfold limb is properly mastered, nirvikalpaka-samādhi becomes easily attainable.
नान्यथा ।
Not otherwise.
अतोऽवश्यमनुष्ठेयं तत् ।
Therefore, that must necessarily be practiced.
इत्थं समाधेरवश्यानुष्ठेयतां श्रुत्वा भूताविष्टवदेतेऽन्यथा कथयन्ति इति मत्वा तत्त्वदृष्टिस्तूष्णीमनुक्त्वा किञ्चिदपि, जहास ।
Hearing thus about the obligatory nature of samādhi, Tattvadṛṣṭi thought, 'Like people possessed by spirits, these people speak incorrectly,' and remained silent without saying anything, merely smiling.
अस्यायं सिद्धान्तः - नैवास्ति नियमो ज्ञानिनः शरीरव्यवहारे ।
His settled doctrine is this: There is no restriction whatsoever on the bodily conduct of a jñānin.
तस्य हि तदा व्यवहारहेतुभूताज्ञानतत्कार्यभेदभ्रमतज्जन्यरागद्वेषादयो न सन्ति ।
For him at that stage, ignorance (which is the root cause of worldly behavior), its effects, the illusion of difference, and the desires and aversions produced by them do not exist.
किन्तु प्रारब्धं कर्मैकमेवावशिष्टम् ।
Only *prārabdha karma* alone remains.
तदेव च तदा तद्व्यवहारहेतुः ।
And that alone is then the cause of his physical behavior.
तादृशस्य च प्रारब्धकर्मणः पुरुषभेदेन नानाप्रकारत्वात् प्रारब्धकर्मजन्यज्ञानिव्यवहारोऽपि नानाप्रकार एव स्यात् न नियतः ।
And since such *prārabdha karma* is of diverse types depending on the individual, the behavior of a jñānin generated by *prārabdha karma* will also be diverse, not uniform.
अयमेव सिद्धान्तपक्षः ।
This alone is the established conclusion (siddhānta).
केचिदाहुः - ज्ञानिनो विहितकर्मानुष्ठाननियमाभावेऽपि, निषिद्धाचरणनिवृत्तौ नियमोऽस्त्येव ।
Some say: Even though there is no restriction to perform scripturally prescribed acts for a jñānin, there is certainly a rule regarding abstention from prohibited actions.
ज्ञानिनो हि प्रवृत्तिर्देहस्थितिहेतुभूतभिक्षाशनकौपीनाच्छादनमात्रग्रहण एव स्यात्, नान्यत्र ।
For the engagement of a jñānin occurs only in accepting mere alms food and a loincloth covering to sustain the body, and nowhere else.
यतः प्रागेव ज्ञानोत्पत्तेर्जिज्ञासादशायां मुमुक्षोः साधनचतुष्टयसत्त्वेन तीव्रविषयदोषदृष्टिवशाद्वैराग्यं सम्पन्नमेव ।
Because even prior to the dawn of knowledge, in the stage of earnest seeking, dispassion was already accomplished in the mumukṣu through the presence of the fourfold means and acute perception of defects in sensory objects.
तादृग्वैराग्यं ज्ञानोत्पत्त्यनन्तरमपि दोषदृष्टिबलाद्विषयमिथ्यात्वनिश्चयवशाच्च दृढतरं वर्तते ।
Such dispassion remains even firmer after the rise of knowledge, owing to the strength of perceiving defects and the firm conviction of the unreality of objects.
अद्वितीयात्मापरोक्षज्ञानबलात् अनात्मपदार्थेषु तुच्छत्वनिश्चये सति पुनः पदार्थसत्यताबुद्धिर्न जायते ।
When there is ascertainment of the voidness of non-Self objects by the power of direct realization of the non-dual Self, the notion of reality in objects never arises again.
दोषदृष्टिप्राबल्ये हि सति नैव रागो जायते ।
For when the seeing of defects is predominant, attachment never arises.
प्रवृत्तिमात्रं च रागमूलकमेव ।
And all activity is rooted solely in desire/attachment.
ज्ञानिनो रागासम्भवान्नैवास्ति प्रवृत्तिः ।
Since attachment is impossible for the jñānin, there is no worldly activity at all.
शरीरजीवनार्थभोजनादिप्रवृत्तिस्तु विनैव रागं प्रारब्धकर्माधीनतयैव जायते ।
However, activities such as eating for bodily maintenance take place solely under the sway of *prārabdha karma*, entirely devoid of attachment.
2.
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् इत्याद्यालोचनं दोषदृष्टिः ।
Reflecting on 'perception of evil/defect in birth, death, old age, disease, and misery' (Gītā 13.8) and so forth constitutes 'perception of defect' (doṣadṛṣṭi).
कर्म च सञ्चितागामिप्रारब्धभेदात् त्रिविधम् ।
And *karma* is threefold by distinction of *sañcita*, *āgāmin*, and *prārabdha*.
तत्र (१) अतीतानन्तशरीरानुष्ठितं सत् फलायानरब्धं कर्म सञ्चितं (२) वर्तमानशरीरकृतं भविष्यत् कर्मागामि ।
There: (1) action performed in countless past bodies which has not yet begun to yield fruit is *sañcita*; (2) action performed in the present body yielding fruit in the future is *āgāmin*.
(३) अतीतशरीरकृतं सत् वर्तमानशरीरहेतुभूतं (शरीरारम्भकं) कर्म प्रारब्धम् ।
(3) Action that was performed in a past body and has become the cause of the present body (the generator of the body) is *prārabdha*.
तत्र च (१) सञ्चितं ज्ञानेन विनश्यति ।
And among them: (1) *sañcita* is destroyed by knowledge.
(२) ज्ञानिन आत्मनि कर्तृत्वादिभ्रान्त्यभावान्नैवास्ति आगामि ।
(2) Because for the knower there is no delusion of agency and so forth in the Self, *āgāmin* does not exist at all.
(३) यत्तु ज्ञानिनः शरीरं जनयित्वा तत्स्थितिहेतुभूतभिक्षाशनादौ प्रवर्तयति प्रारब्धं तत् अन्तरेण भोगं न क्षीयते ।
(3) But that *prārabdha* which, having generated the knower's body, impels him into begging for food and other activities that sustain it, is not exhausted without experiencing its fruits.
क्वचिच्च (अपरोक्षानुभूतिविवेकचूडामण्यादिग्रन्थेषु) सञ्चितागामिकर्माभावन्यायबलात् ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धमपि नैव सम्भवति ।
And in certain texts (such as *Aparokṣānubhūti*, *Vivekacūḍāmaṇi*, etc.), by the logical principle of the absence of *sañcita* and *āgāmin* karma, even *prārabdha* is not possible for the knower.
अतो भोजनादिप्रवृत्तिरपि तस्य न युज्यते इति यदुच्यते ।
As for what is said: 'Therefore, even activity such as eating is not appropriate for him' —
तत्रायमभिप्रायः - ज्ञानिनः स्वदृष्ट्या स्वात्मनि क्रियातत्फलसम्बन्धो नास्त्येव ।
Here this is the intended purport: From the knower's own standpoint, there is no connection whatsoever with action or its fruit in his own Self.
तस्मात्सर्वकर्मप्रतिषेधः प्रारब्धप्रतिषेधश्च स्वात्मनि क्रियते, न तु ज्ञानिनः शरीरे भोगमेव नोत्पादयतीति ।
Therefore, the negation of all *karma* and the negation of *prārabdha* is stated with respect to one's own Self, not that it produces no experience at all in the knower's body.
यतो (१) ज्ञानिनः सञ्चितं कर्म ज्ञानेन नश्यति ।
Because (1) the knower's *sañcita* karma is destroyed by knowledge;
(२) आगामिनस्तु कर्मणः सम्बन्ध एव नास्ति ।
(2) of *āgāmin* karma there is no connection whatsoever;
(३) प्रारब्धं तु भोगत एव नश्यति नान्यथा ।
(3) but *prārabdha* is destroyed only through experience, not otherwise.
अयमेव च सूत्रकाराद्यभिप्रायः ।
And this indeed is the intended purport of the Sūtrakāra (Bādarāyaṇa) and others.
तस्मात्प्रारब्धवशाच्छरीरपोषणादिनिर्वाहकक्रियादिषु, ज्ञानिनः प्रवृत्तिः स्यादेव ।
Therefore, on account of *prārabdha*, the knower's activity in sustaining actions such as nourishing the body does indeed occur.
अन्यत्र तु न स्यात् ।
In other things, however, it would not occur.
1.
कुसूलस्थधान्यं पुनः पुनः पूर्यमाणं क्रमेण भुज्यमानं यथा, तथानेकजन्मार्जितमन्तःकरणोपहितसाक्ष्यज्ञानावरणशक्तिनिष्ठं कर्म सञ्चितम् ।
Just as grain kept in a granary is repeatedly filled and gradually consumed, so too the *karma* accumulated across many births, residing in the veiling power (*āvaraṇa-śakti*) of *avidyā* pertaining to the *sākṣin* conditioned by the *antaḥkaraṇa*, is *sañcita*.
2.
वर्तमानशरीरकृतमितः परं कालान्तरफलप्रदं कर्मागामि ।
Action done by the present body which gives fruit at a later time from now is *āgāmin*.
कृषिस्थधान्यवत् ।
Like grain standing in a field.
3.
एतेष्वेव यत्किञ्चित्परिपक्वं सत् वर्तमानशरीरद्वारा सुखदुःखप्रदत्वेनाज्ञानविक्षेपशक्त्याश्रयि कर्म प्रारब्धम् ।
That portion among these which has ripened and, residing in the projecting power (*vikṣepa-śakti*) of *avidyā*, delivers pleasure and pain through the present body, is *prārabdha*.
अन्नभूतधान्यवत् ।
Like grain that has been made into food.
4.
असङ्गोऽहमकर्ताभोक्ता इति निश्चयबलाज्ज्ञानिनः कर्मलेपो न सम्भवति ।
On the strength of the conviction 'I am unattached, non-doer, and non-experiencer', the taint of *karma* is not possible for the knower.
कर्तृत्वाद्यभिमानेन फलाभिलाषिण एव कर्मफलसुखादिसम्बन्धः ।
The connection with the pleasure and other experiences resulting from *karma* belongs only to one who desires fruit through the egoistic identification with agency and so forth.
5.
सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति, वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यः इत्यादिश्रुतिस्मृतिशतेभ्यः सर्वशास्त्राणां निर्विशेषाद्वितीयब्रह्मात्मचैतन्ये तात्पर्यमध्यवसितम् ।
From hundreds of Śruti and Smṛti passages such as 'That goal which all the Vedas declare' and 'I alone am to be known through all the Vedas', it is determined that the purport of all scriptures lies in the attributeless, non-dual consciousness of the *ātman* as *Brahman*.
एतज्ज्ञानाधिकारी त्वष्टाचत्वारिंशत्संस्कारसंस्कृतोऽनन्तकोटिजन्मसु परमेश्वरप्रसादमहिम्ना नितान्तनिर्मलीकृतान्तःकरणः कृतकृत्यो विषयेषु मलमूत्रनरकादिब्रह्मलोकान्तेषु सुविरक्तः ।
The qualified aspirant for this knowledge, however, is one purified by the forty-eight sacramental rites, whose mind has been rendered utterly pure through the majesty of the grace of the Supreme Lord over infinite millions of births, who has accomplished all that was to be done, and who is thoroughly dispassionate towards objects ranging from feces, urine, and hell up to Brahmaloka.
नास्य किञ्चिदप्यन्यदणुमात्रमज्ञानादिकमस्ति ।
For him there remains not the slightest trace of ignorance and its effects, not even of the measure of an atom.
कुतः प्रारब्धकल्पनावकाशः ।
Whence then could there be any room for positing *prārabdha*?
अज्ञानमेव न कुतो जगतः प्रसङ्गो जीवेशदेशिकविकल्पकथातिदूरे ।
When *avidyā* itself does not exist, whence any occasion for the world? The talk of distinctions between *jīva*, *Īśvara*, and the teacher is far removed indeed.
एकान्तनिर्मलचिदेकरसस्वरूपं ब्रह्मैव केवलमहं परिपूर्णमस्मि ॥
I am solely the plenary *Brahman* alone, whose nature is the single essence of consciousness, absolutely pure.
वस्तुतो नास्ति चाज्ञानं चित्प्रकाशविरोधतः । अतोऽज्ञानं न चाज्ञानबाधकञ्च निरूपणे ॥ एकं ब्रह्मैव नैवान्यदिति मे निश्चिता मतिः ॥
'In reality, ignorance does not exist at all, because it is opposed to the light of consciousness. Therefore, upon investigation, there is neither ignorance nor the sublater of ignorance; Brahman alone is one, nothing else exists at all — such is my firm conviction.'
ननु क्रियाकारकफलरूपस्य प्रपञ्चस्य भेदमपि श्रुतिः प्रतिपादयति आत्मन आकाशः सम्भूतः, ज्योतिष्टोमेन स्वर्गकामो यजेत इत्यादिना ।
[Objection]: But does not Śruti also propound difference in the manifold world consisting of action, instruments, and fruits through passages such as 'From the Ātman, space arose' and 'He who desires heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma'?
तत्कथं सर्वस्य ब्रह्मात्मत्वमिति चेत् ।
If it is asked: how then is everything identical with *Brahman* as *ātman*?
अत्रोच्यते ।
Here it is replied:
साक्षादर्थस्वभावेन श्रुतिः सेयं प्रवर्तते । श्रोतुश्चित्तविपाकेन विषण्णा विवशा श्रुतिः ॥ इति ।
'This Śruti proceeds directly according to the true nature of reality; but, despondent and helpless on account of the state of maturity of the hearer's mind, Śruti adapts.'
ऐतदात्म्यमिदं सर्वम् इत्येषा श्रुतिरर्थस्वभावेन परमार्थस्वाभाव्येन न साक्षाद्विद्यमानमेवार्थं प्रतिपादयितुं प्रवृत्ता ।
This Śruti passage, 'All this has this [Self] as its essence', sets out to propound by the inherent nature of reality — that is, by the nature of absolute reality — the truly existing reality alone, not directly anything else.
ईदृग्विधस्यार्थस्यासंस्कृतचित्तैर्दुरधिगमत्वात् ।
Because such a truth is hard to grasp for those of unpurified minds,
तच्चित्तपरिपाकानुसारेण भेदश्रुतिर्मायामयव्यवहारसिद्धं भेदमनुवदन्ती साध्यसाधनफलादिलक्षणं जगद्वैचित्र्यं प्रतिपादयति ।
Śruti that speaks of difference, restating the difference established in transactional experience fabricated by *māyā* in accordance with the maturation of their minds, sets forth the variegated universe characterized by means, ends, and fruits.
न परमार्थत इत्यर्थः ।
This means: not from the absolute standpoint.
सोपानक्रमतो देवा मन्दं मन्दं हितं नृणाम् । उपदिश्य विषण्णापि पुनः पक्वाधिकारिणः ॥ ऐतदात्म्यमिदं सर्वमित्याह परमाद्वयम् । जगज्जीवेश्वरत्वादिविचित्रविभवं विना ॥ केवलं चित्सदानन्दब्रह्मात्मैक्यपरा श्रुतिः । जगज्जीवेश्वरत्वादि सर्वं ब्रह्मैव केवलम् ॥ इति स्वपूर्णताज्ञानं परमाद्वैतवेदनम् । इतोऽन्यद्यत्परिज्ञानं तदज्ञानं न संशयः ॥ विचारेणायमेवार्थस्त्वविचारेण नैव हि । न कदाचिद्विशेषोऽस्तीत्येतज्ज्ञानं सुदुर्लभम् ॥
'Instructing men gradually step by step for their benefit, Śruti, though distressed [by their unpreparedness], declares to the mature aspirant supreme non-duality: 'All this is of the nature of the Self', without any variegated display of world, *jīva*, or *Īśvara*. Śruti is solely intent on the oneness of *Brahman* and *ātman* as consciousness, existence, and bliss: world, *jīva*, *Īśvara*, etc. are all pure *Brahman* alone. Such knowledge of one's own fullness is the supreme realization of non-duality; whatever cognition is other than this is ignorance, without doubt. Through inquiry, this alone is the reality, but through non-inquiry it appears otherwise; the knowledge that 'never is there any differentiation' is exceedingly rare.'
सुदुर्लभं निर्विशेषब्रह्मात्मैक्यसाक्षात्कारस्य वर्णाश्रमधर्मपरितोषितपरमेश्वरप्रसादैकसमधिगम्यत्वादित्यर्थः ।
'Exceedingly rare' means: because direct realization of the oneness of the attributeless *Brahman* and *ātman* can be attained solely through the grace of the Supreme Lord, who is pleased by the performance of the duties of one's *varṇa* and *āśrama*.
परमार्थसत्तैवैका श्रुतिसम्मता ।
Absolute reality alone is the single reality approved by Śruti.
तद्रीत्या मायायास्तुच्छत्वेन प्रारब्धकर्मादिकं न सम्भवति ।
According to that view, since *māyā* is utterly non-existent (*tuccha*), *prārabdha karma* and the like are not possible at all.
अनिर्वचनीयप्रातिभासिकसत्ताभ्युपगमेऽपि मायायाः, प्रारब्धं नैव युज्यते ।
Even if one admits an inexplicable (*anirvacanīya*) or apparent (*prātibhāsika*) reality for *māyā*, *prārabdha* is not tenable at all.
नादबिन्दूपनिषदि- उत्पन्ने तत्त्वविज्ञाने प्रारब्धं नैव मुञ्चति । तत्त्वज्ञानोदयादूर्ध्वं प्रारब्धं नैव विद्यते ॥ देहादीनामसत्त्वात्तु यथा स्वप्ने विबोधतः । कर्मजन्मान्तरीयं यत्प्रारब्धमिति कीर्तितम् ॥ तत्तु जन्मान्तराभावात्पुंसो नैवास्ति कर्हिचित् । स्वप्नदेहो यथाध्यस्तस्तथैवायं हि देहकः ॥ अध्यस्तस्य कुतो जन्म जन्माभावे कुतः स्थितिः । उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य मृद्भाण्डस्येव पश्यति ॥ अज्ञानञ्चेति वेदान्तैस्तस्मिन्नष्टे क्व विश्वता । यथा रज्जुं परित्यज्य सर्पं गृह्णाति वै भ्रमात् ॥ रज्जुखण्डे परिज्ञाते सर्परूपं न तिष्ठति ॥ अधिष्ठाने तथा ज्ञाते प्रपञ्चे शून्यतां गते । देहस्यापि प्रपञ्चत्वात् प्रारब्धावस्थितिः कुतः ॥ अज्ञानिजनबोधार्थं प्रारब्धमिति चोच्यते ॥ इति ।
In the Nādabindu Upaniṣad: 'Once knowledge of reality has arisen, *prārabdha* does not linger at all; subsequent to the dawn of knowledge of reality, *prārabdha* simply does not exist. Owing to the non-existence of the body etc., just as upon waking from a dream, that karma of another birth which is celebrated as *prārabdha* does not exist for the person at all, because of the absence of other births. Just as the dream-body is superimposed, so indeed is this waking body. Whence can there be birth for what is superimposed? And in the absence of birth, whence continuance? Vedānta views ignorance as the material cause of the world, just as clay is of a pot; when that ignorance is destroyed, where is worldhood? Just as one mistakenly takes a rope to be a snake due to delusion, but when the piece of rope is recognized, the snake-form no longer remains; so too, when the substratum is known and the world dissolves into nothingness, since the body is also part of the world, whence can there be any continuance of *prārabdha*? *Prārabdha* is spoken of only for the instruction of the ignorant.'
अध्यात्मोपनिषदि ज्ञानोदयात् पुरारब्धं कर्म ज्ञानान्न नश्यति इति स्फुटतयावेद्यते ।
In the Adhyātma Upaniṣad, the objection 'Karma begun prior to the rise of knowledge does not perish by knowledge' is clearly raised and addressed.
अदत्वा स्वफलं लक्ष्यमुद्दिश्योत्सृष्टबाणवत् । व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ ॥ न तिष्ठति भिनत्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् । अजरोऽस्म्यमरोऽस्मीति य आत्मानं प्रपद्यते ॥ तदात्मना तिष्ठतोऽस्य कुतः प्रारब्धकल्पना । प्रारब्धं सिध्यति तदा यदा देहात्मना स्थितिः ॥ देहात्मभावो नैवेष्टः प्रारब्धं त्यज्यतामतः । प्रारब्धकल्पनाप्यस्य देहस्य भ्रान्तिरेव हि ॥ अध्यस्तस्य कुतः सत्त्वमसत्यस्य कुतो जनिः । अजातस्य कुतो नाशः प्रारब्धमसतः कुतः ॥ ज्ञानेनाज्ञानकार्यस्य समूलस्य लयो यदि । तिष्ठत्ययं कथं देह इति शङ्कावतो जडान् ॥ समाधातुं बाह्यदृष्ट्या प्रारब्धं वदति श्रुतिः । न तु देहादिसत्यत्वबोधनाय विपश्चिताम् ॥ परिपूर्णमानद्यन्तमप्रमेयमविक्रियम् । सद्घनं चिद्घनं नित्यमानन्दघनमव्ययम् ॥ प्रत्यगेकरसं पूर्णमनन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् । अहेयमनुपादेयमनाधेयमनाश्रयम् ॥ इत्यादि ।
'[It is replied:] Just as an arrow shot aiming at a target does not stop without delivering its effect, even if released with the thought that the target is a tiger and discovered afterwards to be a cow, but forcefully pierces the target with momentum — so too the bodily continuance appears. Yet for him who realizes the Self saying 'I am ageless, I am immortal', and abides as that Self, whence is there any conception of *prārabdha*? *Prārabdha* is established only when there is identification with the body. Identification with the body is not accepted at all; therefore let *prārabdha* be discarded. The positing of *prārabdha* for this body is mere delusion. Whence reality for the superimposed? Whence birth for the unreal? Whence destruction for the unborn? Whence *prārabdha* for the non-existent? Śruti speaks of *prārabdha* from an external viewpoint only to console the dull-witted who doubt, 'If all effects of ignorance are dissolved root and all by knowledge, how does this body remain?' — not to teach the reality of the body etc. to the wise. [For the Self is] all-full, without beginning or end, immeasurable, immutable, pure Being, pure Consciousness, eternal, pure Bliss, imperishable, the inner single essence, infinite, all-pervading, impossible to abandon or acquire, without support and needing none...' and so on.
एतदेवापरोक्षानुभूतिविवेकचूडामण्यादौ च प्रतिपादितम् ।
This very point has been propounded in works such as *Aparokṣānubhūti* and *Vivekacūḍāmaṇi*.
दृष्टिसृष्ट्येकजीववादयोः प्रपञ्चस्य स्वप्नमनोरथशुक्तिरजतादिवदज्ञातसत्त्वाभावात्, ज्ञानेनाज्ञाननाशे समूलनाश एव सर्वस्य स्यात् ।
In the doctrines of *Dṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-vāda* and *Eka-jīva-vāda*, because the world, like a dream, daydreams, or shell-silver, has no existence when unperceived (*ajñāta-sattva*), when ignorance is destroyed by knowledge, complete destruction with root of all things occurs.
नाणुमात्रमविशष्येत ।
Not even the measure of an atom would remain.
द्वैतमात्रस्याज्ञानमूलत्वात् ।
Because all duality has its sole root in *avidyā*.
तथा चोक्तं सिद्धान्तलेशसङ्ग्रहे - सर्वज्ञात्मगुरवस्तु विरोधिसाक्षात्कारोदये लेशतोऽप्यविद्यानुवृत्त्यसम्भवात् जीवन्मुक्तिशास्त्रं श्रवणादिविध्यर्थवादमात्रं शास्त्रस्य जीवन्मुक्तिप्रतिपादने प्रयोजनाभावात् । अतः कृतनिदिध्यासनस्य ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कारोदयमात्रेण सविलासवासनाविद्यानिवृत्तिरित्यपि कञ्चित्पक्षमाहुरिति (सू. भा. री. ३.८.३०) ।
And so it is stated in the *Siddhāntaleśasaṅgraha*: 'Preceptor Sarvajñātmamuni, however, states a certain view: since upon the rise of the contradictory direct realization not even a trace of *avidyā* can continue, the scriptures on *jīvanmukti* are mere *arthavāda* for the injunction of *śravaṇa* and the like, as the scripture has no distinct purpose in propounding *jīvanmukti*. Therefore, for one who has practiced *nididhyāsana*, by the mere rise of the realization of *Brahman*, there is the cessation of *avidyā* together with its effects and latent impressions' (Sūtra-bhāṣya-rīti 3.8.30).
कल्पितस्याज्ञातसत्त्वाभावात् दृष्ट्यदृष्टभ्यामुत्पत्तिलयावुक्तौ ।
Because that which is imagined has no existence when unperceived, origination and dissolution are stated to be coextensive with perception and non-perception.
व्यावहारिकसत्त्वे त्वनास्था श्रुतेः इत्यानन्दगिरिटीकायाम् ।
'Śruti, however, has no regard for empirical reality' — thus in the sub-commentary of Ānandagiri.
रामानन्दीयायां तु स्वप्नवत्कल्पितस्याज्ञातसत्त्वाभावात् दर्शनं सृष्टिः । अदर्शनं लय इति दृष्टिसृष्टिपक्षः श्रुत्यभिप्रेत इति भावः इति ।
In the *Rāmānandīya*, however: 'Since what is imagined has no unperceived existence just like a dream, perception is creation, and non-perception is dissolution — thus the doctrine of *Dṛṣṭi-sṛṣṭi* is intended by Śruti: this is the purport.'
अतः प्रातिभासिकपक्षे अविद्यालेशस्य ज्ञानान्नाशानन्तरमवस्थित्यसम्भवात्प्रारब्धकथानवकाश एव ।
Therefore, in the *prātibhāsika* (apparent-reality) position, since a trace of *avidyā* cannot possibly remain after destruction by knowledge, there is indeed no room at all for any talk of *prārabdha*.
व्यावहारिके प्रतिकर्मव्यवस्थायामेव सृष्ट्यादिश्रुतिजीवन्मुक्तिशास्त्रादिनिरूपणावकाशः ।
Only in the empirical framework, within the arrangement of distinct objects and experiences (*pratikarma-vyavasthā*), is there room for setting forth Śruti passages on creation and treatises on *jīvanmukti*.
इत्थमधिकारित्रायाणा-॥
Thus, of the three kinds of qualified aspirants...
466 · अत्राक्षेपः
कर्म हि अनेकप्रकारकम् ।
Karma is indeed of many varieties.
एकशरीरारम्भकमेकं कर्म ।
One kind of *karma* initiates only a single physical body.
अनेकशरीरारम्भकमेकं कर्मेति ।
While another kind of *karma* brings about multiple successive bodies.
तत्र एकमेव कर्म यत्रानेकशरीराणि आरभते तत्र तादृशकर्मफलभूतप्रथमशरीर एव ज्ञानोत्पत्तौ सत्यामपि ज्ञानिनः शरीरान्तराण्यपि तत्फलभूतानि सम्भवेयुः ।
Now, where a single *karma* initiates multiple bodies, even if liberation-granting knowledge arises in the very first body yielded by that *karma*, further bodies resulting from that very same *karma* might still have to be taken by the *jñānin*.
अन्तरेण भोगं प्रारब्धं कर्म नैव नश्यति ।
For without being experienced through enjoyment and suffering, *prārabdha-karma* is never exhausted.
467 · तत्र समाधानं
प्रारब्धकर्मफलभूतानि यावन्ति शरीराणि तावन्त्यपि ज्ञानिनः शरीराणि भवन्त्येव ।
As many bodies as are the result of prārabdha karma, so many bodies indeed come to be for the *jñānin*.
प्रारब्धभोगयोग्यादधिकं शरीरं न जायेत ।
No body in excess of what is suitable for the enjoyment of *prārabdha* would be born.
तेन ज्ञानमपि सफलमिति यदि कश्चित्समाधानं ब्रूयात्, तन्न युज्यते ।
If someone were to offer the resolution that 'thereby knowledge too is fruitful', that is not tenable.
वेदस्यायं सिद्धान्तः - ज्ञानिनः प्राणा लोकान्तरं वास्मिन् लोके देहान्तरं वा न प्राप्नुवन्ति ।
This is the settled conclusion of the Veda: the vital airs of the *jñānin* do not reach another world, nor another body in this world.
अपि तु अत्रैवान्तःकरणमिन्द्रियाणि च सम्प्रलीयन्ते ।
On the contrary, right here the inner organ and the senses dissolve completely.
प्राणस्य गमनं विना शरीरान्तरं न प्राप्यते ।
Without the departure of the *prāṇa*, another body cannot be obtained.
तस्मात् ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धशेषबलाच्छरीरान्तरं जायेतेति कथनं न सम्भवति ।
Therefore, the statement that another body would be born for the *jñānin* by the force of remaining *prārabdha* is not possible.
इदं त्वत्र समाधानं - यत्र एकेन कर्मणा अनेकशरीराणि जायन्ते, उत्तममध्यमाधमानामुपदेशभेदेन विविच्य विषयः श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणेतिहासादिसर्वग्रन्थानां विज्ञेयो गुरुमुखात् ।
This, however, is the resolution here: where multiple bodies arise from a single karma, the subject-matter of all texts including Śruti, Smṛti, Purāṇa, and Itihāsa must be understood from the mouth of the Guru by discriminating the difference in instruction for superior, middling, and inferior aspirants.
नान्यथा ।
Not otherwise.
इष्टसिध्यभावेऽपि पतनप्रसङ्गात् ।
Because otherwise, in the absence of attaining the desired goal, there would be the contingency of downfall.
तथा चोक्तम्- माया ह्यचिन्त्यानिर्वाच्या जगज्जन्मादिकारिणी । अदृश्या परमानर्थहेतुर्दुर्घटकारिणी ॥ लौकिकास्तां हि मन्यन्ते वास्तवीं युक्तिशालिनः । नरोऽनिर्वचनीयां तु तुच्छां श्रौतात्मवेदिनः ॥ अतः श्रौतमतौ सत्यां मायायास्तुच्छतावशात् । सुखेन ब्रह्मविज्ञानं सिद्ध्येदेव न संशयः ॥ (गुरुज्ञानवा-च. प. ४.१५.५७.५९)
And likewise it has been said: 'Māyā is indeed unthinkable, indeterminable, causing the creation etc. of the world, invisible, the source of supreme misery, and the maker of the impossible. Ordinary worldly people consider her real; the rationalists consider her indeterminable (*anirvacanīyā*); but knowers of the Self revealed in Śruti know her to be utterly non-existent (*tucchā*). Therefore, when the Śruti view is established, on account of the total unreality of Māyā, the knowledge of Brahman is easily accomplished without doubt.' (Guru-jñāna-vāsiṣṭha / Pañcadaśī 4.15, 57, 59)
इत्थं लौकिकदृष्ट्यैतत् सर्वैरप्यनुभूयते । युक्तिदृष्ट्या त्वनिर्वाच्या नासदासीदिति श्रुतेः ॥ प. चि. १२८॥
'Thus from the worldly viewpoint this is experienced by everyone; but from the viewpoint of reasoning it is *anirvacanīyā* (indescribable), on the authority of the Śruti passage 'It was neither non-existent [nor existent]'.' (Pañcadaśī, Citradīpa 128)
नासदासीद्विभातत्वान्नो सदासीच्च बाधनात् । विद्यादृष्ट्या श्रुतं तुच्छं तस्य नित्यनिवृत्तितः ॥ १२९॥
'It was not non-existent because it was perceived; nor was it existent because it is sublated. From the viewpoint of knowledge (*vidyā-dṛṣṭi*), it is declared by Śruti to be utterly unreal (*tuccha*) because of its eternal non-existence.' (Pañcadaśī 6.129)
तुच्छानिर्वचनीया च वास्तवी चेत्यसौ त्रिधा । ज्ञेया माया त्रिभिर्बोधैः श्रौतयौक्तिकलौकिकैः ॥ १३०॥1,2,1
'Māyā is to be understood in three ways—as non-existent (*tucchā*), indeterminable (*anirvacanīyā*), and real (*vāstavī*)—by three kinds of understanding: Scriptural (*śrauta*), logical (*yauktika*), and empirical (*laukika*).' (Pañcadaśī 6.130)
टिप्पणी
1.
न तस्य प्राणा उत्क्रामन्ति ॥ अत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते (बृ. ४.४.६-७) इति श्रुतेः ।
On account of the Śruti text: 'His vital airs do not depart... here itself he attains Brahman' (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.4.6-7).
2.
ब्रह्महत्यादिकमेकमपि कर्म नरकानुभवानन्तरं श्वसृगालसर्पाद्यनेकजन्महेतुत्वेन स्मृतिपुराणादिप्रसिद्धम् ।
Even a single deed such as killing a brahmin is well known in the Smṛtis and Purāṇas as being the cause of multiple births as dogs, jackals, snakes, etc., after the experience of hell.
कृत्तिकाशुद्धपूर्णिमायां स्वामिदर्शने कृते धनादिसम्पद्विशिष्टः सप्तजन्मसु ब्राह्मणो जायत इति च ।
And it is also stated that when the vision of Lord Svāmī (Kārttikeya) is performed on the pure full-moon day of Kṛttikā, one is born as a brahmin endowed with wealth and prosperity across seven births.
इत्थमनेकजन्महेतुभूतमेकमेव कर्म प्रारब्धरूपेण फल-॥
In this manner, a single karma that becomes the cause of multiple births [begins to yield] fruit in the form of prārabdha...
तत्र चरम एव जन्मनि ज्ञानं जायेत, न तु पूर्वतनशरीरेषु ।
In that case, knowledge can arise only in the final birth, and not in the preceding bodies.
अनेकशरीरप्रदप्रारब्धस्य तत्र प्रतिबन्धकत्वात् ।
Because the prārabdha that grants multiple bodies acts as an obstacle to knowledge in those previous births.
यथा (१) विषयासक्तिः, (२) बुद्धिमान्द्यम्, (३) भेदवादिद्वैतशास्त्रवचनविश्वासश्चेत्यादिर्ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धः तथा ॥ दानादागामिप्रतिबन्धो भवति ।
Just as (1) attachment to sense objects, (2) dullness of intellect, and (3) faith in the words of dualistic scriptures taught by dualists, etc., constitute obstacles to knowledge, similarly, a future obstacle arises from the impending fruition of such karma.
श्रवणादिविचाररूपज्ञानसाधने प्रवृत्तस्यापि पुरुषस्येदृशप्रतिबन्धे सति नैव ज्ञानं जायते ।
Even for a person engaged in the means of knowledge in the form of inquiry like śravaṇa etc., when such an obstacle exists, knowledge certainly does not arise.
तस्मात् एतत्कर्मफलभूतचरमजन्मन्येव भाविप्रतिबन्धाभावात् ज्ञानमुत्पद्यते ।
Therefore, knowledge arises only in the final birth resulting from this karma, because there is no remaining future obstacle.
जन्मान्तरानुष्ठितं श्रवणादिकमपि तदा तत्रोपकरोतीति तदपि न निष्फलम् ।
Even the śravaṇa and other practices performed in a previous life come to assist at that time, and hence that practice is never fruitless.
भरतस्य प्रारब्धं जन्मत्रयस्य हेतुरभूत् ।
The prārabdha of Bharata was the cause of three births.
सत्यामपि साधनसामग्र्यां नाभूत्तस्य ज्ञानम् ।
Even though all the means were present, knowledge did not arise for him (in the intermediate births).
तृतीये तु जन्मनि विनाप्युपदेशं जन्मान्तरकृतश्रवणादिबलात्समजायत ज्ञानम् ।
In the third birth, however, even without direct instruction, knowledge arose purely through the strength of śravaṇa and reflection practiced in a prior birth.
1.
बुद्धिमान्द्यविशिष्टविषयासक्तिकुतर्कविपर्ययदुराग्रहाख्यो वर्तमानः प्रतिबन्धः ।
The present obstacle (vartamāna-pratibandha) is known by the names of dullness of intellect, intense attachment to sense-objects, fallacious reasoning, misconception, and stubborn dogma.
पुत्रवित्तदारादीष्टवस्तुनाशानन्तरमपि तत्स्मरणात्मको भूतप्रतिबन्धः ।
The past obstacle (bhūta-pratibandha) consists of the lingering remembrance of dear objects such as sons, wealth, and wife, even after they have been lost.
ब्रह्मलोकादिलोकान्तरभोगेच्छा, अथवा भाविजन्महेतुभूतप्रारब्धकर्मशेष आगामी प्रतिबन्धः ।
The future obstacle (āgāmi-pratibandha) is the desire for enjoyment in other worlds such as Brahmaloka, or the remaining remnant of prārabdha karma that gives rise to a future birth.
तथा चोक्तं पञ्चदश्यां (९.३२-४६) विचार्याप्यापरोक्ष्येण ब्रह्मात्मानं न वेत्ति चेत् । आपरोक्ष्यावसानत्वाद्भूयो भूयो विचारयेत् ॥ विचारयन्नामरणान्नैवात्मानं लभेत चेत् । जन्मान्तरे लभेतैव प्रतिबन्धक्षये सति ॥ इह वामुत्र वा विद्येत्येवं सूत्रकृतोदितम् । शृण्वन्तोऽप्यत्र बहवो यन्न विद्युरिति श्रुतिः ॥ गर्भ एव शयानः सन् वामदेवोऽवबुद्धवान् । पूर्वाभ्यस्तविचारेण यद्वदध्ययनादिषु ॥ बहुवारमधीतेऽपि सदा नायाति चेत्पुनः । दिनान्तरेऽनधीत्यैव पूर्वाधीतं स्मरेत्पुमान् ॥ कालेन परिपच्यन्ते कृषिगर्भादयो यथा । तद्वदात्मविचारोऽपि शनैः कालेन पच्यते ॥ पुनः पुनर्विचारेऽपि त्रिविधप्रतिबन्धतः । न वेत्ति तत्त्वमित्येतत् वार्तिके सम्यगीरितम् ॥ कुतस्तज्ज्ञानमिति चेत् तद्धि बन्धपरिक्षयात् । असावपि च भूतो वा भावी वा वर्ततेऽथवा ॥ अधीतवेदवेदार्थोऽप्यत एव न मुच्यते । हिरण्यनिधिदृष्टान्तादिदमेव हि दर्शितम् ॥ अतीतेनापि महिषीस्नेहेन प्रतिबन्धतः । भिक्षुस्तत्त्वं न वेदेति गाथा लोके प्रगीयते ॥ अनुसृत्य गुरुः स्नेहं महिष्यां तत्त्वमुक्तवान् । ततो यथावद्वेदैष प्रतिबन्धस्य सङ्क्षयात् ॥
And likewise it is stated in the Pañcadaśī (9.32–46): 'If even after inquiring one does not directly know Brahman as the Self, he should inquire again and again, since inquiry has direct realization as its terminus. If inquiring even until death he does not realize the Self, he will surely attain it in another birth upon the destruction of the obstacle. The author of the Sūtras has declared: 'Knowledge arises either in this life or the next.' The Śruti also says: 'Many who hear of it do not know it.' Sage Vāmadeva, even while lying in the womb, became enlightened through the inquiry practiced in his previous life, just as in secular study, etc. If, despite studying many times, a lesson is not remembered at that moment, on another day a person recalls what was previously studied even without restudying. Just as agriculture and gestation mature in due course of time, so too Self-inquiry ripens gradually over time. Despite repeated inquiry, one does not know the Truth owing to the threefold obstacle; this is accurately stated in the Vārttika. If it is asked: 'Whence does that knowledge arise?', the answer is: 'From the complete elimination of obstacles'—and this obstacle is either past, future, or present. For this very reason, one who has studied the Vedas and their meaning is still not liberated; this is demonstrated through the analogy of the hidden gold treasure. There is a popular traditional story sung in the world that a monk could not know the Truth owing to the obstacle of past attachment to a she-buffalo. The Guru, adapting his teaching to the monk's attachment to the she-buffalo, imparted the Truth through that medium; thereupon, upon the destruction of the obstacle, the monk realized the Truth as it is.'
विलक्षणप्रारब्धम् अपि ज्ञानप्रतिबन्धकम् एव ।
An extraordinary *prārabdha* is also indeed an obstacle to knowledge.
प्रतिबन्धकसद्भावदशायां क्रियमाणं ज्ञानसाधनीभूतं श्रवणमननादिकं सर्वं प्रतिबन्धकनिवृत्त्यनन्तरमेव चिरकालप्रतिबद्धमपि प्रथमजन्मकृतमेव सत् शरीरान्तरे ज्ञानमुत्पादयति ।
All the practices such as *śravaṇa* and *manana*, performed as means to knowledge while an obstacle was still present, will—despite having been blocked for a long time—generate knowledge in another body only after the cessation of that obstacle, though performed in an earlier life.
तद्यथा वामदेवस्य किलर्षेः पूर्वजन्मनि कृतश्रवणादेरपि प्रारब्धकर्मफलभूतेनैकेन शरीरेण शेषभूतेन बलवता प्रतिबन्धान्न ज्ञानमुद्भूतं श्रवणाद्यनुष्ठानदशायामेव ।
Thus, for example, in the case of sage Vāmadeva, even though he had performed *śravaṇa* etc. in a previous birth, knowledge did not arise at the very time of performing *śravaṇa* owing to a powerful remaining obstacle in the form of one intermediate body that was the fruit of *prārabdha karma*.
शरीरपातेन शरीरान्तरप्राप्तिसमये पूर्वजन्मकृतमेव श्रवणादिकं तस्य गर्भ एव ज्ञानं जनयति स्म ।
Upon the demise of that body, at the time of taking another body, that very *śravaṇa* etc. performed in the previous birth produced knowledge in him even while still in the womb.
तस्माज्ज्ञानानन्तरं शरीरान्तरसम्बन्धो नैव स्यात् ।
Therefore, after the dawn of knowledge, there can be no connection with another body at all.
ज्ञानिनो वर्तमानशरीरचेष्टा तु प्रारब्धकर्माधीनतया जायते ।
The physical activities in the current body of the enlightened person occur solely under the influence of *prārabdha karma*.
तत्रापि शरीरनिर्वाहकत्वेन यावदाक्षिप्तं कर्म तावदेव स्यात् ।
Even there, only as much activity takes place as is necessitated by karma for the bare maintenance of the body.
रागजन्याधिकयथेष्टचेष्टादिकं नैव स्यात् ।
Superfluous or arbitrary actions born of attachment can never occur in him.
तस्मात्सर्वप्रवृत्तिशून्य एव ज्ञानी स्यात् ।
Therefore, the knower of Truth remains entirely devoid of any willful egoic activity.
468 · इत्थं निवृत्तिप्रधान एव स्याज्ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारःअत्रेयमाशङ्का
मनसो हि अत्यन्तचाञ्चल्यम् एव स्वभावः ।
Indeed, extreme restlessness alone is the inherent nature of the mind.
तस्य च न निरालम्बनतया स्थितिः क्षणमात्रम् अपि सम्भवति ।
And its remaining steady without any support is not possible even for a single moment.
यत्किञ्चिद् आलम्बनम् आश्रित्य एव मनसः स्थितिः स्यात् ।
Only by leaning upon some support can the mind stay steady.
अतः मनसः यत्किञ्चिद्-आलम्बन-प्राप्तये ज्ञानिनः अपि प्रवृत्तिः स्यात् इति ।
Therefore, even a knower must have active engagement in order to provide some support for his mind—[such is the objection].
तत्र इदं प्रतिवचनम् - असमाहित-चित्तस्य समाधि-अनुष्ठान-शून्यस्य चित्त-समाधान-अभावेन मनसः चाञ्चल्ये अपि समाहित-चित्तस्य अनवरतं समाधिम् अनुतिष्ठतः तत् न स्यात् ।
To that, this is the reply: Although restlessness of the mind exists for one of uncollected mind who lacks the practice of *samādhi* owing to the absence of mental composure, that does not happen for one of collected mind who incessantly practices *samādhi*.
ज्ञानी तु समाधौ सदा स्थितः भवति ।
The knower, however, remains always established in *samādhi*.
तस्मात् न एव स्यात् कदाचिद् अपि प्रवृत्तिः ज्ञानिनः इति ।
Therefore, there can never be any outward activity at all for the knower.
प्रज्ञा-मान्द्यं कुतर्कः च विपर्यय-दुराग्रहः । शमाद्यैः श्रवणाद्यैः च तत्र तत्र उचितैः क्षयं नीते अस्मिन् प्रतिबन्धे अतः स्वस्य ब्रह्मत्वम् अश्नुते ॥
'Dullness of intellect, specious reasoning, and stubborn erroneous conviction—when this threefold obstacle is brought to destruction by appropriate means such as *śama* etc. and *śravaṇa* etc. respectively, one then realizes one's own identity with Brahman.'
आगामि-प्रतिबन्धः च वामदेवे समीरितः । एकेन जन्मना क्षीणः भरतस्य त्रिजन्मभिः ॥
'A future obstacle was declared in the case of Vāmadeva (which was exhausted in a single birth), and in three births for Bharata.'
योगभ्रष्टस्य गीतायाम् अतीते बहुजन्मनि । प्रतिबन्ध-क्षयः प्रोक्तः न विचारः अपि अनर्थकः ॥1,2
'In the Gītā, the destruction of obstacles is stated to occur for one fallen from yoga after many births have elapsed; nor is inquiry ever futile.'
टिप्पणी
1.
जन्मान्तर-हेतु-भूतः प्रारब्ध-शेषः ।
[The future obstacle is] the remnant of *prārabdha* karma that causes another birth.
2.
अत्र वामदेव-शब्देन ऋषभदेव-पुत्रः जडभरतः अपि गृह्यते ।
Here, along with Vāmadeva, Jaḍabharata, the son of Ṛṣabhadeva, is also implied.
तस्य जन्म-त्रय-हेतु-भूत-प्रारब्ध-शेषः अवर्तत ।
There remained in his case a residue of *prārabdha* that caused three births.
ततः साधन-सम्पत्तौ सत्याम् अपि न अभूत् ज्ञानम् ।
Hence, even though the full wealth of spiritual qualifications was present, knowledge did not dawn.
तृतीये जन्मनि अन्तरेण एव उपदेशं प्राग्-अनुष्ठित-विचार-बलात् एव अपरोक्ष-ज्ञानं सम्बभूव ।
In his third birth, even without any fresh instruction, direct realization arose purely by the power of inquiry (*vicāra*) performed earlier.
समाध्यष्टाङ्गनिरूपणम्॥ ४६९–४७४ ॥
469 · समाध्यङ्गान्यष्टौ
तानि च (१) यमः, (२) नियमः, (३) आसनम्, (४) प्राणायामः, (५) प्रत्याहारः, (६) धारणा, (७) ध्यानम्, (८) समाधिः सविकल्पः इति ।
And they [the eight limbs of *samādhi*] are: (1) *yama*, (2) *niyama*, (3) *āsana*, (4) *prāṇāyāma*, (5) *pratyāhāra*, (6) *dhāraṇā*, (7) *dhyāna*, and (8) *savikalpa-samādhi*.
470 · तत्र यमः
(१) अहिंसा, (२) सत्यम्, (३) अस्तेयम्, (४) ब्रह्मचर्यम्, (५) अपरिग्रहः इति पञ्च-विधः यमः ।
(1) Non-violence (*ahiṃsā*), (2) truthfulness (*satya*), (3) non-stealing (*asteya*), (4) continence (*brahmacarya*), and (5) non-possessiveness (*aparigraha*)—thus *yama* is fivefold.
471 · नियमः
(१) शौचम्, (२) सन्तोषः, (३) तपः, (४) स्वाध्यायः, (५) ईश्वर-प्रणिधानम् इति पञ्च-विधः नियमः ।
(1) Purity (*śauca*), (2) contentment (*santoṣa*), (3) austerity (*tapas*), (4) sacred study (*svādhyāya*), and (5) devotion to the Lord (*īśvara-praṇidhāna*)—thus *niyama* is fivefold.
ज्ञानसमुद्र-आख्ये ग्रन्थे दश-विधः यमः, दश-विधः नियमः च उक्तः ।
In the work named *Jñānasamudra*, a tenfold *yama* and a tenfold *niyama* are stated.
सा च पौराणिकी रीतिः ।
And that is the Purāṇic method.
वेदान्त-सम्प्रदाय-रीत्या तु प्रत्येकं तयोः पञ्च पञ्च एव भेदाः ।
According to the tradition of Vedānta, however, there are only five divisions each for both of them.
472 · आसनं
अनन्ता हि आसनभेदाः ।
Indeed, the varieties of yogic postures (āsanas) are endless.
तत्र स्वस्तिकं गोमुखं वीरं कूर्मं पद्मं कुक्कुटमुत्तानं कूर्मकं धानुष्कं मत्स्यं पश्चिमतानं मयूरं शवं सिंहं भद्रं सिद्धमिति प्रक्रम्य चतुरशीतिरासनानि योगग्रन्थेषु निरूपितानि ।
Among these, starting with Svastikāsana, Gomukhāsana, Vīrāsana, Kūrmāsana, Padmāsana, Kukkuṭāsana, Uttānāsana, Kūrmakāsana, Dhānuṣkāsana, Matsyāsana, Paścimatānāsana, Mayūrāsana, Śavāsana, Siṁhāsana, Bhadrāsana, and Siddhāsana, eighty-four postures have been delineated in Yoga treatises.
तत्रैव तानि तल्लक्षणान्यपि विस्तरशो ज्ञेयानि ।
Their detailed descriptions and characteristics should be learned from those very texts.
अत्र तु ग्रन्थविस्तरभयात्तेषां वेदान्तेऽत्यन्तोपयोगाभावाच्च न लिख्यन्ते ।
Here, however, for fear of lengthening the text and because they have no essential utility in Vedānta, they are not written down.
तेषु सिंहं भद्रं पद्मं सिद्धमिति चत्वारि मुख्यान्यासनानि ।
Among them, four postures are primary: Siṁhāsana, Bhadrāsana, Padmāsana, and Siddhāsana.
तत्रापि सिद्धासनमेवात्यन्तसाधनम् ।
Even among these, Siddhāsana alone is the principal means.
तल्लक्षणञ्चैकत्रोक्तम् — योनिस्थानकमङ्घ्रिमूलघटितं कृत्वा दृढं विन्यसेन्मेढ्रे पादमथैकमेव हृदये कृत्वा हनुं सुस्थिरम् । स्थास्नुः संयमितेन्द्रियोऽचलदृशा पश्येद्भ्रुवोरन्तरं ह्येतन्मोक्षकपाटभेदजनकं सिद्धासनं प्रोच्यते इति ।1,2,3
And its definition is stated elsewhere: 'Pressing firmly the heel of one foot against the perineum, one should place the other foot firmly above the genitals; resting the chin steadily on the chest, remaining motionless with senses fully controlled, one should gaze with unmoving eyes at the space between the eyebrows. This is called Siddhāsana, which unlocks the door to liberation.'
टिप्पणी
1.
यमादिलक्षणं हठयोगप्रदीपिकायां पातञ्जलसूत्रेऽन्यत्र तत्तट्टिप्पण्यादौ चोक्तम् ।
The definitions of *yama* and other limbs are stated in the *Haṭhayogapradīpikā*, the *Pātañjala Yoga Sūtras*, and elsewhere in their respective commentaries and notes.
राजयोगानुसारेण तु श्रीभगवत्पादप्रणीतापरोक्षानुभूतिग्रन्थोक्तं प्रकारमवलम्ब्यात्र किञ्चिल्लिख्यते — सर्वं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानादिन्द्रियग्रामसंयमः । यमोऽयमिति सम्प्रोक्तोऽभ्यसनीयो मुहुर्मुहुः (अपरोक्ष. १०४) ॥ न केवलमहिंसा ।
However, according to Rāja Yoga, adopting the method stated in the work *Aparokṣānubhūti* by Śrī Bhagavatpāda, a little is written here: 'The restraint of the entire aggregate of the senses arising from the direct realisation that 'Everything is Brahman' is declared to be *yama*; this should be practiced again and again' (Aparokṣānubhūti 104) — not merely non-injury (ahiṁsā).
2.
सजातीयप्रवाहश्च विजातीयतिरस्कृतिः । नियमो हि परानन्दो नियमात्क्रियते बुधैः (अपरोक्ष. १०५) ॥ न केवलं शौचादिः ।
'The continuous flow of thoughts of the same nature (Brahman) and the complete rejection of thoughts of a different nature (non-Brahman) is *niyama*, which confers supreme bliss, and is regularly practiced by the wise' (Aparokṣānubhūti 105) — not merely purity (śauca) and other physical disciplines.
3.
सुखेनैव भवेद्यस्मिन्नजस्रं ब्रह्मचिन्तनम् । आसनं तद्विजानीयान्नेतरत्सुखनाशनम् ॥
That in which ceaseless contemplation of Brahman takes place with ease should be known as āsana (posture), not any other posture that destroys ease.
न केवलं कम्बलादिकम् ।
It does not merely mean a blanket-seat and the like.
गुदावृषणयोर्मध्ये वामपादं नियोजयेत् । दक्षपादाग्रभागञ्च वामजङ्घान्तरे न्यसेत् ॥ हस्तयुग्मं न्यसेदङ्के सिद्धासनमितीरितम् । कुण्डलीबोधकं शीघ्रं समाधेश्चोपकारकम् ॥ इति ।
One should place the left foot between the anus and the scrotum (perineum), and place the front part of the right foot between the left shin and thigh; one should place both hands on the lap — this is declared to be siddhāsana, which quickly awakens the kuṇḍalinī and aids samādhi.
तत्रैव मतान्तरम् — मेढ्रादुपरि विन्यस्य सव्यगुल्फं तथोपरि । गुल्फान्तरञ्च निक्षिप्य सिद्धासनमिदं भवेत् ॥ एतत्सिद्धासनं प्राहुरन्ये वज्रासनं विदुः । मुक्तासनं वदन्त्येके प्राहुर्गुप्तासनं परे ॥ इति ।
Right there is another view: Placing the left ankle above the genitals, and likewise placing the other ankle on top of it, this becomes siddhāsana. Some call this siddhāsana; others know it as vajrāsana; some call it muktāsana, and others call it guptāsana.
सम्पीड्य सीविनीं सूक्ष्मां गुल्फेनैव च सव्यतः । सव्यं दक्षिणगुल्फेन मुक्तासनमितीरितम् ॥ इति ।
Firmly pressing the subtle perineal suture with the left ankle, and pressing the left ankle with the right ankle, is proclaimed as muktāsana.
निपीड्य सीविनीं सूक्ष्मां दक्षिणेतरगुल्फतः । वामं चान्येन गुल्फेन मुक्तासनमिदं भवेत् ॥ इति च ।
And: Pressing the subtle perineal suture with the non-right (left) ankle, and pressing the left ankle with the other ankle, this becomes muktāsana.
इदमेव सिद्धासनमत्यन्तं प्रधानम् ।
This siddhāsana alone is pre-eminently principal.
कानिचिदासनानि रोगनाशहेतूनि ।
Some postures serve the purpose of curing diseases.
कानिचित् प्राणायामादिसमाध्यङ्गसाधकानि ।
Some accomplish limbs of samādhi like prāṇāyāma and so forth.
इदं तु सिद्धासनं समाधिकालोपयोगित्वादत्यन्तं प्रधानमुच्यते ।
This siddhāsana, however, is said to be the most principal because it is directly useful at the time of samādhi.
इदमेव वज्रासनम्, मुक्तासनम्, गुप्तासनमित्यनेकधोच्यते ।
This very posture is designated variously as vajrāsana, muktāsana, and guptāsana.
473 · प्राणायामः
आसनसिद्ध्यनन्तरं प्राणायामः कर्तव्यः ।
After achieving stability in posture (*āsana*), *prāṇāyāma* (breath-control) should be practiced.
प्राणायामस्तु अनेकविधः ।
*Prāṇāyāma*, however, is of many varieties.
तथापि तल्लक्षणं सङ्ग्रहेणोच्यते - (१) नासिकाया वामच्छिद्रस्थेडाख्यनाडीद्वारा वायोरन्तः पूरणं कार्यम् ।
Even so, its definition is stated in brief: (1) Drawing the breath inside through the channel named *Iḍā* located in the left nostril should be done.
तद् एव पूरकं इत्युच्यते ।
That alone is called *pūraka* (inhalation).
(२) दक्षिणनासिकास्थपिङ्गलाख्यनाडीद्वारा वायोर्बहिर्निःसरणं कार्यम् ।
(2) Expulsion of the breath outward through the channel named *Piṅgalā* in the right nostril should be done.
तद् एव रेचकं इत्युच्यते ।
That alone is called *recaka* (exhalation).
(३) सुषुम्नाद्वारा वायोर्निरोधनं कार्यम् ।
(3) Retention of the breath through the *Suṣumnā* channel should be done.
तद् एव कुम्भकं इत्युच्यते ।
That alone is called *kumbhaka* (retention).
इत्थं क्रियमाणानाम्1,2,3,4,5
Of these being performed in this manner...
टिप्पणी
1.
चित्तादिसर्वभावेषु ब्रह्मत्वेनैव भावनात् । निरोधः सर्ववृत्तीनां प्राणायामः स उच्यते ॥
'Due to contemplating all states such as the mind as Brahman alone, the cessation of all mental modifications is called *prāṇāyāma*.'
2.
केचन प्राणायामं (१) बाह्यम्, (२) आभ्यन्तरम्, (३) स्तम्भवृत्तिकमिति वदन्ति ।
Some declare *prāṇāyāma* to be threefold: (1) external, (2) internal, and (3) motionless (*stambha-vṛtti*).
निश्वासं कृत्वा तद्गतिनिरोधो बाह्यः ।
Having exhaled, the suspension of its movement is the external *prāṇāyāma*.
प्राणोच्छ्वासं कृत्वा तन्निरोधः आभ्यन्तरः ।
Having inhaled the breath, its retention is the internal *prāṇāyāma*.
बाह्यान्तर्गतेः समकालं निरोधः स्तम्भवृत्तिरिति च ।
And the simultaneous suspension of both outward and inward movement is *stambha-vṛtti*.
3.
अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति भावना पूरकः ।
The constant contemplation 'I am Brahman' is the true *pūraka*.
4.
अनात्मप्रपञ्चनिषेधो रेचकः ।
The negation of the non-Self universe is *recaka*.
5.
अखण्डाकारवृत्त्याचलता कुम्भकः ।
Steadfastness by means of the undivided *vṛtti* of Brahman is *kumbhaka*.
पूरकरेचककुम्भकानां समुदायः प्राणायाम इत्युच्यते ।
The aggregate of *pūraka*, *recaka*, and *kumbhaka* is called *prāṇāyāma*.
स च प्राणायामो द्विविधः - (१) एकोऽगर्भः, (२) अपरः सगर्भः ।
And that *prāṇāyāma* is of two kinds: (1) one is *agarbha* (without seed-mantra), and (2) the other is *sagarbha* (with seed-mantra).
(१) प्रणवोच्चारणं विना क्रियमाणः प्राणायामोऽगर्भः ।
(1) The *prāṇāyāma* performed without chanting *Praṇava* (Om) is *agarbha*.
(२) प्रणवोच्चारणेन सह क्रियमाणः प्राणायामः सगर्भः ।
(2) The *prāṇāyāma* performed together with the recitation of *Praṇava* is *sagarbha*.
474 · प्रत्याहारधारणाध्यानानि
स्वस्वविषयेभ्यः सकलेन्द्रियनिरोधः प्रत्याहारः ।
The restraint of all the sense organs from their respective objects is *pratyāhāra* (withdrawal of the senses).
नैरन्तर्येणान्तःकरणस्यैकाकारतास्थितिः धारणा ।
The uninterrupted abiding of the mind (*antaḥkaraṇa*) in a single form is *dhāraṇā* (concentration).
बह्वन्तराययुक्ताद्वितीयप्रत्यग्ब्रह्मणि प्रवहदन्तःकरणप्रवाहो ध्यानं इत्युच्यते ।
The steady stream of the inner organ flowing towards the non-dual innermost Brahman despite facing many obstacles is called *dhyāna* (meditation).
475 · समाधिः
व्युत्थानसंस्कारतिरस्कारेण निरोधसंस्कारप्रकटनेन च सह अन्तःकरणस्य एकाग्रतापरिणामः समाधिः ।
The modification of one-pointedness of the mind along with the setting aside of outgoing latent impressions and the manifestation of restraining latent impressions is samādhi.
अयम् च समाधिः द्विविधः - (१) सविकल्पसमाधिः, (२) निर्विकल्पसमाधिः च इति ।
And this *samādhi* is of two kinds: (1) *savikalpa-samādhi*, and (2) *nirvikalpa-samādhi*.
(१) ज्ञातृज्ञानज्ञेयरूपत्रिपुटीभानसहिताद्वितीयब्रह्मविषयकान्तःकरणवृत्त्यवस्थितिः सविकल्पसमाधिः इति उच्यते ।
(1) The abiding of the *vṛtti* of the *antaḥkaraṇa* taking the non-dual Brahman as its object, accompanied by the appearance of the triad (*tripuṭī*) of knower, knowledge, and object of knowledge, is called *savikalpa-samādhi*.
सः च द्विविधः - (१.१) शब्दानुविद्धः, (१.२) शब्दाननुविद्धः च इति ।
And that is of two kinds: (1.1) *śabdānuviddha* (associated with words), and (1.2) *śabdānanuviddha* (unassociated with words).
(१.१) अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति शब्देन सहितः यः सः शब्दानुविद्धः ।
(1.1) That which is accompanied by the verbal formulation 'I am Brahman' is *śabdānuviddha*.
(१.२) तद्रहितः तु शब्दाननुविद्धः ।
(1.2) But that which is devoid of that [verbal formulation] is *śabdānanuviddha*.
(२) त्रिपुटीभानरहिताखण्डब्रह्माकारान्तःकरणवृत्त्यवस्थितिः निर्विकल्पसमाधिः इति उच्यते ।
(2) The abiding of the *vṛtti* of the *antaḥkaraṇa* taking the form of the undivided Brahman, free from any manifestation of the triad (*tripuṭī*), is called *nirvikalpa-samādhi*.
एवम् सविकल्पनिर्विकल्पभेदेन समाधिः द्विविधः ।
Thus, by the division into *savikalpa* and *nirvikalpa*, *samādhi* is of two kinds.
तत्र सविकल्पसमाधिः साधनम् ।
Among these, *savikalpa-samādhi* is the means.
निर्विकल्पसमाधिः फलम् ।
*Nirvikalpa-samādhi* is the fruit.
साधनात्मकसविकल्पसमाधौ यद्यपि त्रिपुटीरूपद्वैतप्रतीतिः अस्ति ।
Although in *savikalpa-samādhi*, which is of the nature of a means, there is perception of duality in the form of the triad,
तथापि तत् द्वैतं कारणब्रह्मात्मना एव प्रतीयते ।
even so, that duality is perceived only as identical with Brahman, the cause,
न पृथक् ।
and not as distinct.
यथा मृद्विकारान् मृद्रूपत्वेन ।1,2,3,4
Just as one perceives the modifications of clay in their true nature as clay.
टिप्पणी
1.
विषयेष्वात्मतां दृष्ट्वा मनसश्चित्तमज्जनम् । प्रत्याहारः स विज्ञेयोऽभ्यसनीयो मुमुक्षुभिः ॥
'Seeing the Self in all objects, the immersion of the mind into consciousness is to be known as *pratyāhāra*, which should be practised by seekers of liberation.'
2.
यत्र यत्र मनो याति ब्रह्मणस्तत्र दर्शनम् । मनसो धारणञ्चैव धारणा सा परा मता ॥
'Wherever the mind goes, seeing Brahman there and fixing the mind in it is regarded as the supreme *dhāraṇā*.'
3.
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति सद्वृत्त्या निरालम्बतया स्थितिः । ध्यानशब्देन विख्याता परमानन्ददायिनी ॥
'The unsupported resting in the state through the noble *vṛtti* 'I am Brahman alone', bestowing supreme bliss, is celebrated by the word *dhyāna*.'
4.
निर्विकारतया वृत्त्या ब्रह्माकारतया पुनः । वृत्तिविस्मरणं सम्यक्समाधिर्ज्ञानसंज्ञकः ॥
'Through the unchanging modification taking the form of Brahman, the complete forgetfulness of the *vṛtti* itself is true *samādhi*, termed *jñāna*.'
अथातः सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि समाधिं भवनाशनम् । समाधिः संविदुत्पत्तिः परजीवैकतां प्रति ॥
'Now, therefore, I shall fully explain *samādhi* which destroys worldly existence: *samādhi* is the arising of consciousness regarding the oneness of the supreme Self and the *jīva*.'
महावाक्यलक्ष्यस्वरूपसाक्षात्कार एव समाधिः इह विवक्षितः इत्यर्थः ।
The direct realization of the essential nature indicated by the *mahāvākyas* is alone intended here by the term *samādhi* — this is the meaning.
जानतः विवेकिनः मृद्विकाराः घटादयः मृद्रूपाः एव प्रतीयन्ते तथा सविकल्पकसमाधौ त्रिपुटीरूपद्वैतम् अपि ब्रह्मात्मना एव प्रतीयते ।
Just as to a knowing, discriminating person the products of clay such as pots are perceived only as clay, so too in *savikalpa-samādhi* the duality in the form of the triad is perceived only as identical with Brahman.
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ अपि सविकल्पसमाधौ इव त्रिपुटीरूपं द्वैतं विद्यमानम् अपि न प्रतीयते ।
In *nirvikalpa-samādhi*, though duality in the form of the triad exists subtly as in *savikalpa-samādhi*, it is not perceived at all.
यथा जले निक्षिप्तः लवणपिण्डः निलीनः विद्यमानः अपि नेत्रेण न गृह्यते तद्वत् ।
Just as a lump of salt cast into water, though dissolved and present, is not seen by the eye, so it is.
तथा च सविकल्पनिर्विकल्पसमाध्योः अयम् भेदः - (१) सविकल्पसमाधौ ब्रह्मस्वरूपेण द्वैतं प्रतीयते ।
And thus, this is the distinction between *savikalpa* and *nirvikalpa* *samādhi*: (1) in *savikalpa-samādhi*, duality is perceived as identical to Brahman;
(२) निर्विकल्पसमाधौ त्रिपुटीरूपं द्वैतं न प्रतीयते इति ।
(2) in *nirvikalpa-samādhi*, duality in the form of the triad is not perceived at all.
476 · सुषुप्तिनिर्विकल्पसमाध्योर्भेदः
सुषुप्तौ अन्तःकरणवृत्तिः ब्रह्माकारतां न प्राप्नोति ।
In deep sleep (*suṣupti*), the *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti* does not assume the form of Brahman.
किन्तु कारणाज्ञानात्मतां भजते ।
Rather, it merges into causal *ajñāna*.
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ तु ब्रह्माकारतया अन्तःकरणवृत्तिः वर्तते ।
In *nirvikalpa-samādhi*, however, the *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti* remains in the form of Brahman.
इत्थम् - सुषुप्तौ सवृत्तिकान्तःकरणस्य अभावः ।
Thus: in deep sleep, there is the absence of the *antaḥkaraṇa* along with its modifications.
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ सवृत्तिकान्तःकरणस्य सत्त्वे अपि न प्रतीतिः ।
In *nirvikalpa-samādhi*, even though the *antaḥkaraṇa* along with its *vṛtti* exists, there is no perception of it.
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ अन्तःकरणस्य ब्रह्माकारवृत्त्युत्पत्तौ सविकल्पसमाध्याभ्यासः हेतुः ।
The practice of *savikalpa-samādhi* is the cause for the arising of the *antaḥkaraṇa*'s *vṛtti* taking the form of Brahman in *nirvikalpa-samādhi*.
तस्मात् एव साधनरूपाष्टाङ्गेषु सविकल्पः समाधिः अपि गण्यते ।
For this very reason, *savikalpa-samādhi* is also counted among the eight limbs that serve as means.
निर्विकल्पसमाधिः तु तस्य फलम् ।
*Nirvikalpa-samādhi*, on the other hand, is its fruit.
477 · निर्विकल्पसमाधेर्द्वैविध्यम्निर्विकल्पसमाधिरपि द्विविधः
(१) एकोऽद्वैतभावनारूपः, (२) अपरोऽद्वैतावस्थानस्वरूपः ।
'(1) One is of the nature of meditation on non-duality, and (2) the other is of the nature of remaining established in non-duality.'
अद्वैतब्रह्माकारान्तःकरणवृत्तिः अद्वैतभावनारूपनिर्विकल्पसमाधिरित्युच्यते ।
The mental mode (*vṛtti*) taking the form of non-dual *Brahman* is called the *nirvikalpa-samādhi* in the form of meditation on non-duality (*advaita-bhāvanā-rūpa*).
एतत्समाध्यभ्यासाधिक्ये सति ब्रह्माकारा वृत्तिरपि शान्ता भवति ।
When the practice of this *samādhi* intensifies, even the *vṛtti* that has assumed the form of *Brahman* becomes quiescent.
सैव वृत्तिरहितावस्थाद्वैतावस्थानरूपनिर्विकल्पसमाधिरित्युच्यते ।
That very state devoid of any *vṛtti* is called *nirvikalpa-samādhi* in the form of abiding in non-duality (*advaitāvasthāna-rūpa*).
यथा सन्तप्तायसि निक्षिप्तो जलबिन्दुस्तस्मिन्नेव प्रविशति ।
Just as a drop of water cast onto red-hot iron merges into it completely,
तथाद्वैतभावनारूपः समाधिरपि दृढाभ्यासवशादत्यन्तं प्रकाशमाने ब्रह्मात्मनि प्रविशति ।
so too, by virtue of sustained practice, the *samādhi* in the form of meditation on non-duality dissolves into the supremely effulgent *Brahman*-Self.
अत्र प्रथमः समाधिः द्वितीयस्य साधनं भवति ।1,2,3
Here, the first *samādhi* serves as the means for the second.
टिप्पणी
1.
वायूपादानकत्वादग्न्युत्पत्तिस्थितिनाशानां वायुरुपादानकारणमग्नेः ।
Because the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of fire depend on air, air is the material cause of fire.
यथा वायोरभावे दीपः प्रशाम्यति ।
Just as in the absence of air a lamp goes out,
अनुकूलवायुप्रदेशे अचलः प्रकाशते ।
and in a place with favorable air it shines steadily,
तथैव समाधावन्तःकरणस्य सुतरामभावे शरीरं पतेत् ।
even so, if the *antaḥkaraṇa* were completely absent in *samādhi*, the body would collapse.
तस्मान्मनोबुद्धिचित्ताहङ्कारादिवृत्तिं विना सूक्ष्मरूपेण निर्वृत्तिकमेवान्तःकरणमास्ते ।
Therefore, without gross modifications such as mind, intellect, memory, and ego, the *antaḥkaraṇa* remains in a subtle, modification-free state alone.
समाधेरुत्थानसमये समाधिसुखस्मरणसत्त्वात् अननुभूते च स्मरणासम्भवात् समाधावपि वृत्तिसद्भावोऽनुमीयते ।
Moreover, because there is memory of the bliss of *samādhi* upon emerging from it, and memory of an unexperienced object is impossible, the subtle presence of *vṛtti* even in *samādhi* is inferred.
समाधावन्तःकरणाभावे योगिशरीरं पतेदेव सुप्तदेहवत् ।
If there were complete absence of the *antaḥkaraṇa* in *samādhi*, the yogin's body would collapse just like that of a sleeping person.
न तु तथा पतति ।
However, it does not fall down in that manner.
तस्मात्समाधावन्तःकरणमस्त्येवेति स्वीकर्तव्यमिति तात्पर्यम् ।
Therefore, one must accept that the *antaḥkaraṇa* does indeed exist in *samādhi*; this is the purport.
2.
अद्वैतभावनारूपः समाधिः ।
The *samādhi* in the form of meditation on non-duality.
3.
अद्वैतावस्थानरूपस्य ।
Of the *samādhi* in the form of abiding in non-duality.
समाधिरयं ज्ञानस्य सप्तमभूमिकारूपयोगस्य परमोऽवधिः ।
This *samādhi* is the highest culmination of yoga, which is the seventh plane (*bhūmikā*) of knowledge.
478
अद्वैतावस्थानरूपसमाधिसुषुप्त्योर्भेदः अद्वैतावस्थानरूपसमाधेः सुषुप्तेश्चेयान् भेदः ।
The difference between *advaitāvasthāna-rūpa-samādhi* and deep sleep: there is the following difference between *samādhi* of the nature of abiding in non-duality and deep sleep (*suṣupti*).
(१) सुषुप्तावन्तःकरणं तद्वृत्तिश्चाज्ञाने लीयते ।
'(1) In deep sleep, the *antaḥkaraṇa* and its *vṛttis* dissolve into *ajñāna*.'
(२) अद्वैतावस्थानरूपसमाधौ तु वृत्तिर्ब्रह्मप्रकाशचैतन्ये प्रलीयत इति ।
'(2) Whereas in the *samādhi* of abiding in non-duality, the *vṛtti* dissolves completely into the Consciousness that is the illumination of *Brahman*.'
किञ्च (१) सुषुप्तौ स्वरूपानन्दोऽज्ञानावृतो भवति ।
Moreover, (1) in deep sleep, the bliss of one's true nature remains veiled by *ajñāna*.
(२) अत्र तु समाधौ निरावरणो ब्रह्मानन्दो विभाति ।
'(2) But here in *samādhi*, the bliss of *Brahman* shines forth completely unveiled.'
479
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ लयविक्षेपकषायरसास्वादरूपविघ्नचतुष्टयनिरूपणम् निर्विकल्पसमाधौ चत्वारो विघ्नाः स्युः ।
Exposition of the four obstacles in *nirvikalpa-samādhi* in the form of *laya*, *vikṣepa*, *kaṣāya*, and *rasāsvāda*: In *nirvikalpa-samādhi*, four obstacles can arise.
तन्निवृत्त्यर्थं तत्स्वरूपं कथ्यते ।
For the purpose of eliminating them, their true nature is described.
(१) लयः, (२) विक्षेपः, (३) कषायः, (४) रसास्वाद इति विघ्नाः चत्वारः ।
'(1) Laya, (2) vikṣepa, (3) kaṣāya, and (4) rasāsvāda' — these are the four obstacles.
तत्र लयः = आलस्येन निद्रया वा वृत्त्यभावो लय इत्युच्यते ।
Among these, *laya*: the absence of *vṛtti* caused by lethargy or sleep is called *laya*.
तस्मिन्सति सुषुप्तितुल्यावस्था समाधिनिष्ठस्य जायते ।
When that occurs, a state akin to deep sleep overtakes the practitioner of *samādhi*.
ब्रह्मानन्दोऽपि तदा तिरोभवति ।
Then, even the bliss of *Brahman* becomes veiled.
तस्मान्निद्रालस्यादिनिमित्तैर्यदा वृत्तिः स्वोपादानेऽन्तःकरणे लीयेत, तदा योगी सावधानः सन् निद्रादिकं निरुध्य वृत्त्युत्पादनं कुर्यात् ।
Therefore, when the *vṛtti* is about to dissolve into its material cause, the *antaḥkaraṇa*, due to sleep, indolence, and other causes, then the yogin, remaining vigilant, must check sleep and the rest, and reactivate the *vṛtti*.
इदमेव श्रीगौडपादाचार्यैश्चित्तसम्बोधनमित्युक्तम् ।
This alone has been declared by Śrī Gauḍapādācārya as 'awakening the mind' (*citta-sambodhana*).
लयरूपस्य विघ्नस्य विरोधि निद्रालस्यादिनिरोधकं वृत्तिप्रवाहरूपं जागरणमेव चित्तसम्बोधनम् ।
The awakening that opposes the obstacle of *laya*, checking sleep and lethargy, and consisting in an unbroken stream of *vṛtti*, is precisely what is meant by 'awakening the mind' (*citta-sambodhana*).
480 · विक्षेपः
यथा हि बहिर्मार्जारादिभयाच्चटका गृहान्तः प्रविश्य भयक्लेशव्याकुलतादिनिवृत्तियोग्यं स्थलं तत्कालं तत्रापश्यन्ती बहिरेव पुनरागत्य भयं वा मरणादिरूपं दुःखं वा प्राप्नुयात् तथैव बहिरनात्मपदार्थान् दुःखहेतुत्वेन बुद्ध्वाद्वैतानन्दं विषयीकर्तुं चित्तवृत्तिरन्तर्मुखीभूय, प्रत्यक्चैतन्य1,2
Just as a sparrow, entering inside a house out of fear of cats and the like outside, not finding at that moment a place suitable for relieving its fear, distress, and agitation, goes back outside and meets with fear or the suffering of death, etc., exactly in the same way, the mental modification (*citta-vṛtti*), realizing external non-Self objects to be the causes of sorrow, turns inward to experience non-dual bliss, [and in the innermost Consciousness...]
टिप्पणी
1.
ननु वृत्तिर्निर्विकारे ब्रह्मप्रकाशचैतन्ये प्रलीयते इत्यसङ्गतमेवोक्तम् ।
[Objection:] It was stated that the *vṛtti* dissolves in the changeless Consciousness of Brahman-illumination; this is altogether inconsistent.
तस्य तदनुपादानत्वात् ।
For Brahman is not the material cause (*upādāna*) of the *vṛtti*.
उपादाने एव च कार्यलयौचित्यात् इति चेत् ।
And because dissolution of an effect is proper only into its material cause — if this be argued:
पूर्वोक्ते दृष्टान्तेऽपि हि विचारदृष्ट्या जलबिन्दुर्न तप्तायसि लीयते ।
[Reply:] Even in the earlier-stated analogy, upon analytical reflection, a drop of water does not dissolve into hot iron,
अनुपादानत्वात् ।
Because the hot iron is not its material cause,
किन्तु स्वोपादानभूतेऽग्नावेव ।
But rather in fire alone, which is its own material cause.
अतो यथा तत्र अयोलयस्त्वौपचारिकः तथात्रापि पूर्वोक्तसमाधिदशायां राजसतामसगुणानां निःशेषं नाशादाविर्भूते सत्त्वगुणात्मके स्वोपादाने एवाज्ञाने वृत्तेर्लयः ।
Therefore, just as there the dissolution in iron is figurative, so here too, in the aforementioned state of *samādhi*, upon the complete destruction of the *rajas* and *tamas* qualities, the dissolution of the *vṛtti* takes place in its own material cause alone — namely, *ajñāna* dominated by the *sattva* quality which has become manifest.
न निर्विकारस्वप्रकाशब्रह्मचैतन्ये ।
And not in the changeless, self-luminous Brahman-Consciousness directly.
अथापि स्वप्रकाशब्रह्मावभासनिमित्तत्वाद्वृत्तिलयस्य ब्रह्मप्रकाशे वृत्तेर्लयोक्तिरौपचारिकी ।
Even so, since the manifestation of self-luminous Brahman is the occasioning cause of the *vṛtti*'s dissolution, the statement that the *vṛtti* dissolves in the light of Brahman is metaphorical.
अथवा तादृशसमाध्यनुभवितृब्रह्मविद्वरिष्ठदृष्ट्या गुणादीनामप्रतीतेः शुद्धं ब्रह्मैव प्रकाशते इति तत्र तद्वृत्त्यभावो जायते ।
Alternatively, from the standpoint of the exalted knower of Brahman experiencing such *samādhi*, since the *guṇa*s and other factors are not perceived, pure Brahman alone shines, and thus the cessation of that *vṛtti* occurs there.
अत एव च ब्रह्मप्रकाशचैतन्ये वृत्तेर्लयः कथ्यते इति मन्तव्यम् ।
It should therefore be understood that for this very reason the dissolution of the *vṛtti* is said to be in the Consciousness of Brahman-illumination.
2.
गौडपादाचार्यैर्माण्डूक्योपनिषत्कारिकायां कथितम् ।
It has been stated by Śrī Gauḍapādācārya in the *Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad Kārikā*:
स्वरूपस्यात्मनोऽत्यन्तसूक्ष्मत्वात् किञ्चित्कालमपि तत्र स्थैर्यमप्राप्य चैतन्यस्वरूपानन्दमननुभूय पुनर्बहिर्मुखीभवति ।
Because the essential nature of the *ātman* is extremely subtle, [the mind], without attaining steadiness there even for a little while and without experiencing the bliss of Consciousness, turns outward again.
ईदृग्वृत्तिरेव बहिर्मुखीभूता विक्षेप इत्युच्यते ।
Such a *vṛtti* alone, having turned outwards, is termed distraction (*vikṣepa*).
चित्तवृत्तेः स्थिरतां विना न स्वरूपानन्दस्य लाभो भवति ।
Without the steadiness of the *citta-vṛtti*, the attainment of the natural bliss of the Self cannot take place.
तस्मात् वृत्तावन्तर्मुखीभूतायामपि यावन्न सा ब्रह्माकारतां भजते, तावद्योगी नियतमानसो बाह्येष्वनात्मपदार्थेषु पुनः पुनर्दोषभावनया वृत्तिं निरुद्ध्य अन्तर्मुखामेव तां स्थापयेत् ।
Therefore, even when the *vṛtti* has turned inward, so long as it does not assume the form of Brahman (*brahmākāra*), so long the yogin, with a controlled mind, should restrain the *vṛtti* by repeatedly contemplating defects in external non-Self objects and keep it established inward alone.
विक्षेपरूपविघ्नविरोधी योगिप्रयत्नः शम इति गौडपादाचार्यैरुच्यते ।
The yogin's effort that counters this obstacle of distraction is termed tranquility / quelling (*śama*) by Śrī Gauḍapādācārya.
481 · कषायः
रागादयो दोषाः कषाया इत्युच्यन्ते ।
Defects such as attachment (*rāga*) and the like are called *kaṣāya*s.
ते च बाह्याभ्यन्तरभेदेन द्विप्रकारा भवन्ति ।
And they are of two kinds, distinguished into external and internal.
तत्र (१) स्त्रीपुत्रधनादिरूपा विषया वार्तमानिकाः, बाह्या उच्यन्ते ।
There, (1) present objects consisting of wife, son, wealth, and the like are called external.
त एव भूता भाविनो वा चिन्तामुपारूढा मनोराज्यमात्रसिद्धा आन्तराः ।
(2) The very same objects, whether past or future, when ascended to conscious thought and existing merely as mental reverie, are the internal ones.
त एते द्विविधा अपि रागादयः समाधिप्रवृत्ते योगिनि न सम्भवन्ति ।
Both these twofold attachments and defects do not occur in a yogin engaged in *samādhi*.
अन्तःकरणस्य पञ्च भूमयः - (१) क्षेपः, (२) मूढता, (३) विक्षेपः, (४) एकाग्रता, (५) निरोधभूमिका चेति चित्तस्य पञ्च भूमयः सन्ति ।
There are five planes (*bhūmi*s) of the *antaḥkaraṇa*: (1) restlessness (*kṣepa*), (2) dullness (*mūḍhatā*), (3) distraction (*vikṣepa*), (4) one-pointedness (*ekāgratā*), and (5) the restrained plane (*nirodha-bhūmikā*) — these are the five planes of the mind.
लोकवासनादेहवासनाशास्त्रवासनादिरूपा रजोगुणपरिणामात्मिका दृढतरानेकानात्मवासनाः क्षेपा इत्युच्यन्ते ।
(1) The very firm and numerous latent impressions regarding the non-Self, which take the form of world-obsession (*loka-vāsanā*), body-obsession (*deha-vāsanā*), scriptural pride (*śāstra-vāsanā*), etc., and consist of the transformation of the *rajo-guṇa*, are called restlessness (*kṣepa*).
निद्रालस्यप्रमादादिस्तमोगुणपरिणामोऽन्तःकरणस्य मूढतेत्युच्यते ।
(2) The transformation of the *tamo-guṇa* in the mind characterized by sleep, laziness, heedlessness, etc., is called dullness (*mūḍhatā*).
ध्याने प्रवृत्तस्य चित्तस्य कदाचिद्बाह्यप्रवृत्तिर्विक्षेप इति कथ्यते ।
(3) The occasional outward movement of the mind that is otherwise engaged in meditation is called distraction (*vikṣepa*).
अन्तःकरणस्यातीतपरिणामवर्तमानपरिणामयोः समानाकारतापत्तिः एकाग्रतेत्युच्यते ।
(4) The attainment of identical form between the past modification and the present modification of the mind is called one-pointedness (*ekāgratā*).
अस्यायमर्थः - समाधिकाले योगिनोऽन्तःकरणे एकाग्रता जायते ।
The meaning of this is: at the time of *samādhi*, one-pointedness arises in the yogin's mind.
सा चैकाग्रता न वृत्त्यभावरूपा ।
And that one-pointedness is not of the nature of total absence of mental modifications (*vṛtti*s).
समाधिकालीनान्तःकरणपरिणामविशेषाः सर्वेऽपि ब्रह्मैव विषयीकुर्वन्ति ।
All the specific thought-modifications of the mind at the time of *samādhi* take Brahman alone as their object.
तत्रान्तःकरणस्यातीतपरिणामवर्तमानपरिणामयोः केवलब्रह्माकारतापत्त्या समानाकारता जायते ।1,2,3,1,2,3
Therein, between the past modification and the present modification of the mind, a sameness of form occurs because both assume solely the form of Brahman.
टिप्पणी
1.
मैव निन्दतु लोको माम् ।
'Let not the world censure me at all.
सर्वेऽपि मां स्तुवन्तु इत्याग्रहयुक्तो दृढतरः संस्कारो लोकवासनेत्युच्यते ।
May all people praise me' — the deep-seated latent impression accompanied by such insistent fixation is called world-obsession (*loka-vāsanā*).
2.
स्थूलसूक्ष्मदेहनिष्ठरोगात्मकपापफलानि मलानि मणिमन्त्रौषधादिना वा तीर्थयात्रादिपुण्यकर्मणा वा निःशेषं निवर्तयामि, इति वा देहेऽस्मिन् पुष्टिसौन्दर्यादिरूपं पुण्याद्यतिशयफलं सम्पादयामि इति वा दृढतरः संस्कारो देहवासनेत्युच्यते ।
'Let me completely remove the impurities which are the fruits of sin in the form of diseases residing in the gross and subtle bodies by means of gems, mantras, medicines, etc., or by meritorious deeds like pilgrimages, etc.', or 'Let me acquire in this body the heightened fruits of merit etc. in the form of bodily nourishment, beauty, etc.' — the deep-seated latent impression of this nature is called body-obsession (*deha-vāsanā*).
1.
अयमत्राशयः ।
This is the intent here.
यस्य हि राजगृहप्रवेशेऽधिकारोऽस्ति तं द्वारपालः कदाचिन्निरुणद्धीति प्रसक्तस्य प्रतिषेधो युज्यते ।
For only when someone has the right to enter the king's palace and the doorkeeper stops him at times, is prohibition appropriate for that which is otherwise applicable.
यस्य पुनस्तत्र अधिकार एव नास्ति तस्य कथं निरोधप्रसक्तिः ।
However, for one who has no eligibility there at all, how could there be any occasion for being obstructed?
एवं क्षिप्तान्तःकरणस्य समाधावधिकारप्रसक्तौ तस्य रागादिदोषरूपः कषायो विघ्नकरः स्यात् ।
In the same way, if the agitated mind had eligibility for *samādhi*, then *kaṣāya* in the form of defects like attachment and aversion would be an obstacle.
तस्य तु समाध्यधिकार एव नास्ति ।
But he has no eligibility for *samādhi* at all.
तत्कथं रागादिदोषरूपः कषायः समाधिविघ्नकृदिति ।
Therefore, how can *kaṣāya* in the form of defects like attachment be an obstacle to *samādhi*?
2.
रागादयोऽत्र त्रिप्रकारा भवन्तीति कापि प्रक्रिया ।
There is a certain methodology stating that attachment and the like are of three kinds here.
सा चैवं - (१) बाह्याः, (२) आन्तराः, (३) वासनारूपाश्चेति ।
And that is as follows: (1) external, (2) internal, and (3) in the form of latent impressions (*vāsanā*).
(१) बाह्यप्रवृत्तिहेतुभूता रागादयो बाह्या उद्युक्ता इति चोच्यन्ते ।
(1) Attachments and the like that cause outward engagement are called 'external' and 'active'.
(२) मनोराज्यात्मका रागादय आन्तरा आशात्मका इत्युच्यन्ते ।
(2) Attachments and the like consisting of daydreams of the mind are called 'internal' and 'desire-oriented'.
(३) जन्मान्तरेषु प्रागनुभूतविषयरागादिसंस्कारा वासनारूपा इत्युच्यन्ते ।
(3) Latent impressions of attachments etc. towards objects experienced in prior births are called 'of the nature of *vāsanā*'.
वासनाश्च उद्बुद्धानुद्बुद्धभेदेन द्विविधाः ।
And latent impressions are of two kinds: awakened and unawakened.
तन्निरूपणं च विद्यारण्यस्वामिकृते जीवन्मुक्तिविवेके द्रष्टव्यम् ।
And their detailed treatment should be seen in the *Jīvanmuktiviveka* composed by Svāmī Vidyāraṇya.
3.
सकलशास्त्राणामध्ययनं पठनं वा, अर्थावधारणं तदनुष्ठानं वा करोमीति दृढतरः संस्कारः शास्त्रवासनेत्युच्यते ।
The very deep-seated impression thinking, 'I will study or recite all the scriptures, grasp their meaning, or put them into practice', is called *śāstra-vāsanā*.
(५) अस्या एकाग्रतायाः प्रवाहवृद्धिरेव निरोध इत्युच्यते ।
(5) The increase of the continuous stream of this one-pointedness is alone called *nirodha* (cessation).
इमाश्च भूमयः पञ्चापि अन्तःकरणस्यैव अवस्थाविशेषाः ।
And all these five planes are indeed specific states of the mind itself.
पञ्चभूमिकाविशिष्टस्यान्तःकरणस्यैव क्रमात् क्षिप्तम्, मूढम्, विक्षिप्तम्, एकाग्रम्, निरुद्धमिति नाम ।
The mind characterized by the five planes is sequentially given the names: restless (*kṣipta*), dull (*mūḍha*), distracted (*vikṣipta*), one-pointed (*ekāgra*), and restrained (*niruddha*).
तत्र क्षिप्तमूढान्तःकरणयोर्नास्ति समाध्यधिकारः ।
Among them, the restless and dull minds have no eligibility for *samādhi*.
विक्षिप्तान्तःकरणस्य त्वधिकारोऽस्ति ।
However, the distracted mind (*vikṣipta*) does possess eligibility.
एकाग्रनिरुद्धान्तःकरणयोः सम्भवः समाधिकाले ।
The one-pointed and restrained states of mind occur at the time of *samādhi*.
एतत्सर्वं योगशास्त्रे विस्तरतः कथ्यते ।
All this is explained in detail in the *Yoga-śāstra*.
अत्राक्षेपः - ननु रागादिदोषदूषितमन्तःकरणं क्षिप्तमेव वर्तते ।
Here is an objection: Surely a mind tainted by defects like attachment is purely restless (*kṣipta*).
क्षिप्तान्तःकरणस्य च योगेऽधिकार एव नास्तीत्युक्तम् ।
And it was stated that a restless mind has no eligibility in yoga whatsoever.
तत्कथं रागादिदोषरूपः कषायः समाधिविघ्नरूप इत्युच्यते, इति चेत् उच्यते ।
Then how can *kaṣāya*, which is of the form of defects like attachment, be called an obstacle to *samādhi*? If this is asked, the reply is stated.
बाह्यान्तर्भावेन विद्यमाना रागादयः क्षिप्तान्तःकरण एव जायन्ते ।
Attachments and the like present in external and internal modes arise only in the restless mind.
तस्य चान्तःकरणस्याधिकारो नास्ति योगे ।
And that mind has no eligibility in yoga.
तथापि अनेकजन्मसु प्रागनुभूतबाह्याभ्यन्तरविषयकरागद्वेषादयो ये तेषां सूक्ष्मः संस्कारो विक्षिप्ताद्यन्तःकरणेऽपि सम्भवेत् ।
Nevertheless, the subtle impression of those attachments and aversions towards external and internal objects experienced earlier across many births can exist even in a distracted mind.
तस्मात्, रागद्वेषादीनां न कषाय इति नाम ।
Therefore, active attachments and aversions are not termed *kaṣāya*.
किन्तु रागद्वेषादिसंस्कारस्यैव कषाय इति नाम ।
Rather, it is the latent impression of attachment, aversion, etc., that is called *kaṣāya*.
स च संस्कारो यावदन्तःकरणस्यावस्थितिः, तावदनुवर्तेतैव ।
And that latent impression persists as long as the mind exists.
यद्यपि समाध्यवस्थायामप्यन्तःकरणं वर्तत एव ।
Even though the mind does exist even in the state of *samādhi*,
तथापि रागद्वेषादीनामुद्भूतः संस्कार एव समाधिविरोधी ।
nevertheless, only an awakened latent impression of attachment, aversion, etc. opposes *samādhi*,
न त्वनुद्भूतः ।
and not an unawakened one.
उद्भूतः = बहिः प्रकटीकृतः ।
'Awakened' means manifested outwardly.
3.
अत्रायं दृष्टान्तः - राजदर्शनाय स्वगृहात्प्रस्थितमाद्यं राजद्वारमागतं जागरूको द्वारपालो यथा निवारयति ।
Here this is an analogy: just as a vigilant doorkeeper turns back one who has set out from his own home to see the king and has arrived at the first palace gate,
