तथा सकलसंसारविषयेभ्यो दुःखभयान्निर्विकल्पसमाधिसुखानुभवायान्तर्मुखीभूतं योगिनो मनः समाध्यानन्दलाभात्प्रागन्तराले उद्भूतरागादिसंस्काररूपः कषायो निवारयति ।
even so, *kaṣāya*—the arising of latent impressions of passion and the like—blocks the mind of the yogin in the midway stage before the attainment of the bliss of *samādhi*, even when that mind has turned inward from all worldly objects out of fear of sorrow in order to experience the bliss of *nirvikalpa-samādhi*.
तस्मात् स एव समाधिविघ्न इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, that alone is called an obstacle to *samādhi* (*samādhi-vighna*).
अनुद्भूतः = अन्तःस्थितः ।
'*Anudbhūtaḥ*' means remaining internal (latent).
समाधिप्रवृत्तेन योगिना रागद्वेषादिसंस्कारोद्भवे स दोषदृष्ट्या दृढतरवैराग्यबलाच्चापनेयः ।
When the latent impressions of attachment, aversion, and the like arise, it must be removed by the yogin engaged in *samādhi* through seeing defects in them and through the strength of firmer dispassion.
विक्षेपकषाययोरयं भेदः - बाह्यविषयाकारवृत्तेर्विक्षेप इति नाम ।
This is the distinction between *vikṣepa* (distraction) and *kaṣāya* (taint): the mental *vṛtti* taking the form of external objects is designated as *vikṣepa*.
योगिनः प्रयत्नवशादन्तर्मुखीभूतायामपि वृत्तौ रागादिदोषाणामुद्भूतसंस्कारात् सा प्रतिबद्धा सती ब्रह्म न विषयीकरोति, स एव संस्कारः कषाय इत्युच्यते ।
Even when the *vṛtti* is turned inward through the yogin's effort, when it is obstructed by the active latent impressions of defects like attachment and fails to take Brahman as its object, that very latent impression is called *kaṣāya*.
विषयेषु दोषदर्शनपूर्वकं योगिना प्रयत्नातिशयवशात् कषायविघ्नो निवारणीयः ।
The obstacle of *kaṣāya* must be eliminated by the yogin through exceptional effort preceded by observing the defects in sense objects.
482 · रसास्वादः
योगिनो ब्रह्मानन्दानुभवो जायते ।
The experience of the bliss of Brahman arises for the yogin.
विक्षेपरूपदुःखनिवृत्तिश्च अनुभूयते ।
And the cessation of suffering in the form of mental distraction is experienced.
क्वचिद्दुःखनिवृत्त्याप्यानन्दो जायते ।
In certain instances, pleasure arises merely from the cessation of pain.
यथा भारवाहिपुरुषस्य भारापनयादानन्दो जायते ।
Just as relief arises for a porter when his load is put down.
न हि तदानन्दे विषयान्तरं कारणम् ।
Indeed, no other external sense-object is the cause of that pleasure.
भारप्रयुक्तदुःखनिवृत्त्या च सुखं मेऽभूत् इति वक्ति ।
And merely through the cessation of the pain caused by the load, he says, 'I feel happy.'
तथा योगिनोऽपि समाधौ विक्षेपजन्यदुःखनिवृत्त्यापि आनन्दो जायेत, सोऽनुभवो रसास्वाद इत्युच्यते ।
Similarly, for the yogin too in samādhi, joy may arise merely through the cessation of pain produced by mental distraction; that experience is called *rasāsvāda*.
अस्मिन्नेवानन्दे यदि तृप्तः स्याद्योगी तदा सर्वोपाधिशून्यब्रह्मानन्दाकारा वृत्तिर्न स्यात्तस्य ।
If the yogin were to become satisfied with this joy alone, then the vṛtti taking the form of the bliss of Brahman devoid of all upādhis would not arise for him.
ततस्तदधीनानन्दानुभवोऽपि न भवेत् ।
Consequently, the experience of supreme bliss dependent upon that vṛtti would not occur either.
तस्मात् दुःखनिवृत्तिजन्यानन्दानुभवरूपो रसास्वादोऽपि समाधौ विघ्नः स्यात् ।
Therefore, *rasāsvāda*, which is in the form of enjoying the joy born of the cessation of suffering, is also an obstacle in samādhi.
वाञ्छितार्थलाभेऽपि तद्विरोधिनिवृत्त्यानन्दो जायत इत्यत्र दृष्टान्तान्तरमुच्यते ।
To illustrate that joy arises simply from the removal of an obstacle to a desired goal even before the goal is attained, another example is stated.
भूमिस्थो निधिरत्यन्तं क्रूरेण विषधरेण कृष्णसर्पेण रक्ष्यते ।
A treasure buried underground is guarded by an extremely ferocious, venomous black serpent.
तत्प्राप्तेः प्राक्तत्प्राप्तिप्रतिबिन्धस्य सर्पस्य निवृत्त्याप्यानन्दो जायते ।
Prior to attaining that treasure, joy arises simply from the removal of the serpent that was obstructing its attainment.
सर्पनिवृत्तिजन्येनानन्देनैवालम्बुद्धिः सन्निधिलाभोद्यमं यदि त्यजति, तदा निधिलाभजन्यपरमानन्दप्राप्तिर्न स्यात्तस्य ।
If, feeling satisfied merely with the joy of the snake's departure, one abandons the effort to obtain the treasure, then one would never attain the supreme joy born of acquiring the treasure.
तद्वदत्राद्वैतब्रह्मरूपो महानिधिर्देहाद्यनात्मपदार्थप्रतीतिरूपेण विक्षेपसर्पेणावृतो वर्तते ।
Similarly, here, the great treasure in the form of non-dual Brahman is veiled by the serpent of distraction consisting in the perception of non-Self objects like the body.
विक्षेपरूपसर्पनिवृत्त्यापि अवान्तरानन्दरूपो रसास्वादो भवति ।
Mere removal of the serpent of distraction results in *rasāsvāda*, which is an intermediate joy.
अयमेव च निधिरूपेऽद्वैतब्रह्मप्राप्तिजन्यपरमानन्दलाभे विघ्न इत्युच्यते ।
And this very contentment is called an obstacle in gaining the supreme bliss born of attaining non-dual Brahman, the treasure.
अथवा - सविकल्पसमाध्यनुष्ठानोत्तरं निर्विकल्पसमाधिः प्रसिद्ध्यति ।
Alternatively: *nirvikalpa-samādhi* is attained only after the practice of *savikalpa-samādhi*.
सविकल्पसमाधौ त्रिपुटी प्रतीयते ।
In *savikalpa-samādhi*, the triad (*tripuṭī* of knower, knowing, and known) is experienced.
अत एव सोपाधिकोऽयं समाधिरिति वक्ष्यते ।
Hence, this samādhi is described as *sopādhika* (endowed with adjuncts).
निर्विकल्पसमाधौ तु त्रिपुट्यभावादेव निरुपाधिकानन्दो जायते ।
In *nirvikalpa-samādhi*, however, because of the very absence of the triad, unconditioned ānanda arises.
इत्थं सविकल्पसमाध्यारम्भदशायां सोपाधिकः सविकल्पसमाध्यानन्दोऽपरिहार्यतयानुभूयते ।
Thus, at the initial stage of *savikalpa-samādhi*, the conditioned joy of *savikalpa-samādhi* is inevitably experienced.
स एव रसास्वाद इत्युच्यते ।
That itself is called *rasāsvāda*.
तस्माद्विक्षेपनिवृत्तिजन्यानन्दानुभवो वा, सविकल्पसमाध्यानन्दानुभवो वा रसास्वाद इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, either the experience of joy born of the cessation of distraction or the experience of the bliss of *savikalpa-samādhi* is called *rasāsvāda*.
स द्विविधोऽपि रसास्वादो निर्विकल्पसमाधिजपरमानन्दानुभवविरोधित्वाद्विघ्नो भवति ।
Both forms of *rasāsvāda* are obstacles because they obstruct the experience of supreme bliss born of *nirvikalpa-samādhi*.
अतः स परित्याज्य एव ।
Therefore, it must certainly be abandoned.
एवं निर्विकल्पसमाधौ सम्भवत् विघ्नचतुष्टयं सावधानतया परिहृत्य यः समाधिजं परमानन्दमनुभवति स एव जीवन्मुक्तः ।
Thus, one who carefully overcomes the four potential obstacles in *nirvikalpa-samādhi* and experiences the supreme bliss born of *samādhi*, he alone is a jīvanmukta.
483 · ज्ञानिनो बाह्यप्रवृत्तिर्न सम्भवतीत्याक्षेपः
ज्ञानिनश्चित्तं निरालम्बनतया न तिष्ठति ।
The mind of a jñānin does not remain without an object of support.
प्रारब्धबलात्समाधेरुत्थितस्यापि समाध्यनुभूतपरमानन्दस्मृतिः स्यादेव ।
Even for one who has arisen from samādhi due to the force of prārabdha, there is indeed the memory of the supreme ānanda experienced in samādhi.
तस्मादुत्थानसमयेऽपि ज्ञानिनश्चित्तं न निरालम्बं भवति ।
Therefore, even at the time of arising from samādhi, the mind of the jñānin does not remain objectless.
भोजनादिप्रवृत्तिरपि ज्ञानिनः केवलं प्रारब्धकर्मजन्यैव ।
Even activity like eating food for a jñānin is produced solely by prārabdha-karma.
तथापि भोजनादिव्यवहारेषु दुःखमस्तीति ज्ञात्वैव ज्ञानी प्रवर्तते ।
Even so, the jñānin engages in worldly activities such as eating only knowing that there is pain in them.
भोजनादिप्रवृत्तिरपि यस्य समाधिसुषुप्तिविरोधित्वेन शरीरनिर्वाहकतया प्रतीता खेदरूपैव भवति ।
For whom even the activity of eating, being perceived as merely sustaining the body and being opposed to samādhi and deep sleep, is of the very nature of distress,
तस्य न तत्राधिका प्रवृत्तिर्जायते ।
for him no excessive activity arises therein.
एवमनेके आचार्या इममेव पक्षं स्वीकुर्वन्ति ।
In this manner, many ācāryas accept this very position.
जीवन्मुक्तानन्दोऽपि बाह्यप्रवृत्तौ न जायते ।
Also, the bliss of jīvanmukti does not arise during external activity.
किन्तु निवृत्तावेव जायते ।
Rather, it arises only in inward withdrawal.
अतो जीवन्मुक्तिसुखार्थिनो ज्ञानिनो बाह्यप्रवृत्तिरेव न स्यात् ।
Therefore, for a jñānin desirous of the bliss of jīvanmukti, there should be no external activity at all.
484
(४६५-४८३) आवर्तेषु कृतशङ्कायाः समाधानम्—ज्ञानिनो निरङ्कुशप्रवृत्तेः प्रारब्धवशाद्व्यवहारः सिद्ध्यतीति तद्व्यवहारनिवृत्तौ नियमः कर्तव्य इति शङ्कासमाधानम् ।
Resolution of the doubt raised in sections 465–483—resolution of the objection that since the jñānin's worldly engagement occurs due to prārabdha following unbridled action, a restrictive rule must be prescribed to restrain that engagement.
ज्ञानिनो निवृत्तावपि नियमसद्भावोक्तिरसङ्गता ।
The statement that there is a mandatory rule governing cessation for the jñānin is also untenable.
निवृत्तौ वा प्रवृत्तौ वा वेदस्य आज्ञारूपो विधिर्न ज्ञानिनोऽस्ति ।
Neither in cessation nor in engagement is there any mandatory Vedic injunction commanding the jñānin.
तद्व्यवहारे नियमाभावाज्ज्ञानी निरङ्कुशः ।
Due to the absence of any restrictive injunction in his worldly conduct, the jñānin is completely unbridled (free).
तद्व्यवहारः सर्वोऽपि प्रारब्धायत्त एव ।1,2,3,1
All his conduct whatsoever is entirely dependent on prārabdha alone.
टिप्पणी
1.
(१) अखण्डचित्स्वरूपावगाहिचित्तवृत्तेर्निद्रारूपो लयो विघ्नः प्रथमः ।
(1) The first obstacle is laya (dissolution/sleep), which is in the form of sleep falling upon the mind-modification that is absorbed in the partless nature of pure Consciousness.
(२) तस्या विषयान्तरावलम्बनरूपो विक्षेपो विघ्नो द्वितीयः ।
(2) The second obstacle is vikṣepa (distraction), which is of the nature of that mind-modification turning to grasp other external objects.
(३) लयविक्षेपयोरभावेऽपि स्तब्धतारूपः कषायो विघ्नस्तृतीयः ।
(3) The third obstacle is kaṣāya (stiffness/attachment), which is of the form of rigidity (numbness due to latent impressions) even when laya and vikṣepa are absent.
(४) दुःखनिवृत्तिरूपानन्देन सविकल्पसमाध्यानन्देन वा तृप्तचित्तवृत्तिरूपो रसास्वादो विघ्नश्चतुर्थः ।
(4) The fourth obstacle is rasāsvāda (tasting of lower bliss), which consists in the mind-modification resting satisfied with the bliss of cessation of suffering or with the bliss of savikalpa-samādhi.
2.
विषयानन्दः सातिशयानन्दत्वात् साङ्कुशः ।
The pleasure derived from sense objects is limited (sāṅkuśa), because it admits of higher and lower degrees.
ज्ञानिन आनन्दस्तु ब्रह्मानन्दाभिन्नत्वान्निरङ्कुशः ।
The bliss of the jñānin, however, is unbridled (limitless), because it is non-different from the bliss of Brahman.
3.
रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पभ्रान्तिर्यथा बाध्यते तथाधिष्ठानब्रह्मज्ञानेनाहङ्कारादिजगद्भ्रान्तिः बाध्यते ।
Just as the illusion of a snake is sublated by knowledge of the rope, so the illusion of the world beginning with ego is sublated by knowledge of the substratum *Brahman*.
तथापि, यथा सर्पज्ञानजन्यभयकम्पादिः कालान्तरे निवर्तते, तथा प्रारब्धकर्मजन्यभोगोऽपि प्रारब्धनाशानन्तरमेव निवर्तते ।
Even so, just as the fear, trembling, etc., produced by the thought of a snake subside only after some time, so too the experience generated by *prārabdha-karma* ceases only after the exhaustion of *prārabdha*.
मन्दान्धकारस्था रज्जुः पुनरपि सर्पात्मना यथा प्रतीयते, तथा भोगकाले मनुष्योऽहमित्यादिप्रतीतिर्ज्ञानिनोऽपि कदाचिज्जायेत ।
Just as a rope lying in dim light may again appear as a snake, so at the time of experiencing results, an appearance like 'I am human' may occasionally arise even in an enlightened person.
उपादानभूताज्ञाननिवृत्त्यनन्तरमपि प्रपञ्चप्रतीतिर्ज्ञानिनो मुक्तेषुन्यायेन भवत्येव ।
Even after the cessation of *avidyā*, its material cause, the perception of the world does indeed continue for the knower according to the maxim of the discharged arrow.
यथा व्याघ्रबुद्ध्योत्सृष्टो बाणः पश्चाद्गोमतौ उत्पन्नायामपि न स्वयं प्रशान्तवेगो भवति ।
Just as an arrow shot under the impression of a tiger does not spontaneously lose its momentum even when the awareness that it is a cow arises afterwards;
गच्छन्नेव वर्तते ।
it continues in flight;
अन्ते च वेगक्षयादेव प्रशाम्यति ।
and in the end it stops only through the exhaustion of its velocity;
एवं हस्तविसृष्टबाणस्थानीयं प्रारब्धं कर्मापि फलदानाय प्रवृत्तं फलक्षयादेव प्रशाम्यति ।
so too *prārabdha-karma*, which is comparable to an arrow released from the hand, having been set in motion to yield its fruits, ceases only upon the exhaustion of those fruits;
नान्यतः ।
not by anything else.
अतस्तावत्कलं तत्प्रयुक्ता प्रपञ्चप्रतीतिरपि उत्पन्नायामपि ब्रह्ममतौ अनुवर्तेतैव ।
Therefore, for that duration, the world-appearance caused by it does indeed persist, even though knowledge of *Brahman* has arisen.
(१) यस्य ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धं भिक्षाभोजनादिफलमात्रहेतुस्तस्य भिक्षाभोजनादिमात्रे प्रवृत्तिर्जायते ।
(1) That knower whose *prārabdha* is the cause merely of fruits like obtaining food through alms engages only in activities such as obtaining alms.
(२) यस्य तु प्रारब्धमितोऽप्यधिकभोगहेतुः तस्याधिकेऽपि व्यापारे प्रवृत्तिर्भवति ।
(2) But for one whose *prārabdha* is the cause of greater experience than this, engagement takes place even in more extensive activities.
अत्राक्षेपः - ननु यस्य प्रारब्धं भिक्षाभोजनमात्रहेतुस्तस्यैव ज्ञानं जायेत ।
Here is an objection: Knowledge should arise only in one whose *prārabdha* causes merely eating alms.
यस्य पुनः प्रारब्धमधिकव्यापारहेतुर्नैव तस्य ज्ञानं जायेत ।
In one whose *prārabdha* brings about extensive activities, knowledge should never arise.
तस्माद्भिक्षाभोजनादिव्यापारादधिकव्यापारो न ज्ञानिनो युज्यते ।
Therefore, activity greater than mere begging of food and eating is not proper for a knower.
यस्याधिकव्यापारे प्रवृत्तिरस्ति, स नैव स्याज्ज्ञानीति ।
One who is engaged in greater activity cannot be an enlightened person at all.
समाधानं - नेयं सम्भवति शङ्का ।
Resolution: This doubt is not tenable.
यतः श्रीरामकृष्णयाज्ञवल्क्यजनकादयो ज्ञानिन उच्यन्ते ।
Because Śrī Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Yājñavalkya, Janaka, and others are acknowledged as knowers of truth.
तेषु च सभायां विजयेन धनसङ्ग्रहव्यवहारे याज्ञवल्क्यस्य, तथा राज्यपरिपालनादिव्यापारे जनकस्य च प्रवृत्तिः कथिता ।
Among them, Yājñavalkya's engagement in amassing wealth through victory in debate in the assembly, and Janaka's engagement in ruling the kingdom, etc., are well recorded.
अपि च वासिष्ठादिग्रन्थेष्वनेकेषां ज्ञानिनां व्यवहारो नानाप्रकारः कथ्यते ।
Furthermore, in texts such as the *Yogavāsiṣṭha*, the conduct of various enlightened beings is described to be of diverse kinds.
तस्माज्ज्ञानिनः प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैवास्ति नियमः ।
Therefore, there is no fixed rule regarding either the engagement or the renunciation of an enlightened person.
यद्यपि याज्ञवल्क्यः सभायां जयं लब्ध्वा पश्चात् विद्वत्सन्न्यासरूपां निवृत्तिं दधे ।
Although Yājñavalkya, after winning victory in the assembly, later adopted renunciation in the form of *vidvat-sannyāsa*;
प्रवृत्तौ च नानाप्रकारा दुःखहेतुभूता दोषाः कथिताः ।
and various defects leading to grief in active life are mentioned;
तथापि याज्ञवल्क्यस्य विद्वत्सन्न्यासात्प्राक् ज्ञानाभावोक्तिर्न युज्यते ।
still, to claim that Yājñavalkya lacked knowledge before taking up *vidvat-sannyāsa* is incorrect.
ज्ञानं प्रागप्यासीदेव ।
He already possessed knowledge even prior to that.
जीवन्मुक्तिसुखं परं न तेन प्राप्तम् ।
However, the undisturbed bliss of *jīvanmukti* had not yet been attained by him.
तस्माज्जीवन्मुक्तिसुखावाप्तये सर्वस्वसङ्ग्रहपरित्यागमकरोत् ।
Therefore, in order to attain the bliss of *jīvanmukti*, he completely renounced all collected possessions.
(१) याज्ञवल्क्यस्य प्रारब्धं किञ्चित्कालमधिकभोगहेतुरासीत्, पश्चात्स्वल्पभोगहेतुरासीत् ।
(1) Yājñavalkya's *prārabdha* was for a certain time the cause of extensive worldly enjoyment, and later it became the cause of minimal enjoyment.
तस्मात् प्रथमं याज्ञवल्क्यस्य विनैवारुचिं भोगाधिक्यम्, पश्चादत्यन्तारुच्या सर्वभोगत्यागश्चाभूत् ।
Consequently, initially Yājñavalkya experienced abundant enjoyments without revulsion, and afterwards through intense dispassion arose total renunciation of all worldly enjoyments.
(२) जनकस्य प्रारब्धं तु आमरणं राज्यपरिपालनादिरूपविशेषभोगहेतुरासीत् ।
(2) Janaka's *prārabdha*, however, was until death the cause of extensive specific activities such as governing the realm.
तस्मात् तस्य भोगत्यागो नाभूत्कदाचिदपि ।
Therefore, he never renounced his worldly obligations at any time;
नाप्यरुचिर्भोगेषु सञ्जाता ।
nor did aversion arise towards these worldly experiences.
1.
विधिना सर्वकर्मासङ्गपरित्यागी सन्न्यासी ।
One who renounces all actions and attachments according to scriptural injunction is a saṃnyāsin.
स च हंसपरमहंसभेदाद्द्विविधः ।
And he is of two kinds by the division of Haṃsa and Paramahaṃsa.
तीव्रवैराग्ययुक्तो हंससन्न्यासः कुटीचकबहूदकभेदेन द्विप्रकारः ।
Haṃsa renunciation, which is accompanied by intense dispassion, is of two types by the division of Kuṭīcaka and Bahūdaka.
तीर्थाटनाशक्तः कुटीचकः, तीर्थाटनसमर्थो बहूदकः ।
One who is unable to wander on pilgrimage is a Kuṭīcaka, and one who is capable of wandering on pilgrimage is a Bahūdaka.
परमहंससन्न्यासोऽपि विविदिषासन्न्यासो विद्वत्सन्न्यासश्चेति द्विप्रकारः ।
Paramahaṃsa renunciation also is of two types: vividiṣā-saṃnyāsa and vidvat-saṃnyāsa.
प्राग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तेर्विषयदोषदृष्ट्या तीव्रतरवैराग्येण जिज्ञासुना क्रियमाणः सन्न्यासो विविदिषासन्न्यासः ।
The renunciation undertaken by a seeker prior to the dawn of knowledge, through the perception of defects in sense objects and stronger dispassion, is vividiṣā-saṃnyāsa.
ज्ञानानन्तरं दोषदृष्ट्या मिथ्यात्वादिदृढनिश्चयेन तीव्रतमवैराग्येण च विदुषा क्रियमाणः सन्न्यासो विद्वत्सन्न्यासः ।
The renunciation undertaken by the knower after knowledge, through the perception of defects, firm conviction of the illusoriness of objects, and the strongest dispassion, is vidvat-saṃnyāsa.
विद्वत्सन्न्यासादिलक्षणं तु नारदपरिव्राजकोपनिषत्सूतसंहितादौ द्रष्टव्यम् ।
However, the definitions of vidvat-saṃnyāsa and others are to be seen in the Nārada-parivrājaka Upaniṣad, the Sūta-saṃhitā, and other texts.
(३) वामदेवादिप्रारब्धं स्वल्पभोगहेतुरासीत् ।
(3) The prārabdha of sages like Vāmadeva was the cause of very little worldly experience.
अतस्तेषां सदारुच्युत्पत्तेर्भोगेषु प्रवृत्तिरेव नाभूत् ।
Therefore, due to the constant arising of distaste in them, there was no engagement at all in worldly pleasures.
(४) शिखिध्वजस्य ज्ञानानन्तरं राज्यादिष्वधिका प्रवृत्तिः कथ्यते वासिष्ठे ।
(4) In the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha, greater engagement in ruling the kingdom and other affairs is described for Śikhidhvaja even after gaining knowledge.
इत्थं ज्ञानिनां नानाप्रकारा विलक्षणव्यवहाराः कथिताः ।
Thus, various distinct kinds of worldly behaviors are described among knowers.
सर्वेषामपि तेषां सममेव ज्ञानम् ।
Yet the knowledge of all of them is entirely equal.
फलमपि मोक्षरूपं समानमेव ।
The fruit, in the form of mokṣa, is likewise identical.
व्यवहारास्तु प्रारब्धभेदान्नानाप्रकाराः ।
Behaviors, however, are of various kinds owing to differences in their prārabdha karma.
व्यवहारलोपाज्जीवन्मुक्तिसुखमधिक्रियेत ।
With the cessation of worldly activity, the experiential bliss of jīvanmukti increases.
व्यवहाराधिक्ये जीवन्मुक्तिसुखं न्यूनतां व्रजेत् ।
When worldly activity is excessive, the bliss of jīvanmukti undergoes diminution.
485 · ज्ञानिनो विदेहमोक्षत्यागः परलोकेच्छा च न जायतेअत्र केचनाक्षिपन्ति
जीवन्मुक्तिसुखं त्यक्त्वा तुच्छविषयभोगे प्रवृत्तो विदेहमोक्षमपि त्यक्त्वा वैकुण्ठादिलोकेच्छया तत्तल्लोकमपि प्राप्नुयादिति ।
Here some raise an objection: '[If a knower of truth], having abandoned the bliss of jīvanmukti, becomes engaged in the enjoyment of trifling sense-objects, then having likewise cast aside disembodied liberation (videha-mokṣa), he might also attain those respective worlds out of a desire for realms such as Vaikuṇṭha.'
टिप्पणी
1.
ज्ञानं सर्वेषां सममित्यात्रायं श्लोकः प्रसिद्धतया कथ्यते—कृष्णो भोगी शुकस्त्यागी नृपौ जनकराघवौ । वसिष्ठः कर्मकर्ता च त एते ज्ञानिनः समाः ॥ इति ।
To show that knowledge is the same in all, this well-known verse is cited: Kṛṣṇa was an enjoyer of pleasures, Śuka was a total renouncer, Janaka and Rāma were kings, and Vasiṣṭha was an active performer of rites; yet all these knowers of truth are equal.
इत्थमेतेषां प्रारब्धभेदाद्व्यवहारभेदेऽपि ज्ञानं सर्वेषां समानमेवेति साम्प्रदायिकश्लोकार्थः ।
Thus, even though their outward behavior differs on account of variations in their prārabdha-karma, the knowledge of all is entirely equal—this is the purport of the traditional verse.
ननु तत्त्वबोधवतामपि रागादिमत्त्वेन वैषम्योपलम्भाज्ज्ञानस्यापि मुक्तिहेतुत्वं निश्चेतुं न शक्यमित्याशङ्क्य रागादेर्व्याध्यादिवदारब्धकर्मफलत्वान्मुक्तिप्रतिबन्धकत्वमसिद्धम् ।
If one objects: 'Since we observe disparity even among knowers of truth due to presence of attachment etc., it is impossible to be certain that knowledge is the cause of liberation,' we answer: because attachment and so forth, like physical disease, are merely the fruit of prārabdha-karma, their capacity to obstruct liberation is unproven.
अतो न शास्त्रार्थे विप्रतिपत्तव्यमित्याहुर्विद्यारण्यस्वामिनः—प्रारब्धकर्मनानात्वाद्बुद्धानामन्यथान्यथा । वर्तनं तेन शास्त्रार्थे भ्रमितव्यं न पण्डितैः ॥ (चि. दी. २८७) इति ।
Therefore, one should not be conflicted regarding the scriptural import—so says Svāmī Vidyāraṇya: Due to the multiplicity of prārabdha-karma, the conduct of the enlightened varies in diverse ways; therefore, the wise should not be bewildered about the import of scripture. (चि. दी. २८७)
कथं तर्हि प्रतिपत्तव्यमित्याहुः—स्वस्वकर्मानुसारेण वर्तन्तां ते यथा तथा । अविशिष्टः सर्वबोधः समा मुक्तिरिति स्थितिः ॥ (चि. दी. २८८) इति ।
To the question, 'How then should it be understood?', he replies: Let them act in whatever manner according to their respective prārabdha-karma; the awakening in all is undifferentiated, and liberation is identical—this is the established truth. (चि. दी. २८८)
2.
अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति ज्ञानोदयकाल एवाविद्यात्मकोपादानकारणं विनश्यति ।
At the very moment of the rise of the knowledge 'I am Brahman', the material cause of the nature of avidyā perishes.
तत्कार्यभूता जगच्चिदाभासादयोऽपि बाध्यन्त एव ।
Its effects too, such as the world and the reflection of consciousness (cidābhāsa), are indeed sublated.
तथापि प्रारब्धकर्मरूपं निमित्तं यावदवतिष्ठते, तावज्ज्ञानबाधिता अपि देहजगच्चिदाभासादयोऽनुवर्तमाना एव प्रतीयेरन् ।
Even so, as long as the instrumental cause in the form of prārabdha-karma persists, so long would the body, the world, the cidābhāsa, etc., though sublated by knowledge, appear as continuing.
प्रारब्धावसाने च न प्रतीयेरन् ।
And upon the exhaustion of prārabdha, they would no longer appear.
इयमेव विदेहमुक्तिः ।
This alone is videhamukti.
उत्तममध्यमकनिष्ठाधमतराधमतमभेदेन पञ्चविधं प्रारब्धम् ।
Prārabdha is fivefold by the division of superior (uttama), middling (madhyama), lowest (kaniṣṭha), inferior (adhamatara), and most inferior (adhamatama).
(१) सर्वदाजन्ममरणं वैराग्यहेतुभूतं निवृत्तिप्रधानं प्रारब्धमुत्तमम् ।
(1) Prārabdha that is constantly from birth to death a cause of dispassion and characterized primarily by renunciation is superior (uttama).
यथा शुकवामदेवसनकादिप्रारब्धम् ।
As, for example, the prārabdha of Śuka, Vāmadeva, Sanaka, and others.
(२) आदौ प्रवृत्तिहेतुभूतमपि पश्चान्निवृत्तिहेतुभूतं प्रारब्धं मध्यमम् ।
(2) Prārabdha that is at first a cause of active engagement (pravṛtti) but later becomes a cause of renunciation (nivṛtti) is middling (madhyama).
यथा याज्ञवल्क्यादिप्रारब्धम् ।
As, for example, the prārabdha of Yājñavalkya and others.
(३) सदा प्रवृत्तिहेतुभूतं प्रारब्धं कनिष्ठम् ।
(3) Prārabdha that is always a cause of active engagement is lowest (kaniṣṭha).
यथा जनकादिप्रारब्धम् ।
As, for example, the prārabdha of Janaka and others.
(४) आदौ निवृत्तिहेतुभूतं सत् पश्चात्प्रवृत्तिहेतुभूतं प्रारब्धमधमतरम् ।
(4) Prārabdha that is at first a cause of renunciation, but subsequently becomes a cause of active worldly engagement, is inferior (adhamatara).
यथा शिखिध्वजालर्करहूगणप्रियव्रतादिप्रारब्धम् ।
As, for example, the prārabdha of Śikhidhvaja, Alarka, Rahūgaṇa, Priyavrata, and others.
(५) कामचारकामवादकामभक्षादिहेतुभूतं प्रारब्धं अधमतमम् ।
(5) Prārabdha that is the cause of unrestricted movement, speech, eating at will, etc., is most inferior (adhamatama).
यथा दत्तात्रेयादिप्रारब्धम् ।
As, for example, the prārabdha of Dattātreya and others.
नैवायं सम्भवत्याक्षेपः -
Nor is this objection at all tenable:
(१) जीवन्मुक्तिसुखत्यागो भोगप्रवृत्तिश्च ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धबलात् सम्भवति ।
(1) Renouncing the bliss of jīvanmukti and engaging in enjoyment is possible for the knower by the force of prārabdha;
(२) विदेहमुक्तित्यागः परलोकगमनं च तस्य नैव सम्भवति ।
(2) But renunciation of videhamukti and departure to another world is not at all possible for him.
यतः (१) ज्ञानिनः प्राणा बहिर्न गच्छन्ति ।
Because (1) the prāṇas of a knower do not depart outwards,
न तस्य प्राणा उत्क्रामन्ति इत्यादिश्रुतेः ।
due to śruti passages such as 'His prāṇas do not depart'.
तस्मान्न परलोकगमनं ज्ञानिनः सम्भवति ।
Therefore, departure to another world is not possible for a knower.
(२) विदेहमोक्षत्यागश्च न सम्भवति ।
(2) And renunciation of videhamokṣa is impossible.
यतो ज्ञानेन निःशेषाज्ञाननिवृत्तौ प्रारब्धभोगानन्तरं स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीराकारपरिणतस्य मूलाज्ञानस्य स्वाधिष्ठानचैतन्ये निःशेषप्रविलय एव विदेहमोक्ष इति कथ्यते ।
Because, upon the complete cessation of ignorance through knowledge, after experiencing the prārabdha, the complete dissolution into its own substratum Consciousness of the root ignorance (mūlāvidyā)—which had transformed into the shapes of the gross and subtle bodies—is itself called videhamokṣa.
स चाज्ञाननाशेऽवश्यं भवति ।
And that inevitably takes place upon the destruction of ignorance.
मूलाज्ञानेऽवशिष्टे, निवृत्तस्याज्ञानस्य पुनरापाते वा, विदेहमुक्तिर्न सिद्ध्येत् ।
Videhamukti would fail to be attained only if root ignorance remained, or if removed ignorance recurred.
मूलाज्ञानविरोधिज्ञानोदयसमकालमेव चाज्ञानं नावशिष्यते ।
And ignorance does not remain at all, at the very moment of the rise of knowledge opposed to root ignorance.
प्रमाणतो नष्टमज्ञानमपि न पुनरुत्पद्यते, ततो न विदेहमोक्षाभावः सम्भवति ।
Ignorance destroyed by pramāṇa never arises again; hence the absence of videhamokṣa is impossible.
विदेहमोक्षत्यागो परलोकगमने च ज्ञानिन इच्छा न जायेत ।
Moreover, no desire would arise in the knower to forgo videhamokṣa or to depart to another world.
यतो ज्ञानिन इच्छापि तावत् केवलं प्रारब्धाधीनैव जायते ।
Because even a desire in the knower arises solely depending on prārabdha.
यावतीं सामग्रीं विना ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धभोगो न जायेत, तावतीमेव सामग्रीं प्रारब्धं जनयति ।
Prārabdha generates only as much requisite accessories without which the knower's experience of prārabdha would not occur.
न हीच्छां विना भोगो जायेत ।
For without desire, no experience of enjoyment could take place.
तस्माज्ज्ञानिन इच्छापि प्रारब्धफलभूतैव ।
Therefore, even the desire of a knower is merely the fruition of prārabdha.
लोकान्तरे वा, इहलोके वा शरीरान्तरसम्बन्धोऽपि ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धाधीनो न जायते इत्येतत् प्रागेवास्मिन् तरङ्गे प्रतिपादितम् ।
That connection with another body, either in another world or in this world, never occurs for a knower even as dependent on prārabdha, has already been established earlier in this chapter.
तस्माज्ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धबलादपि विदेहमोक्षत्यागे वा परलोकगमने वा नैवेच्छा सम्भवति ।
Therefore, even by the force of prārabdha, a desire to forgo videhamokṣa or to go to another world is not at all possible for the knower.
486 · ज्ञानिनो मन्दप्रारब्धवशाज्जीवन्मुक्तिसुखविरुद्धा प्रवृत्तिः
जीवन्मुक्तिसुखस्य विरोधिनी वर्तमानशरीरस्थाधिकभोगेच्छा भिक्षाभोजनादिवत् जनकादीनां सम्भवति ।
The desire for excessive enjoyment situated in the present body, which is opposed to the happiness of jīvanmukti, is possible in the case of Janaka and others, just like food through alms.
अत्रायमभिप्रायः - ज्ञानिनो बाह्यप्रवृत्तिर्न जीवन्मुक्तिविरोधिनी ।
Here this is the underlying meaning: the outward engagement of a jñānin is not opposed to jīvanmukti itself;
किन्तु जीवन्मुक्तिविलक्षणसुखविरोधिनी ।
rather, it is opposed to the distinct/experiential bliss of jīvanmukti.
आत्मा हि नित्यमुक्तः ।
For the *ātman* is ever-liberated.
भ्रान्त्याविद्योत्थया तस्मिन्बन्धः प्रतीयते ।
Bondage is merely perceived in it through delusion born of *avidyā*.
यदा पुनर्ज्ञानं जायते तदैवाविद्याजन्यबन्धभ्रमोऽपि निवर्तते ।
When knowledge arises, at that very moment the delusion of bondage born of *avidyā* ceases.
ज्ञानोत्पत्त्यनन्तरमपि न बन्धभ्रमो जायते ।1
Even after the rise of knowledge, no delusion of bondage ever arises again.
टिप्पणी
1.
देहात्मज्ञानवज्ज्ञानं देहात्मज्ञानबाधकम् । आत्मन्येव भवेद्यस्य स नेच्छन्नपि मुच्यते ॥ इति ।
'He in whom the knowledge sublating the notion of body as self arises with respect to the Self just as firmly as the ordinary idea that the body is the self, is liberated even without desiring it' (Upadeśasāhasrī 4.5).
स्वप्नात्प्रबुद्धस्य यथा स्वप्नभ्रान्तिनिवृत्तिपरित्यागे स्वप्नदृष्टपरलोकगमने च नैवेच्छा जायते ।
Just as for one awakened from a dream, there is no desire at all to abandon the cessation of dream-delusion, nor to go to the other world seen in the dream,
तथा ज्ञानिनोऽपि बन्धभ्रान्तिनिवृत्तिरूपविदेहमोक्षपरित्यागे स्वर्गादिपरलोकगमने च नैवेच्छा सम्भवति ।
likewise, for the jñānin too, no desire is possible either to abandon videha-mukti (which is the cessation of the delusion of bondage) or to go to higher worlds like heaven.
बन्धभ्रान्त्यभाव एव सशरीरस्य ज्ञानिनो जीवन्मुक्तिरित्युच्यते ।
The mere absence of the delusion of bondage for an embodied jñānin is called jīvanmukti.
देहादिप्रवृत्तिनिवृत्त्यादौ चिदात्मनि बन्धभ्रान्तिर्न ज्ञानिनः सम्भवति ।
During the activity or cessation of the body etc., no delusion of bondage is possible for the jñānin in the *cit-ātman*.
तस्माद्बाह्यप्रवृत्त्यापि जीवन्मुक्तिर्न निवर्तते ।
Therefore, even through outward activity, jīvanmukti is not sublated.
तथापि बाह्यप्रवृत्तौ जीवन्मुक्ते विलक्षणं सुखं न जायते ।
Nevertheless, during outward activity, the distinct experiential joy of jīvanmukti does not manifest.
एकाग्रतापन्नान्तःकरणपरिणामवशादेव तत्सुखं जायते ।
That bliss arises solely due to the modification of the internal organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*) having achieved one-pointed concentration.
स चैतकाग्रतापरिणामो बाह्यप्रवृत्त्या प्रतिबध्यते ।
And this transformation of one-pointedness is obstructed by external activity.
इत्थं प्रारब्धभेदवशाज्ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारो नानाप्रकारः ।
Thus, according to differences in *prārabdha*, the conduct of a jñānin is of diverse kinds.
परन्तु यस्य प्रारब्धमधिकप्रवृत्तिहेतुः, तस्य तन्मन्दप्रारब्धमित्युच्यते ।
However, one whose prārabdha is the cause of excessive outward engagement, his prārabdha is termed *manda-prārabdha* (sluggish prārabdha).
यतो हि अधिका प्रवृत्तिरेकाग्रताविरोधिनी ।
Because excessive activity is indeed opposed to one-pointed concentration.
अन्तरेण चैकाग्र्यं निरुपाधिकानन्दो न प्रतीयेत ।
And without one-pointedness, the unconditioned ānanda cannot be felt.
एतच्च समाधिनिरूपणप्रकरणे कथितम् ।
And this has already been stated in the section determining samādhi.
ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारोऽनियतः॥ ४८७–४८८ ॥
487
यदुक्तं ज्ञानिनः सकलानात्मपदार्थेषु मिथ्याबुद्धिसद्भावात् न रागः सम्भवति ।
As to what was asserted — that for a knower, due to the presence of the cognition of falsity in all non-Self objects, attachment is not possible,
अतः प्रवृत्तिरेव न स्यादिति ।
and therefore activity would never occur at all —
नैतद्युज्यते ।
this is not tenable.
कुतः, यथा देहे मिथ्यात्वबुद्धौ सत्यामपि ज्ञानिनो देहानुकूलभिक्षादौ केवलं प्रारब्धबलात् प्रवृत्तिर्जायते, तथा यस्य ज्ञानिनोऽधिकभोगार्थं प्रारब्धं वर्तते, तस्याधिकापि प्रवृत्तिर्जायेतैव ।
Why? Just as, even when the cognition of the falsity of the body is present, the knower's activity in seeking alms suitable for the body arises purely through the force of prārabdha, similarly, for whichever knower prārabdha exists for greater experiencing, greater activity would certainly arise for him as well.
यथा च ऐन्द्रजालिकमायां मिथ्येति जानन्तोऽपि तद्दिदृक्षया सर्वे जनाः प्रवर्तन्ते ।
And just as all people engage out of a desire to watch a magician's illusion even while knowing it to be false,
तथा सर्वेष्वपि पदार्थेषु मिथ्यात्वबुद्धौ सत्यामपि तद्भोगार्थं ज्ञानिनः प्रवर्तन्ते ।
likewise, even when the knowledge of the falsity of all objects is present, knowers engage in them for the sake of experiencing their prārabdha.
488 · अत्राक्षेपसमाधाने
यस्य पुनः यस्मिन् पदार्थे दोषदृष्टिरस्ति तत्र तस्य राग एव न भवेत् ।
Moreover, he who perceives faults in an object can have no attachment to it.
तस्मात्प्रवृत्तिरपि तस्य तदधीना न स्यादिति चेत्, तत्रेदं समाधानं - यस्यापथ्यस्य सेवनेनान्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां रोगाधिक्यं तत्र दोषनिश्चये सत्यपि यथा प्रारब्धवशाद्रोगिणो जानतोऽपि प्रवृत्तिर्जायते, प्रारब्धबलात् तथा ज्ञानिनोऽपि सर्वव्यवहारेषु प्रवृत्तिः सत्यामपि दोषदृष्टौ जायत एव ।1,2,3,1,2
If it is argued that 'therefore no activity dependent on that object could arise in him', here is the resolution: just as a sick person engages in unwholesome diet due to the force of prārabdha even when he knows through positive and negative concomitance that it aggravates disease and is certain of its harm, so too, by the force of prārabdha, activity in all worldly transactions does indeed arise for the jñānin, even though his perception of fault remains intact.
टिप्पणी
1.
सर्वस्वातन्त्र्येण भुवं पालयतो राज्ञो रोगकारणीभूतं प्रारब्धं कर्म प्रतिबन्धकत्वान्मन्द इत्युच्यते यथा तथाविद्यातत्कार्यभूतशत्रून् संहृत्य ब्रह्मीभूतस्य ज्ञानिनोऽधिकप्रवृत्तिहेतुभूतं प्रारब्धमेकाग्रताया विरोधित्वान्मन्दमित्युच्यते ।
Just as the prārabdha karma that causes illness in a king ruling the earth with absolute autonomy is called 'inferior' (manda) because it acts as an obstacle, so too, for a jñānin who has become Brahman by annihilating the enemies consisting of avidyā and its effects, the prārabdha causing extensive worldly activity is called 'inferior' because it opposes mental one-pointedness.
मन्दमित्यस्य पदस्य निकृष्टमित्यत्रार्थः ।
The meaning of the word 'manda' here is 'inferior/defective' (nikṛṣṭa).
2.
षष्ठे तरङ्ग उक्तम् ।
This was stated in the sixth chapter.
3.
अत्रायं विवेकः - मन्दं तीव्रं तीव्रतरमिति प्रारब्धं कर्म त्रिविधम् ।
Here is the distinction: prārabdha karma is of three kinds — mild, intense, and very intense.
इत्थं ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारे न नियमः अस्ति ।
Thus, there is no fixed rule regarding the empirical conduct of a knower of truth.
अयं च पक्षः सविस्तरं तृप्तिदीपे विद्यारण्यस्वामिभिः प्रतिपादितः ।
And this position has been expounded in detail by Svāmī Vidyāraṇya in the Tṛptidīpa chapter (of the Pañcadaśī).
तस्मात्तत्त्वदृष्टेर्ज्ञानिनो व्यवहारोऽनियत एव ।
Therefore, the conduct of the knower who has perceived reality is indeed unregulated.
अत एव समाधिरूपनियमविधिं श्रुत्वा तत्त्वदृष्टिः परिजहास ।
For this very reason, on hearing of an injunctive rule prescribing samādhi, the seer of reality laughed.
यस्योपादेयफलं भिक्षान्नवदधिकप्रयत्नलभ्यं भवति, यस्य चाकस्मिकहेयफलं निवर्तनीयरोगवदल्पप्रयत्नेन निवर्तते तत्प्रारब्धं मन्दप्रारब्धमित्युच्यते ।
That prārabdha whose desirable fruit is obtainable only with great effort (like food gained through begging) and whose sudden undesirable fruit is averted with little effort (like a curable disease) is called mild prārabdha (manda-prārabdha).
यस्योपादेयफलं मृष्टान्नवदल्पप्रयत्नलभ्यम् ।
(And) whose desirable fruit is obtainable with little effort like a delicious meal,
यस्य चाकस्मिकहेयफलं कष्टसाध्यफलवदधिकप्रयत्ननिवर्त्यं भवति तादृशं प्रारब्धं तीव्रप्रारब्धमित्युच्यते ।
and whose sudden undesirable fruit is removable only with great effort (like an affliction cured with difficulty) — such prārabdha is called intense prārabdha (tīvra-prārabdha).
यस्य चोपादेयफलं स्वस्थानोपनतान्नवत् विनैव प्रयत्नं स्वतः एव लभ्यते, यस्य बलात्कारलब्धहेयफलं महिषव्रणवदामरणं प्रयत्नतः अपि न निवर्तते ।
And whose desirable fruit is obtained spontaneously without any effort at all (like food delivered to one's door), and whose forcibly imposed undesirable fruit is not averted even with effort until death (like an incurable sore on a buffalo),
तत्प्रारब्धं तीव्रतरमित्युच्यते ।
that prārabdha is called very intense (tīvratara-prārabdha).
इत्थं मन्दतीव्रप्रारब्धयोः फलं प्रयत्नाधीनम् ।
In this manner, the fruit of mild and intense prārabdha is dependent on effort.
तत्प्रयत्नहेतुः शुभाशुभवासनाः ।
The cause of that effort is the auspicious and inauspicious latent impressions (vāsanās).
तद्वासनानिवृत्तिः पुरुषप्रयत्नसाध्या ।
The eradication of those latent impressions can be accomplished by human effort.
तत्रापि शुभवासनानिवृत्तिर्दुःसङ्गादिप्रयत्नाज्जायते ।
Even there, the eradication of auspicious impressions occurs through efforts such as keeping bad company.
अशुभवासनानिवृत्तिः सत्सङ्गविवेकज्ञानवैराग्यादिना जायते ।
The eradication of inauspicious impressions occurs through good company, discrimination, knowledge, dispassion, and the like.
यस्माज्ज्ञानी सत्सङ्गविवेकज्ञानवैराग्यादिसम्पन्नो भवति, तस्मात् तच्चित्तेऽशुभवासनाप्रवृत्तिहेतुभूता काप्यशुभवासना नैवास्ति ।
Because the knower is fully endowed with good company, discrimination, knowledge, dispassion, etc., there remains in his mind no inauspicious impression whatsoever that could cause sinful action.
किन्तु शुभप्रवृत्तिहेतुभूता शुभवासनैवास्ते ।
Rather, only auspicious impressions causing noble activity remain.
ततः तस्य ज्ञानिनो मन्दतीव्ररूपप्रारब्धफलभूतनिषिद्धाचरणे विधिनिषेधावगतगुणदोषबुद्ध्यभावात् शुभवासनात्मकस्वभाववशादुन्मत्तवैष्णववत् ब्राह्मणादिशिशुवच्च प्रवृत्तिरेव न सम्भवेत् ।
Hence, even in prohibited actions that might arise as the fruit of mild or intense prārabdha, because he has no notion of virtue or sin derived from injunctions and prohibitions, and by force of his innate disposition formed of noble impressions, no inclination toward prohibited action can ever occur in that knower, just as in an ecstatic devotee of Viṣṇu or an innocent brāhmaṇa child.
किन्तु निवृत्तिरेव स्यात् ।
Rather, there would only be abstention.
कस्यचिद्रोगिणोऽन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां दोषनिश्चये सत्यपि, अपथ्यसेवने या प्रवृत्तिर्जायते न सा प्रयत्नशीलस्यापि रोगिणो जायते ।
Even when a patient has ascertained through positive and negative experience that an unwholesome diet is harmful, the impulse to consume unwholesome food does not arise in a patient who exercises self-restraint and effort.
तथापि जिह्वाचापल्यवतः प्रयत्नहीनस्य रोगिणोऽपथ्यसेवने प्रवृत्तिर्जायते ।
Nevertheless, in a sick person who has a restless tongue and lacks effort, the inclination to consume unwholesome food does arise.
प्रयत्नशीलस्यापि कस्यचिदपथ्यकरणे प्रवृत्तिर्जायते ।
And in some rare cases, even in one making effort, an impulse to take unwholesome food arises.
तदेतत् तीव्रस्य प्रारब्धस्य फलम् ।
That is the fruit of intense prārabdha.
तदेवं दोषनिश्चयमिथ्यात्वनिश्चयरूपदृढविवेकवतो ज्ञानिनो मन्दस्य वा, तीव्रस्य वा, प्रारब्धकर्मणः फलभूता यथेष्टचेष्टारूपा निषिद्धप्रवृत्तिर्नैव सम्भवति ।
Thus, in the knower who has firm discrimination consisting in the certainty of defects and the certainty of the world's falsity, forbidden activity in the form of wanton conduct as the fruit of mild or intense prārabdha karma is never possible.
प्रारब्धभक्ता यदाक्षिपन्ति - प्रारब्धफलं विशिष्टं त्यक्तुं न शक्यते ।
As for what the fatalists (who idolize prārabdha) object: 'The specific fruit of prārabdha cannot be avoided;
अतो व्यर्थः पुरुषप्रयत्न इति ।
therefore human effort is futile' —
तन्न युज्यते ।
that is not proper.
तथाभ्युपगमे हि सर्वज्ञप्रणीतं वैद्यमन्त्रयोगशास्त्रादिकं सर्वं तन्निवृत्त्युपायप्रतिपादकं व्यर्थं स्यात् ।
For if that were admitted, all the scriptures composed by the omniscient sages — medicine, mantras, yoga, and so forth — which expound the means for averting such afflictions, would become totally useless.
दृष्टफलहेतुभूतोपायबोधकशास्त्रवैयर्थ्यकथनं च न विवेकिनां सङ्गच्छते ।
And asserting the futility of scriptures that teach practical means producing visible results is unacceptable to discriminating thinkers.
प्रारब्धं पूरुषप्रयत्नश्चेत्येतद्द्वयमत्यावश्यकमित्येव वासिष्ठाद्युत्तमग्रन्थानामभिप्रायः ।
'Both prārabdha and human effort are indispensable' — this alone is the settled purport of sublime texts such as the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha.
1.
अत्रायमभिप्रायः - स्वाधीने कार्ये नियमः सम्भवति ।
Here this is the purport: a fixed rule is possible only in an action that is under one's own control.
पराधीने तु कार्ये स न युज्यते ।
But in an action dependent on another, that rule does not apply.
ज्ञानिनां शरीरव्यवहारश्च नानाप्रारब्धकर्माधीनो वर्तते ।
And the bodily conduct of the knowers of truth is dependent upon various prārabdha-karmas.
तस्मात् हस्तमुक्तेषुतुल्यप्रारब्धाधीनो ज्ञानिदेहव्यवहारो न नियतः ।
Therefore, the bodily behavior of a knower, being dependent on prārabdha that is like an arrow discharged from the hand, is not uniform.
रागादिवासना निरुद्ध्य स्वाधीनचित्ताः केचन ज्ञानिनो मन्दस्य वा तीव्रस्य वा प्रारब्धकर्मणः फलभूतं शरीरव्यवहारं नियमयन्ति ।
Some knowers, having restrained latent impressions like attachment and holding their minds under control, regulate their bodily conduct resulting from mild or intense prārabdha-karma.
तीव्रतरप्रारब्धफलभूतं शरीरव्यवहारं नियन्तुं नैव प्रभवन्ति ।
However, they are not able to regulate the bodily conduct that is the fruition of exceedingly intense prārabdha.
2.
विनापि प्रीतिं ज्ञानिनः प्रारब्धभोगो जायते ।
The experiencing of prārabdha takes place for a knower even without any liking or attachment.
प्रारब्धं चेच्छानिच्छापरेच्छाभेदात् त्रिविधम् ।
And prārabdha is threefold due to the distinctions of *icchā* (desire), *anicchā* (absence of desire), and *parecchā* (prompted by another's desire).
तच्च श्रीविद्यारण्यकृते तृप्तिदीपे (१५३-१६२) पद्येषु सम्यगुपपादितम् ।
And that has been well expounded in verses (153–162) of the Tṛptidīpa authored by Śrī Vidyāraṇya.
489 · तत्त्वदृष्टेर्देशकालाद्यनपेक्षो देहपातः
इत्थं कञ्चित्कालं तत्र तत्र सञ्चारं कृत्वा सम्यग्ज्ञानवान् तत्त्वदृष्टिः प्रारब्धभोगं बुभुजे ।
In this way, having wandered here and there for some time, Tattvadṛṣṭi, possessing complete knowledge, exhausted his prārabdha experience.
ततस्तत्प्राणास्तत्रैव लिल्युः ।
Then his prāṇas dissolved right there.
प्रारब्धभोगानन्तरं ज्ञानिनां प्राणानां कुत्रापि गमनाभावात्, तत्त्वदृष्टेः प्राणोऽपि स्वोपादाने एव लीनोऽभूदिति उक्तं भवति ।
Because there is no departure anywhere for the prāṇas of knowers after the end of prārabdha experience, it is stated that Tattvadṛṣṭi's prāṇa dissolved right into its own material cause.
ज्ञानिनां शरीरत्यागार्थं न कालविशेषादिनियमापेक्षास्ति ।
For knowers, there is no requirement of any specific rule regarding time etc. for giving up the body.
उत्तरायणे अथवा दक्षिणायने तेषां शरीरपातः सम्भवेत् ।
The fall of their body may occur in the northern solstice or in the southern solstice;
सर्वथाप्यसौ मुक्त एव ।
in every circumstance he is indeed liberated.
तथा, देशविशेषनियमापेक्षापि नास्ति ।
Likewise, there is no requirement of rules regarding a specific place either.
काश्यादिपुण्यदेशेषु वा, अत्यन्तमलिनदेशेषु वा ज्ञानिनां देहपातः सम्भवेत् ।
The knower's body may fall either in sacred places like Kāśī or in extremely unclean places;
सर्वथाप्यसौ मुक्त एव ।
in every circumstance he is indeed liberated.
तथा, आसनविशेषनियमापेक्षापि नास्ति ।
Likewise, there is no requirement of rules regarding a specific posture either.
भूमौ वा शवासने वा सिद्धासने वा स्थित्वा देहपातः सम्भवेत् ।
The fall of the body may occur lying on the ground, in śavāsana, or seated in siddhāsana;
सर्वथाप्यसौ मुक्त एव ।
in every circumstance he is indeed liberated.
तथैव, सावधानमना ब्रह्मध्यानेन रोगादिना व्याकुलान्तःकरणो हाहेति विलपनेन वा देहं त्यजेत् ।
Just so, he may abandon the body either with an attentive mind through meditation on Brahman, or with an agitated mind lamenting 'Alas, alas!' due to illness etc.;
सर्वथाप्यसौ मुक्त एव ।
in every circumstance he is indeed liberated.
यदैव ज्ञानिनो ज्ञानेनाज्ञानं निवर्तते, तदैव स ज्ञानी मुक्तो भवति ।
The very moment ignorance is dispelled by knowledge for the knower, at that very moment that knower becomes liberated.
एवं ज्ञानिनो विदेहमुक्तौ न देशकालासनादिनियमापेक्षास्ति ।
Thus, for a knower's videhamukti, there is no requirement of any rules regarding place, time, posture, and so forth.
यथैव ज्ञानिनो देहपाते देशकालाद्यपेक्षा नास्ति, तथैव ज्ञानोत्पत्तिसाधने श्रवणादावपि देशकालाद्यपेक्षा नास्त्येव ।
Just as there is no dependence on place, time, etc., in the knower's body-falling, exactly so there is no dependence on place, time, etc., even in the means for the rise of knowledge, such as śravaṇa.
उपासकस्य तु देशकालाद्यपेक्षा स्यादेव ।
For a practitioner of upāsanā, however, dependence on place, time, etc., certainly exists.
490 · अत्राक्षेपसमाधाने
भीष्मादयो ज्ञानिनः स्मर्यन्ते ।
Bhīṣma and others are remembered in traditional lore as knowers of Brahman.
तत्र भीष्मस्तूत्तरायणं विना कुतः प्राणा1,2न्न
There, why did Bhīṣma not give up his life-breaths without the northern solstice (Uttarāyaṇa)?
टिप्पणी
1.
अत्रायं साम्प्रदायिकः श्लोकः— काश्यां वा ज्ञानिनो देहश्चण्डालस्य गृहेऽपि वा । ज्ञानक्षणे भ्रान्तिहानेर्ज्ञानी मुक्तो हि सर्वथा ॥ इति ।
Here is this traditional verse: 'Whether the body of a knower falls in Kāśī or in the house of an outcaste, the knower is completely liberated indeed at the very moment of knowledge owing to the eradication of delusion.'
2.
अयमेवार्थः पञ्चदश्यां श्रीविद्यारण्यकृतौ भूतविवेके उक्तः— नीरोग उपविष्टो वा रुग्णो वा विलुठन् भुवि । मूर्च्छितो वा त्यजत्वेष प्राणान् भ्रान्तिर्न सर्वथा ॥ १०६॥ दिने दिने स्वप्नसुप्त्योरधीते विस्मृतेऽप्ययम् । परेद्युर्नानधीतः स्यात् तद्वद्विद्या न नश्यति ॥ १०७॥ प्रमाणोत्पादिता विद्या प्रमाणं प्रबलं विना । न नश्यति न वेदान्तात् प्रबलं मानमीक्ष्यते ॥ १०८॥ इति ।
This very point is stated in the Pañcadaśī of Śrī Vidyāraṇya: 'Whether healthy and sitting upright, or sick and rolling on the earth, or unconscious—let him cast off life-breaths; delusion never returns. Day after day, even if what was studied is forgotten during dream and deep sleep, a man does not on the morrow become unstudied; likewise, knowledge is not destroyed. Knowledge generated by a valid means of knowledge (pramāṇa) is not destroyed without a stronger pramāṇa; and no pramāṇa stronger than Vedānta is seen.'
जहौ इति चेत् ।
If you ask, '(Why did he wait and then) give up his life?'
श‍ृणु ।
Listen.
भीष्मादयो ह्याधिकारिकाः पुरुषाः ।
For Bhīṣma and others were persons holding special cosmic offices (*ādhikārika-puruṣas*).
ते च उपासकानामुपदेशार्थमेव देशकालविशेषप्रतीक्षां चक्रुः ।
And they awaited a particular time and place solely to instruct meditators (*upāsakas*).
वसिष्ठभीष्मादीनामाधिकारिकपुरुषत्वात्तेषामनेकानि जन्मानि अभवन् ।
Because Vasiṣṭha, Bhīṣma, and others were *ādhikārika-puruṣas*, they had multiple births.
आधिकारिकपुरुषाणामेककल्पपर्यन्तं प्रारब्धमवतिष्ठते ।
The *prārabdha* of *ādhikārika-puruṣas* endures until the completion of an entire *kalpa*.
अन्तरेण कल्पावासानं न तेषां विदेहमोक्षो भवति ।
Without the conclusion of the *kalpa*, their disembodied liberation (*videha-mokṣa*) does not occur.
कल्पान्तरालकाल एव तेषामनेकानि जन्मानीच्छावशाज्जायन्ते ।
Within the span of that *kalpa*, multiple births occur for them by virtue of their will.
तथापि आत्मस्वरूपे जन्ममरणादिवत्त्वभ्रान्तिर्न तेषां सम्भवति ।
Even so, the delusion of attributing birth, death, etc., to the true nature of the *ātman* is impossible for them.
तस्माज्जीवन्मुक्ता एव ते ।
Therefore, they are indeed *jīvanmuktas*.
तेषां व्यवहारः सर्वोऽपि परोपदेशनिमित्त एव ।
All their empirical activity is solely for the sake of instructing others.
ज्ञानिनां व्यवहारे नान्यः कोऽपि नियमोऽस्ति ।
There is no other restrictive rule whatsoever regarding the conduct of knowers.
अनेनैवाभिप्रायेण तत्त्वदृष्टेर्देहपाते देशकालासनादीनामन्यतमदपि नोक्तम् ।
With this very intention, not even one among place, time, posture, etc., was stipulated at the time of bodily demise for Tattvadṛṣṭi.
491 · अदृष्टेर्देशकालाद्यपेक्षो देहपातः
द्वितीयः शिष्यस्त्वदृष्टिर्गङ्गातीरे एव शुभस्थाने एकान्ते सुपवित्रे च देशे ब्रह्मध्यानेन त्यक्त्वा स्वं देहं प्रागुक्तेनोत्तरायणमार्गेण ब्रह्मलोकं गत्वा क्रमेण ब्रह्मीभूय निरतिशयमानन्दमवाप ।
The second disciple, Adṛṣṭi, however, gave up his body right on the bank of the Gaṅgā in an auspicious, solitary, and supremely sacred spot through meditation on Brahman; going to Brahmaloka via the previously described path of the northern solstice, he gradually became Brahman and attained unsurpassable bliss.
उत्तमेषु देशेषु, उत्तरायणादिषूत्तमेषु कालेषु वा यदा शरीरमुपासकः परित्यजति, तदैव उपासना फलिष्यति ।
Only when the meditator (*upāsaka*) casts off the body in excellent places or at auspicious times such as Uttarāyaṇa, will the *upāsanā* bear fruit.
यद्यपि ज्ञानिनो मरणसमये ज्ञेयस्मृतिमत्त्वाद्यपेक्षा नास्ति ।
Although for the knower there is no requirement of having remembrance of the object of knowledge (*jñeya*) at the time of death;
तथापि उपासकस्य तदा ध्येयादिस्वरूपस्मरणापेक्षा वर्तते ।
Yet for the meditator (*upāsaka*), the requirement of remembering the nature of the object of meditation (*dhyeya*) at that time indeed exists.
(१) यो यादृशध्येयविषयकं ध्यानं पूर्वमसकृदकरोदुपासकः तस्य तादृशध्येयविषयकस्मृतावन्ततः सत्यामेव उपासनाफलं सिद्ध्यति ।
(1) The fruit of meditation is attained only when the meditator, who previously practiced repeatedly meditation focused on a particular object of meditation, has at the end the corresponding remembrance of that object.
(२) यथोपासकस्यान्तकाले ध्येयस्मृतिरपेक्ष्यते, तथा ध्येयब्रह्मप्राप्तये पञ्चमतरङ्गोक्तमार्गचिन्तनमप्यपेक्ष्यते ।
(2) Just as the remembrance of the meditated deity is required for the meditator at the end of life, so too contemplation of the path described in the Fifth Wave is required for attaining the meditated Brahman.
मार्गचिन्तनस्याप्युपासनाङ्गत्वात् ।
Because contemplation of the path is also an auxiliary limb of meditation.
ज्ञानार्थे श्रवणादौ देशकालासनाद्यपेक्षा नास्ति ।
For the purpose of knowledge, in *śravaṇa* and the rest, there is no dependence on place, time, posture, etc.
ध्याने तु उत्तमदेशनिरन्तरकालसिद्धाद्यासनप्रभृतीनामपेक्षा वर्तत एव ।
In meditation (*dhyāna*), however, the requirement of an auspicious place, uninterrupted time, postures such as Siddhāsana, etc., certainly exists.
तस्मादेवादृष्टेरुत्तमदेशभूतगङ्गातीरस्थितिः, तत्रैवैकान्ते निरन्तरब्रह्मध्यानं देहत्यागश्च कथितः ।
For this very reason, Adṛṣṭi's residence on the Gaṅgā's bank (an excellent place), his uninterrupted meditation on Brahman in solitude right there, and his casting off the body were recounted.
तर्कदृष्टेर्निश्चयः॥ ४९२–५०२ ॥
492 · अष्टादश विद्यास्थानानि सर्वाण्यपि च शास्त्राणि ब्रह्मज्ञानहेतुभूतानि
तृतीयशिष्यस्तु तर्कदृष्टिर्गुरुमुखादुपदेशं प्राप्य स्वावगतविषये शास्त्रान्तरविरोधपरिहाराय निखिलशास्त्राभिप्रायं विचार्य इत्थं निश्चिकाय ।
However, the third disciple, Tarkadṛṣṭi, having received the teaching directly from the mouth of the Guru, reflected upon the true intention of all scriptures in order to dispel apparent contradictions with other texts regarding the truth he had realised, and concluded thus.
(१) सकलशास्त्राणां परमं प्रयोजनं मोक्ष एव ।
(1) The ultimate goal of all scriptures is *mokṣa* alone.
(२) मोक्षसाधनं च ज्ञानमेकमेव ।
(2) And the only means to *mokṣa* is knowledge alone.
(३) तच्च ज्ञानमद्वयात्मतत्त्वनिश्चयरूपम् ।
(3) And that knowledge is of the nature of firm ascertainment of the non-dual reality of the *ātman*.
(४) भेदनिश्चयस्तु न यथार्थज्ञानम् ।
(4) Conviction in difference, however, is not valid knowledge.
(५) शास्त्राण्यपि निखिलानि साक्षात्, परम्परया वा ब्रह्मज्ञानहेतुभूतानि ।
(5) All scriptures as well serve as the cause of the knowledge of Brahman, either directly or indirectly.
संस्कृता वैखरी वाणी अष्टादशप्रस्थानरूपा वर्तते ।
Refined audible speech (*vaikharī vāṇī*) manifests in the form of eighteen distinct canonical disciplines (*prasthānas*).
तत्र- (१) कानिचिच्छास्त्राणि कर्मप्रतिपादकानि ।
Among these: (1) Some scriptures expound ritual action (*karma*).
(२) कानिचिद्विषयसुखोपायप्रतिपादकानि ।
(2) Some expound the means for attaining sense pleasures.
(३) कानिचिद्ब्रह्मान्यदेवतोपासनाबोधकानि ।
(3) Some teach meditation (*upāsanā*) on deities other than Brahman.
(४) कानिचिज्ज्ञानहेतुभूतानि ।
(4) Some serve as the causes for knowledge.
तत्रापि न्यायसाङ्ख्यादिशास्त्राणि भेदज्ञानमेव यथार्थं कथयन्ति ।
Even among them, systems like Nyāya and Sāṅkhya state that the knowledge of difference alone is valid.
तदेवं सर्वेषां शास्त्राणां यद्यप्यद्वैतब्रह्मबोधकत्वं न समभवति ।
Thus, although it appears that all scriptures do not directly reveal non-dual Brahman;
तथापि, सकलशास्त्रप्रणेतारः सर्वज्ञाः कृपालवश्च ।
Nevertheless, the original authors of all scriptures were omniscient and compassionate.
तत्कृतमूलसूत्राणामर्थोऽपि वेदानुसार्येव ।
The real meaning of the original sūtras authored by them is indeed completely consistent with the Vedas.
परन्तु तद्व्याख्यातारो भ्रान्त्या मूलसूत्रकाराभिप्रायविरुद्धानेवार्थान् कल्पयन्ति ।
However, subsequent commentators, through delusion, conceive meanings that are contrary to the true intention of the original authors of the sūtras.
सूत्राणामर्थस्तु वेदविरोधी न भवति ।
The true meaning of the sūtras is not opposed to the Veda.
वेदानुसार्येव भवति ।
It is always in complete alignment with the Veda.
तर्कदृष्टिरत्युत्तमसंस्कारवशादित्थं निश्चयं चकार ।
Owing to the force of exceptionally noble latent impressions (*saṃskāras*), Tarkadṛṣṭi reached this firm conclusion.
493 · अष्टादश विद्यायाः प्रस्थानानि
वेदाश्चत्वारः ।
The Vedas are four.
उपवेदाश्चत्वारः ।
The subsidiary Vedas (*upavedas*) are four.
वेदाङ्गानि षट् ।
The Vedic auxiliaries (*vedāṅgas*) are six.
पुराणन्यायमीमांसाधर्मशास्त्राणि चत्वारि चेत्येवं वैखरी वाणी संस्कृतभाषारूपा अष्टादशभेदा भवति ।
And the four branches consisting of Purāṇa, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, and Dharmaśāstra — thus, audible speech (*vaikharī vāṇī*) in the form of the Sanskrit language possesses eighteen divisions.
अष्टादश प्रस्थानानि इति त एव भेदा उच्यन्ते ।
These very divisions are designated as the eighteen canonical disciplines (*aṣṭādaśa-prasthānāni*).
टिप्पणी
1.
परा, पश्यन्ती, मध्यमा, वैखरी चेति चतस्रो वाचः ।
Speech has four levels: *parā*, *paśyantī*, *madhyamā*, and *vaikharī*.
तत्र वैखरी परश्रवणयोग्याकारादिवर्णात्मनाभिव्यक्तीभवति ।
Among these, *vaikharī* manifests itself as articulate letters beginning with 'a' that are audible to others.
2.
विद्याङ्गानि प्रस्थानानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
The branches of knowledge are known as *prasthānas*.
इत्थमग्निपुराणारम्भे प्रतिपादितम् ।
This is expounded at the very commencement of the Agni Purāṇa.
तथा मधुसूदनसरस्वतीस्वामिकृतप्रस्थानभेदग्रन्थे च ।
And likewise in the treatise *Prasthānabheda* composed by Svāmī Madhusūdana Sarasvatī.
494 · चतुर्णामपि वेदानां ब्रह्मज्ञान एव तात्पर्यम्
ऋग्वेदः, यजुर्वेदः, सामवेदः, अथर्ववेद इति वेदाश्चत्वारः ।
The Vedas are four, namely: Ṛgveda, Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, and Atharvaveda.
तत्र- (१) कानिचिद्वाक्यानि ज्ञेयब्रह्मबोधकानि ।
Among them: (1) some sentences reveal the knowable Brahman (nirguṇa-Brahman).
(२) कानिचिद्ध्येयब्रह्मबोधकानि ।
(2) Some reveal the meditatable Brahman (saguṇa-Brahman).
(३) इतराणि तु कर्मबोधकानि ।
(3) While the remaining ones reveal ritual actions (karma).
कर्मावबोधकवेदवचनानामप्यन्तःकरणशुद्धिद्वारा ज्ञानमेव प्रयोजनं भवति ।
Even of the Vedic statements teaching rituals, the ultimate purpose is knowledge alone, by means of purifying the mind.
कस्यापि वेदवचनस्य न प्रवृत्तावभिप्रायः ।
The real intention of no Vedic statement whatsoever is to impel one into worldly activity.
किन्तु स्वाभाविकनिषिद्धकर्मप्रवृत्तेर्निरोध एवाभिप्रायः ।
Rather, the intention is only to restrain natural inclinations toward prohibited actions.
तस्मादभिचारादिकर्मप्रतिपादकाथर्ववेदस्यापि निवृत्तावेव तात्पर्यम् ।
Therefore, even the Atharvaveda, which expounds malevolent rites (abhicāra) and the like, has its essential purport in cessation alone.
शत्रुः संहर्तव्य इति द्वेषवशाद्यो गरदाने वा, अग्निदाहे वा प्रवर्तते तं शत्रुमारणप्रवृत्तेर्व्यावर्तयितुमभिचारकर्मरूपाः श्येनयागादयः कथिताः ।
To turn a person away from murdering his enemy who, under the sway of hatred thinking 'my enemy must be killed', is about to administer poison or set fire, malevolent rites such as the Śyena sacrifice are prescribed.
शत्रुसंहारे निमित्तभूतं कर्माभिचार इत्युच्यते ।
The ritual act that becomes the instrumental cause in destroying an enemy is called *abhicāra* (malevolent rite).
ईदृशं कर्म श्येनयाग इत्युच्यते ।
Such a rite is called the Śyena sacrifice.
श्येनयागकर्तव्यताबोधकवेदवचनानामपि शत्रुवधकामः श्येनेनाभिचरन् यजेत इत्यादीनां श्येनयागप्रवृत्तौ न तात्पर्यम् ।
Even of the Vedic sentences prescribing the duty of the Śyena sacrifice, such as One desiring the destruction of an enemy should perform sorcery by means of the Śyena sacrifice, the purport is not to impel one to perform the Śyena sacrifice.
किन्तु शत्रुमारणकामस्य श्येनयागादिविलक्षणविषदानादिशत्रुमारणोपायान्तरनिवृत्तावेव तात्पर्यम् ।
Rather, the true purport is only to turn a person desirous of killing his enemy away from other means of murder such as administering poison, which are distinct from the Śyena sacrifice.
प्रवृत्तेर्द्वेषत एव प्राप्तत्वात् ।1
Because the inclination to act is already obtained naturally from hatred itself (and hence does not need a Vedic injunction).
टिप्पणी
1.
ऋग्वेदे (२१) शाखाः ।
In the Ṛgveda, there are 21 branches.
यजुर्वेदे (१०९) शाखाः ।
In the Yajurveda, there are 109 branches.
सामवेदे (१०००) शाखाः ।
In the Sāmaveda, there are 1,000 branches.
अथर्ववेदे (५०) शाखाः ।
In the Atharvaveda, there are 50 branches.
यथा कश्चन वृक्षस्वामी यजमानः स्वपुत्रेभ्यस्तच्छाखा विभज्य दद्यात् तथा भगवान् श्रीवेदव्यासोऽपि वेदं चतुर्धा विभज्य पुनस्तत्र काश्चन शाखाः कल्पयित्वा, प्रतिशाखं विधिभेदांश्च कल्पयामास ।
Just as a tree-owner patron divides the branches of his tree and gives them to his sons, so Lord Śrī Vedavyāsa divided the Veda fourfold, arranged various recensions (śākhās) within them, and fashioned distinctive rules for each branch.
यावत्यः शाखास्तावत्य उपनिषदः इति मुक्तिकोपनिषदि महावाक्यरत्नावल्यां च कथ्यते ।
It is stated in the *Muktikopaniṣad* and the *Mahāvākyaratnāvalī*: As many branches as there are, so many are the Upaniṣads.
अशीत्युत्तरशताधिकसहस्रसङ्ख्याकाः (११८०) शाखाः ।
The branches are 1,180 in number.
तस्मादुपनिषदोऽपि तावत्सङ्ख्याका (११८०) एव भवन्ति ।
Therefore, the Upaniṣads are also precisely 1,180 in number.
तत्र (८४०) शाखाः कर्मप्रतिपादकत्वात् कर्मकाण्डा उच्यन्ते ।
Among these, 840 branches are called *karma-kāṇḍa* because they propound action.

232 branches are called *upāsanā-kāṇḍa* because they teach the meditatable Brahman.
(१०८) शाखा ज्ञेयब्रह्मबोधकत्वात्, वेदस्यान्त्यभागत्वात्, वेदसारार्थबोधकत्वाच्च वेदान्ताः, ज्ञानकाण्डा उपनिषद इति चोच्यन्ते ।
108 branches, because they reveal the knowable Brahman, form the end-portion of the Vedas, and reveal the essential message of the Veda, are called Vedāntas, *jñāna-kāṇḍas*, and Upaniṣads.
तत्रापि (अष्टोत्तरशतोपनिषत्स्वपि) ईशकेनकठप्रश्नमुण्डमाण्डूक्यतित्तिरिः । ऐतरेयश्च छान्दोग्यं बृहदारण्यकं दश ॥ इति दशोपनिषदो मुख्याः ।
Even among those 108 Upaniṣads, ten are principal: Īśa, Kena, Kaṭha, Praśna, Muṇḍaka, Māṇḍūkya, Taittirīya, Aitareya, Chāndogya, and Bṛhadāraṇyaka—these ten.
तत्र ऐतरेयोपनिषदृग्वेदगता ।
Among them, the Aitareya Upaniṣad belongs to the Ṛgveda.
ईशबृहदारण्यके शुक्लयजुर्वेदगते ।
Īśa and Bṛhadāraṇyaka belong to the Śukla-Yajurveda.

Kaṭhavallī and Taittirīya belong to the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda.

Kena and Chāndogya belong to the Sāmaveda.
प्रश्नमुण्डकमाण्डूक्योपनिषदोऽथर्ववेदगता इति विभागः ।
Praśna, Muṇḍaka, and Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣads belong to the Atharvaveda—such is the division.
योऽन्यतः प्राप्तोऽर्थः न तत्र वाक्यस्याभिप्रायः ।
Whatever matter is already obtained from other sources (such as instinct or natural passions), the Vedic sentence does not intend to enjoin that.
इत्थमथर्ववेदसामान्यं निवृत्तावेव तात्पर्यवत् ।
Thus, the general body of the Atharvaveda has its true purport in cessation alone.

That the sentences teaching rituals in the other three Vedas serve as an expedient to knowledge via mind-purification is exceedingly clear.

उपवेदानाम् अपि चतुर्णां क्रमात् ब्रह्मज्ञाने एव तात्पर्यम् - (१) आयुर्वेदः, (२) धनुर्वेदः, (३) गान्धर्ववेदः, (४) अर्थवेदः, इति उपवेदाः चत्वारः ।
The true purport of even the four Upavedas is, in due sequence, directed only toward the knowledge of Brahman: (1) Āyurveda, (2) Dhanurveda, (3) Gāndharvaveda, and (4) Arthaveda — these are the four Upavedas.
तत्र - (१) आयुर्वेदः - आयुर्वेदस्य कर्तारः ब्रह्मा, प्रजापतिः, अश्विनीकुमारौ, धन्वन्तरि-आदयः च ।
Among them: (1) Āyurveda — the authors and propagators of Āyurveda are Brahmā, Prajāpati, the two Aśvinīkumāras, Dhanvantari, and others.

Its systematic treatises and the medical texts of Caraka, Vāgbhaṭa, and others are indeed forms of Āyurveda itself.
वात्स्यायन-कृत-कामशास्त्रम् अपि आयुर्वेद-अन्तर्गतम् एव ।
The Kāmaśāstra composed by Vātsyāyana is also included within Āyurveda itself.

For the subject matter of Kāmaśāstra, such as aphrodisiac treatments (vājīkaraṇa) and retention therapies (stambhana), has also been expounded by Caraka and others.

Even of Āyurveda, the ultimate purport lies in establishing dispassion (vairāgya) alone.
आयुर्वेदरीत्या रोगादिनिवृत्तौ अपि पुनः रोगादिसम्भवात् ।
Because even after disease and suffering are alleviated through the methods of Āyurveda, they recur again.
तस्मात् लौकिकोपायाः सर्वे अपि तुच्छाः एव ।
Therefore, all empirical worldly remedies are ultimately hollow and insufficient.
तस्मात् औषधदानादिजनितपुण्याविर्भूतान्तःकरणशुद्धिद्वारा ब्रह्मज्ञाने एव आयुर्वेदस्य उपयोगः ।
Therefore, the true utility of Āyurveda is toward the knowledge of Brahman alone, by way of the purification of the mind brought about through the spiritual merit produced by giving medicines and selfless healing.
(२) धनुर्वेदः - विश्वामित्रकृते धनुर्वेदे आयुधं निरूपितम् ।
(2) Dhanurveda — in the Dhanurveda composed by Viśvāmitra, weaponry is expounded.

That (weaponry) is of four kinds: (1) discharged (mukta, e.g. arrows), (2) retained in hand (amukta, e.g. swords), (3) both discharged and retained (muktāmukta, e.g. spears), and (4) mechanically propelled (yantramukta).

परिणीताम् उपगच्छेत्, ऋतौ भार्याम् उपेयात्, हुतशेषं भक्षयेत्, सौत्रामण्यां सुराग्रहं गृह्णाति इत्यादिविधिवाक्यानां रागतः स्वतः प्राप्ते सर्वस्त्रीसङ्गे, सदा भार्यासङ्गमे, सदा मधुमांसादिभक्षणे वा प्रवर्तने नैव तात्पर्यम् ।
The true purport of injunctive statements such as 'One should approach a married wife', 'One should approach one's wife in her fertile period', 'One should eat the remnant of offerings', and 'He takes the wine cup in the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice' is certainly not to prompt union with any woman, constant union with one's wife, or constant consumption of honey, meat, etc., which are already naturally obtained through passionate impulse.
किन्तु स्वभावसिद्धसर्वतोमुखस्वेच्छाप्रवृत्तिसङ्कोचद्वारा निवृत्तौ एव परमतात्पर्यम् ।
Rather, their ultimate purport lies only in cessation, through the restriction of natural, unrestrained, self-willed impulses.
तस्मात् तादृशवेदवाक्यानि परिसङ्ख्याविधिस्वरूपाणि भवन्ति, न तु अपूर्वविधिरूपाणि ।
Therefore, such Vedic statements are in the nature of exclusionary injunctions (*parisaṅkhyā-vidhi*), not original injunctions (*apūrva-vidhi*).
न वा नियमविधिरूपाणि ।
Nor are they restrictive injunctions (*niyama-vidhi*).
श्येनयागबोधकाथर्ववेदवचनानाम् अपि द्वेषतः प्राप्तशत्रुमारणप्रवर्तने न तात्पर्यम् ।
Even the statements of the Atharvaveda prescribing the Śyena sacrifice do not have as their purport the instigation to kill an enemy, which is already prompted by hatred.
किन्तु तादृशस्वभावसिद्धप्रवृत्तिनिरोधनद्वारा तादृशविषदानादिक्रूरकर्मनिवर्तने एव तात्पर्यम् ।
Rather, the intent lies solely in restraining from such cruel deeds as administering poison, by checking such natural impulses.
तस्मात् श्येनयागबोधकवचनम् अपि परिसङ्ख्यात्मकम् एव इति कथ्यते ।
Therefore, even the injunction enjoining the Śyena sacrifice is said to be purely exclusionary (*parisaṅkhyā*).
तथा च भागवते— लोके व्यवायामिषमद्यसेवा नित्यास्तु जन्तोर्न हि तत्र चोदना । व्यवस्थितिस्तासु विवाहयज्ञसुराग्रहैरासु निवृत्तिरिष्टा ॥ (भा. पु. ११.५.११) इति ।
And so it is said in the Bhāgavatam: 'In this world, indulgence in sex, meat, and wine is natural for beings; there is no scriptural injunction for them. Their regulation is made through marriage, sacrifice, and the sacrificial wine-offerings; complete withdrawal from them is what is truly intended' (Bhā. Pu. 11.5.11).

A Vedic injunction that teaches the restriction of inclinations naturally obtained through attachment or aversion is called an exclusionary injunction (*parisaṅkhyā*).
चक्रादयो हस्तेन मुच्यमानत्वात् मुक्ता इत्युच्यन्ते ।

खड्गादयोऽमुक्ता इति ।
(2) Swords and the like are called 'amukta' (held/non-discharged).
परश्वादयो मुक्तामुक्ता इति ।
(3) Battle-axes and the like are called 'muktāmukta' (both discharged and held).
शरगोलकादयो यन्त्रमुक्ता इति ।
(4) Arrows, bullets, and the like are called 'yantramukta' (discharged from a mechanical device/bow).

(1) A weapon that is discharged is called an *astra*.
अमुक्तं शस्त्रम् इति ।
(2) A weapon that is held is called a *śastra*.

For all these four classes of weapons, presiding deities such as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Paśupati, Prajāpati, Agni, and Varuṇa, as well as their respective mantras, are stated.

And they are of four kinds: (1) foot-soldier, (2) charioteer, (3) cavalryman, and (4) elephant-rider.

Omens and auspicious observances in battle are also stated.

(1) Such subject matter is explained in the first section of the Dhanurveda.
आचार्यलक्षणम्, ततः शस्त्राभ्यासक्रमादिकं च द्वितीयपादे ।

For Dhanurveda teaches the duty of a Kṣatriya, which consists in protecting the subjects against evil-doers and thieves.

(3) Gāndharvaveda: And this became famous in the world through the sage Bharata.

Therein, singing, dancing, instrumental music, etc., along with musical notes, rhythm, modulations, and so forth, are expounded in detail.

चतुर्णामपि वेदानां षडङ्गानि स्युः ।
There are six auxiliary limbs (aṅgas) of all four Vedas.
(१) शिक्षा, (२) कल्पः, (३) व्याकरणम्, (४) निरुक्तम्, (५) ज्यौतिषम्, (६) छन्दः (पिङ्गलशास्त्रादि) चेति षट् वेदार्थज्ञानोपयोगित्वाद्वेदाङ्गानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
These six — (1) Śikṣā (phonetics), (2) Kalpa (ritual procedure), (3) Vyākaraṇa (grammar), (4) Nirukta (etymology), (5) Jyautiṣa (astronomy), and (6) Chandas (prosody, e.g. the Piṅgala-śāstra) — are called Vedāṅgas (limbs of the Veda) because they are useful for understanding the meaning of the Vedas.
तत्र- (१) शिक्षा - शिक्षायाः कर्तारः पाणिनिप्रभृतयोऽनेके महर्षयः ।
Among them, (1) Śikṣā: The authors of Śikṣā treatises are many great sages such as Pāṇini and others.

Knowledge of the points of articulation of letters in Vedic words, knowledge of the accents such as udātta, anudātta, and svarita, and so forth arise through Śikṣā.
वेदव्याख्यानरूपा अनेके प्रातिशाख्यनामका ये ग्रन्थास्तेऽप्यत्रैव शिक्षायामन्तर्भवन्ति ।
The many texts named Prātiśākhyas, which serve as commentaries on Vedic phonetics, are also included right here under Śikṣā.
(२) कल्पसूत्रं - कल्पसूत्रैर्वेदबोधितकर्मणामनुष्ठानरीतिरुपदिश्यते ।
(2) Kalpasūtra: Through the Kalpasūtras, the method of executing the rites enjoined by the Veda is taught.
यज्ञकर्मनिर्वर्तका ब्राह्मणा ऋत्विज उच्यन्ते ।
The brāhmaṇas who perform the sacrificial rites are called ṛtviks (priests).
तेषां पृथक् पृथक् कर्तव्यकर्मक्रमावबोधकं कल्पसूत्रम् ।
The Kalpasūtra makes known the distinct sequential duties to be performed by each of them.
कल्पसूत्रकर्तारस्तु कात्यायनाश्वलायनादयो मुनयः ।
The authors of the Kalpasūtras are sages such as Kātyāyana, Āśvalāyana, and others.
कल्पसूत्रं अपि वेदार्थज्ञानोपयोगित्वाद्वेदाङ्गमेव ।
The Kalpasūtra is also indeed a Vedāṅga because of its utility in understanding the Vedic meaning.
(३) व्याकरणं - व्याकरणेनापि वेदशब्दानां शुद्धताज्ञानं जायते ।
(3) Vyākaraṇa: Through grammar also, the knowledge of the linguistic correctness of Vedic words is attained.
तच्च व्याकरणं सूत्ररूपमष्टाध्याय्यात्मकं पाणिनिमुनिना विरचितम् ।
And that grammar, in aphoristic form comprising the eight chapters (Aṣṭādhyāyī), was composed by sage Pāṇini.

तद्व्याख्यानोपव्याख्यानान्यत्र कानिचित् लिख्यन्ते ।
Some of the commentaries and sub-commentaries thereon are listed here:
कर्तृनाम मूलं व्याख्यानं श्रीशङ्करः पद्मपादाचार्यः श्रीशङ्करः श्रीप्रकाशात्मचरणः अखण्डानन्दभिक्षुः विद्यारण्यः नृसिंहाश्रमी वाचस्पतिमिश्रः अमलानन्दः अप्पय्यदीक्षितः अद्वैतानन्दः आनन्दगिरिः रामानन्दः सर्वज्ञात्ममुनिः मधुसूदनस्वामी रामाश्रमी नारायणसरस्वती बालकृष्णानन्दः मधुसूदनस्वामी रामाश्रमी नारायणभट्टः अप्पय्यदीक्षितः शङ्करानन्दः भैरवदत्तपण्डितः रामानन्दस्वामी गङ्गाधरेन्द्रसरस्वती विद्यारण्यः रघुनाथशास्त्री रघुनाथशास्त्री रघुनाधशास्त्री अनूयनारायणः ब्रह्मसूत्रं शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं पञ्चपादिका विविरणं विवरणं पञ्चपादिका शारीरकभाष्यं भामती कल्पतरुः शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं सङ्क्षेपशारीरकं शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं शारीरकभाष्यं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं शारीरकभाष्यं विजयाभिदण्डिनी पञ्चपादिका विवरणं तत्त्वदीपनं विवरणप्रमेयसङ्ग्रहः टीका भामती कल्पतरुः परिमलं ब्रह्मविद्याभरणं न्यायनिर्णयः रत्नप्रभा सङ्क्षेपशारीरकं सङ्क्षेपशारीरकसारसङ्ग्रहः टीका वार्तिकं वार्तिकं वेदान्तकल्पलतिका वृत्तिः वृत्तिः न्यायरक्षामणिः न्यायरक्षामणिः तात्पर्यं ब्रह्मामृतवर्षिणी स्वाराज्यसिद्धिः अधिकरणरत्नमाला शाङ्करपादभूषणं अद्वैतवृत्तिः दिग्दर्शिनी समञ्जसा

500 · स्मृत्यादिग्रन्थानां कर्तारः प्रयोजं च
मनुः, याज्ञवल्क्यः, विष्णुः, यमः, अङ्गिराः, वसिष्ठः, दक्षः, संवर्तः, शातातपः, पराशरः, गौतमः, शङ्खलिखितः, हारीतः, आपस्तम्बः, शुक्रः, बृहस्पतिः, व्यासः, कात्यायनः, देवलः, नारदः एवम्-आदिभिः सर्वज्ञैः वेदानुसारिणः स्मृतिनामकाः ग्रन्थाः रचिताः ।
Works following the Vedas, called Smṛtis, were composed by omniscient sages such as Manu, Yājñavalkya, Viṣṇu, Yama, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, Dakṣa, Saṃvarta, Śātātapa, Parāśara, Gautama, Śaṅkha-Likhita, Hārīta, Āpastamba, Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Vyāsa, Kātyāyana, Devala, Nārada, and others.
ते एव धर्मशास्त्राणि भवन्ति ।
These alone are the Dharmaśāstras.
तेषु वर्णाश्रमकायिकवाचिकमानसिककर्माण्युक्तानि ।
In them are stated the bodily, verbal, and mental duties appropriate to varṇas and āśramas.
एतेषाम् अपि अन्तःकरणशुद्धिद्वारा ज्ञानोत्पत्त्या मोक्षसिद्धिः एव प्रयोजनम् ।
Even for these, the purpose is solely the attainment of *mokṣa* through the arising of knowledge via the purification of the mind (*antaḥkaraṇa*).
साङ्ख्यशास्त्र-योगशास्त्र-वैष्णवतन्त्र-शैवतन्त्रादीनाम् अपि धर्मशास्त्रे एव अन्तर्भावः ।
The inclusion of the Sāṅkhya treatise, the Yoga treatise, Vaiṣṇava tantras, Śaiva tantras, etc., is also within the Dharmaśāstra itself.
मानसिकोपासनारूपकर्मनिरूपकत्वात् ।
This is because they describe activities in the form of mental meditation (*upāsanā*).
501
साङ्ख्यशास्त्रप्रयोजनम् ।
The purpose of the Sāṅkhya scripture.
कपिलः साङ्ख्यशास्त्रं षडध्यायरूपं रचयाम्बभूव ।
Sage Kapila composed the Sāṅkhya scripture consisting of six chapters.
तत्र प्रथमाध्याये तच्छास्त्रविषयः प्रतिपाद्यते ।
Therein, in the first chapter, the subject-matter of that scripture is expounded.
द्वितीयाध्याये महत्तत्त्वाहङ्कारादयः प्रधानकार्याणि उच्यन्ते ।
In the second chapter, the effects of prakṛti, such as the mahat principle, ego-sense, etc., are declared.
तृतीयाध्याये विषयेभ्यः वैराग्योत्पत्तिः कथ्यते ।
In the third chapter, the generation of dispassion towards sense-objects is described.
चतुर्थाध्याये विरक्तानां चरित्रं निरूप्यते ।
In the fourth chapter, the life stories of dispassionate seekers are delineated.
पञ्चमाध्याये परपक्षः खण्ड्यते ।
In the fifth chapter, the rival views are refuted.
षष्ठाध्याये सकलार्थसङ्ग्रहः कथ्यते ।
In the sixth chapter, a summary of all the doctrines is presented.
कर्तृनाम मूलं व्याख्यानं अन्नम्भट्टः ज्ञानेन्द्रः नागेश्वरः प्रकाशात्मश्रीचरणाः ब्रह्मानन्दसरस्वती भवदेवः रङ्गनाथः स्वयम्प्रकाशानन्दः जगन्नाथयतीश्वरः अमलानन्दः गदाधरः ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं शारीरकभाष्यं ब्रह्मसूत्रं ब्रह्मसूत्रं मिताक्षरी ब्रह्मसूत्रार्थप्रकाशिका ब्रह्मसूत्रेन्दुशेखरं शारीरकमीमांसान्यायसङ्ग्रहः वेदान्तसूत्रमुक्तावली वृत्तिः विद्वज्जनमनोहरः वेदान्तवचनभूषणं भाष्यदीपिका शास्त्रदर्पणं सारार्थसङ्ग्रहः एवं नानाप्रकारा व्याख्यानरूपा ग्रन्था वर्तन्ते ।
Thus there exist various commentary-works along with their authors and source texts [such as Annambhaṭṭa's Mitākṣarī on Brahmasūtra, Jñānendra's Brahmasūtrārthaprakāśikā, Nāgeśvara's Brahmasūtrenduśekhara, Prakāśātmayati's Śārīrakamīmāṁsānyāyasaṅgraha, Brahmānandasarasvatī's Vedāntasūtramuktāvalī, Bhavadeva's Vṛtti, Raṅganātha's Vidvajjnamanohara, Svayamprakāśānanda's Vedāntavacanabhūṣaṇa, Jagannāthayatīśvara's Bhāṣyadīpikā on Śārīrakabhāṣya, Amalānanda's Śāstradarpaṇa on Brahmasūtra, and Gadādhara's Sārārthasaṅgraha on Brahmasūtra].
एते च प्रसङ्गात् मुमुक्षोः स्वसिद्धान्तदृढतरज्ञानसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रतिपादिताः ।
And these have been expounded incidentally so that the seeker of liberation may attain firmer knowledge of his own established doctrine.
प्रकृतिपुरुषविवेकात् पूरुषः असङ्गः इति ज्ञानं साङ्ख्यशास्त्रप्रयोजनम् ।
The purpose of the Sāṅkhya scripture is the knowledge that the *puruṣa* is unattached, born from the discrimination between prakṛti and *puruṣa*.
तच्छास्त्रस्य अपि त्वम्पदलक्ष्यार्थशोधनद्वारा महावाक्यजन्यज्ञानोपयोगित्वात् मोक्षः एव फलम् ।
For that scripture too, because it aids the knowledge generated by the Mahāvākyas through the purification of the implied meaning of the term 'tvam' ('thou'), mokṣa alone is the ultimate fruit.
502
योगशास्त्रप्रयोजनं शारीरकोक्त्यविरोधश्च ।
The purpose of the Yoga scripture and its non-contradiction with the statements of the Śārīraka-sūtras.
योगशास्त्रं पादचतुष्टयोपेतम् ।
The Yoga scripture consists of four chapters (pādas).
तत्कर्ता पतञ्जलिः ।
Its author is Patañjali.
स च आदिशेषावताररूपः ।
And he is an incarnation of Ādiśeṣa.
कस्यचन ऋषेः सन्ध्योपासनसमये तदञ्जलिपुटात् उद्भूय भूमौ पतितत्वात् पतञ्जलिः इति नाम्ना प्रसिद्धः ।
Because he manifested from the folded palms (añjali) of a certain sage during the twilight prayer and fell (patita) to the earth, he became famous by the name Patañjali.
स च स्थूलशरीरगतरोगरूपमलनिवृत्त्यर्थं चिकित्साग्रन्थम् अकरोत् ।
(1) And he composed a medical treatise for the removal of the impurity in the form of diseases belonging to the gross body.
अशुद्धपदोच्चारणरूपवाङ्मलनिवृत्त्यर्थं पाणिनीयव्याकरणस्य भाष्यं चकार ।
(2) For the removal of impurities of speech in the form of incorrect pronunciation of words, he composed the commentary on Pāṇini's grammar (the Mahābhāṣya).
विक्षेपरूपान्तःकरणमलापनयाय योगसूत्रं रचयामास ।
(3) For the eradication of the mind's impurity in the form of distraction, he composed the Yogasūtra.
तत्र च प्रथमपादे चित्तवृत्तिनिरोधरूपः समाधिः तत्साधनभूताः अभ्यासवैराग्यादयः च निरूपिताः ।
And therein, (1) in the first chapter (Samādhi-pāda), samādhi in the form of the cessation of mental modifications, and its means such as practice and dispassion, are expounded.
द्वितीयपादे विक्षिप्तचित्तस्य समाधिसाधनीभूतानि यमनियमासनप्राणायामप्रत्याहारधारणाध्यानसमाधिनामकानि अष्टाङ्गानि उक्तानि ।
(2) In the second chapter (Sādhana-pāda), the eight limbs—named yama, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna, and samādhi—which serve as the means to samādhi for one with a distracted mind, are stated.
तृतीयपादे योगविभूतयः कथिताः ।
(3) In the third chapter (Vibhūti-pāda), the supranormal yogic powers are described.
चतुर्थपादे योगफलभूतः मोक्षः कथितः ।
(4) In the fourth chapter (Kaivalya-pāda), liberation (mokṣa), which is the ultimate fruit of Yoga, is described.
इत्थं योगशास्त्रम् अपि ज्ञानसाधनीभूतनिदिध्यासनसम्पादनद्वारा मोक्षहेतुत्वं प्रतिपद्यते ।
Thus, the Yoga scripture also comes to be a cause of mokṣa through facilitating nididhyāsana (meditation), which serves as a direct means to knowledge.
शारीरकसूत्रेषु यत् साङ्ख्ययोगखण्डनं कृतम्, तत् उपनिषद्विरुद्धार्थप्रतिपादकतद्व्याख्यानखण्डनरूपम् एव ।
Whatever refutation of Sāṅkhya and Yoga is made in the Śārīraka-sūtras is solely a refutation of those commentaries which propound meanings contrary to the Upaniṣads.
न तु मूलसूत्रखण्डनरूपम् ।
It is not, however, a refutation of their original root aphorisms.
एवं न्यायवैशेषिकसूत्रखण्डनम् अपि तद्विरुद्धार्थप्रतिपादकव्याख्यानखण्डनार्थम् एव ।
Likewise, the refutation of the Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika aphorisms is also intended solely to refute those commentaries which propound anti-Vedic views.
503 · पाञ्चरात्रपाशुपतादिप्रवृत्तिप्रयोजनम्- (१) पाञ्चरात्रं
नारदेन पाञ्चरात्रनामकं तन्त्रम् अकारि ।
The tantric scripture named Pāñcarātra was composed by Nārada.
तत्र वासुदेवे अन्तःकरणस्य स्थापनं कथितम् ।
Therein, the fixing of the mind on Lord Vāsudeva is taught.
अतः तस्य अपि अन्तःकरणस्थैर्यसम्पादनात् ज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षः एव फलम् ।
Therefore, for that too, through bringing about steadiness of mind and subsequently knowledge, mokṣa alone is the fruit.
सर्वेषाम् अपि वैष्णवग्रन्थानां पाञ्चरात्रे अन्तर्भावः ।
All Vaiṣṇava texts are subsumed under the Pāñcarātra.
तत् च पाञ्चरात्रं धर्मशास्त्रे अन्तर्भवति ।
And that Pāñcarātra is itself subsumed under the category of Dharmaśāstra.
पाशुपतं — पाशुपततन्त्रे पशुपत्याराधनं कथ्यते ।
(2) Pāśupata: In the Pāśupata Tantra, the worship of Lord Paśupati (Śiva) is expounded.
तत्कर्ता पशुपतिः ।
Its author is Lord Paśupati himself.
तस्य अपि अन्तःकरणनैश्चल्यसम्पादनद्वारा मोक्षसाधनं ज्ञानम् एव फलम् ।
For that too, by way of securing unwavering steadiness of the mind, knowledge—which is the means to mokṣa—is the ultimate fruit.
504
शैवग्रन्थाः सर्वेऽपि पाशुपततन्त्रेऽन्तर्भवन्ति ।
All Śaiva texts are included within the Pāśupata Tantra.
तथैव गणेशसूर्यदेव्याद्युपासनाबोधकानां ग्रन्थानामपि चित्तनिश्चलतासम्पादनद्वारा ज्ञानमेव फलम् ।
Likewise, the fruit of the texts teaching the worship of Gaṇeśa, Sūrya, Devī, and others is knowledge alone through the attainment of steadiness of mind.
सर्वेषामप्येषां धर्मशास्त्रेऽन्तर्भावः ।
All of these are also included within Dharmaśāstra.
तत्र देव्युपासनाबोधकग्रन्थेषु द्वौ सम्प्रदायौ वर्तेते ।
Among the texts teaching the worship of Devī, there are two traditions.
एको दक्षिणसम्प्रदायः ।
One is the Dakṣiṇa tradition (Dakṣiṇācāra).
इतर उत्तरसम्प्रदायः ।
The other is the Uttara tradition (Uttarācāra).
उत्तरसम्प्रदायं वाममार्ग इति कथयन्ति ।
They call the Uttara tradition the Vāmamārga (left-hand path).
तत्र- (१) दक्षिणसम्प्रदायरीत्या ये ग्रन्था देव्युपासनं बोधयन्ति, ते धर्मशास्त्रेऽन्तर्भवन्ति ।
Among them: (1) Those texts which teach Devī-worship according to the Dakṣiṇa tradition are included within Dharmaśāstra.
(२) वाममार्गो यस्मिन्ग्रन्थेऽस्ति, स ग्रन्थो धर्मशास्त्रविरुद्धत्वादप्रमाणं भवति ।
(2) That text in which Vāmamārga is set forth is non-authoritative because it contradicts Dharmaśāstra.
वामतन्त्रमपि यद्यपि परमशिवेनाकारि ।
Although the Vāma-tantra was composed by Paramasiva Himself,
तथापि सर्ववेदशास्त्रविरुद्धत्वान्न तत्प्रमाणं भवति ।
nevertheless, because it contradicts all the Vedas and Śāstras, it is not authoritative.
यथा विष्णुना बुद्धावतारे कृतो नास्तिकग्रन्थो वेदविरुद्धत्वादप्रमाणं भवति ।
Just as the atheistic texts composed by Viṣṇu in the Buddha incarnation are unauthoritative due to their opposition to the Vedas,
तथा शिवकृतं वामतन्त्रमपि ।
so also is the Vāma-tantra composed by Śiva.
तत्र हि मदिरादयोऽनेकेऽत्यन्ताशुद्धाः पदार्था ग्राह्यत्वेन कथिताः ।
For therein many extremely impure substances, such as wine, are prescribed as acceptable.
सर्वलोकवञ्चनार्थं मलिनानपि पदार्थान् उत्तमान् कथयति ।
To deceive all people, it declares even impure substances to be exalted.
तद्यथा मदिरा तीर्थम्, मांसं शुद्धम्, मदिरापात्रं पद्मम्, दुर्जनो व्यासः, लशुनः शुकदेवः, ध्वजी मदिराविक्रयी, मदिरोत्पादको दीक्षितः, वेश्यासेवी चर्मकारिण्यादिसेवी चाण्डाल्यादिसेवी च प्रयागसेवी, काशीसेवी, भैरवीचक्रमध्यवर्तिनो चण्डालादयो ब्राह्मणा इत्यादि ।
For instance: wine is called 'holy water' (tīrtha), meat is 'pure', a wine-pot is a 'lotus', a rogue is 'Vyāsa', garlic is 'Śukadeva', a liquor-distiller is a 'flag-bearer' and wine-seller, a wine-maker is an 'initiated priest' (dīkṣita); one consorting with prostitutes, leather-worker women, or outcaste women is said to be 'resorting to Prayāga or Kāśī'; and outcastes and others seated in the Bhairavī circle are called 'Brāhmaṇas', and so forth.
अत्यन्तव्यभिचारिणी योगिनीति, स्वैरी योगीति च प्रतिपादयति ।
It asserts that an extremely adulterous woman is a 'Yoginī' and a licentious man is a 'Yogī'.
एवमादिर्बहुप्रकारो वाममार्गव्यवहारोऽत्यन्तनिषिद्धोऽपि तत्र वर्तते ।
Such manifold conduct of the Vāmamārga, although strictly forbidden, is found therein.
किञ्च पूजासमयेऽनेकदोषयुक्तामपि स्त्रियमुत्तमा शक्तिरिति कथयति ।
Moreover, at the time of ritual worship, it declares even a woman filled with numerous vices to be the 'supreme Śakti'.
जातितश्चण्डालीमत्यन्तव्यभिचारिणीं रजस्वलामपि स्त्रियं देवीबुद्ध्या पूजनीयां कथयति ।
