तत्रापि वेदाविरुद्धानंशान् वेदानुसारित्वात् केचन मन्दाधिकारिणोऽनुतिष्ठन्ति ।
Even among those systems, some dull aspirants follow those portions that do not contradict the Veda, because of their accord with the Veda.
यद्यपि- (१) साङ्ख्यशास्त्रकर्ता कपिलः ।
Although: (1) The author of the Sāṅkhya system is Kapila.
(२) पातञ्जलस्य कर्ता पतञ्जलिः शेषावतारभूतः ।
(2) The author of the Pātañjala system is Patañjali, an incarnation of Śeṣa.
(३) न्यायशास्त्रकर्ता गौतमः ।
(3) The author of the Nyāya system is Gautama.
(४) वैशेषिकशास्त्रकर्ता कणादः ।
(4) The author of the Vaiśeṣika system is Kaṇāda.
(५) पूर्वमीमांसाकर्ता जैमिनिः ।
(5) The author of Pūrva-mīmāṃsā is Jaimini.
(६) उत्तरमीमांसाकर्ता व्यासः ।
(6) The author of Uttara-mīmāṃsā is Vyāsa.
एतेषां माहात्म्यं च सुप्रसिद्धं सर्वेषाम् ।
And the greatness of all of them is well known.
तस्मादेतेषां वचनरूपं शास्त्रं सर्वमपि सममेव प्रमाणं स्यात् ।
Therefore, all the scriptures comprising their words should be equally authoritative.
तथापि सर्ववाक्येभ्योऽपि वेदवाक्यमेव प्रबलं प्रमाणं भवति ।
Even so, the statement of the Veda alone is a stronger means of valid knowledge than all other statements.
वेदस्य हि कर्ता सर्वेश्वरः ।
For the Lord of all is the author of the Veda.
नैव तत्र भ्रमसंशयप्रमादविप्रलिप्सादयः सन्ति दोषाः ।
In Him, there exist no flaws whatsoever such as error, doubt, inadvertence, or desire to deceive.
तदितरशास्त्रकर्तारस्तु जीवा एव ।
However, the authors of the other scriptures are merely jīvas.
एतेषां भ्रमादयो दोषाः सम्भवेयुरेव ।
Defects such as error and delusion are indeed possible in them.
यद्यपि शास्त्रकाराः सर्वे सर्वज्ञाः कथ्यन्ते ।
Although all the treatise authors are said to be omniscient,
तथापि तेषां सर्वज्ञताया योगमाहात्म्यजन्यत्वाद्युञ्जानयोगिनस्ते भवन्ति ।
still, because their omniscience is produced from the power of yoga, they are merely practicing yogins (yuñjāna-yogins).
ईश्वरसर्वज्ञतायाः स्वभावसिद्धत्वादीश्वरो युक्तयोगी ।
Because the omniscience of the Lord is inherent by nature, the Lord is an ever-united yogin (yukta-yogin).
ध्यानेन पदार्थज्ञानं यस्य जायते स युञ्जानो योगीत्युच्यते ।
One whose knowledge of objects arises through meditation is called a yuñjāna-yogin (practicing yogin).
यस्य पुनः सर्वदा एकरसतया सर्वपदार्थगोचरापरोक्षप्रतीतिर्जायते स युक्तो योगीत्युच्यते ।
On the other hand, one in whom direct perception encompassing all objects arises always and uniformly is called a yukta-yogin (ever-united yogin).
तत्र युक्तयोगिकृतवेद एव प्रबलं प्रमाणम् ।
Between the two, the Veda produced by the yukta-yogin (the Lord) alone is the paramount means of knowledge.
युञ्जानयोगिकृतं शास्त्रान्तरजातं सर्वमपि दुर्बलमेव ।
The whole collection of other scriptures authored by yuñjāna-yogins is indeed weak (of inferior authority).
530
अतो वेदानुसारि शास्त्रमेव प्रमाणम् ।
Therefore, scripture that conforms to the Veda alone is an authoritative means of knowledge.
वेदविरुद्धमप्रमाणमेव ।
Whatever contradicts the Veda is definitely unauthoritative.
पञ्चापि शास्त्राणि अप्रमाणानि ।
All the other five philosophical systems are unauthoritative.
वेदविरुद्धत्वात् ।
This is because they contradict the Veda.
वेदविरोधित्वं तेषां विस्पष्टं निरूपितम् ।
Their opposition to the Veda has been clearly demonstrated.
उत्तरमीमांसा तु न कस्मिंश्चिदप्यंशे वेदविरुद्धा भवति ।
Uttaramīmāṃsā, however, does not contradict the Veda in any aspect whatsoever.
अत एव सा सर्वथा प्रमाणम् ।
For this very reason, it is authoritative in every respect.
शास्त्रान्तराण्यपि क्वचिदंशे वेदानुसारितां तत्र दृष्ट्वा मन्दधियः केचन विश्वसन्ति ।
Seeing conformity to the Veda in some parts of the other systems, some dull-witted people place faith in them.
तथापि वेदविरुद्धांशबाहुल्यात् सुतरां तानि परित्याज्यान्येव ।
Nevertheless, because the portions contradicting the Veda predominate, they must absolutely be renounced.
क्वचिदंशे विरोधेऽपि क्वचिदंशे वेदानुसारित्वात् तान्यपि अङ्गीकार्याण्येवेति चेत् ।
If it is objected: 'Even though there is contradiction in some parts, since they conform to the Veda in other parts, they too should be accepted'—
तर्हि जैनमपि शास्त्रं अहिंसा परमो धर्मः इत्यहिंसांशे न हिंस्यात् सर्वा भूतानि इति वेदानुसारित्वादङ्गीकार्यं स्यात् ।
Then even the Jaina scripture, in its portion on non-violence ('Non-violence is the supreme virtue'), conforming to the Vedic injunction 'One should not harm any living beings', would have to be accepted.
जैनशास्त्रं तु वेदबाह्यत्वेन हेयमेव ।
However, the Jaina scripture is strictly to be rejected because it is completely outside the Veda.
यद्यपि सगुत ईश्वरावतारो बुद्ध इति चोच्यते ।
Although it is said that Sugata (the Buddha) was an incarnation of the Lord,
तद्वचनमपि वेदवत् प्रमाणीकर्तव्यमेव ।
[and therefore one might think] his word too ought to be regarded as authoritative just like the Veda,
तथापि स विप्रलिप्सानिमित्तमेवावततार ।
nevertheless, he incarnated solely for the purpose of delusion.
तस्मात् तद्वचनं सर्वथाप्यप्रमाणमेव ।
Therefore, his words are entirely unauthoritative.
वञ्चनेच्छा विप्रलिप्सा ।
Vipralipsā means the desire to deceive.
अत एव सर्वांशेऽपि वेदानुसारित्वादुत्तरमीमांसैव सर्वथा मुमुक्षुभिरुपादेया ।
Therefore, since it conforms to the Veda in every aspect, Uttaramīmāṃsā alone should by all means be accepted by seekers of liberation.
उत्तरमीमांसा हि सूत्रात्मना श्रीवदव्यासेनाकारि ।
Indeed, Uttaramīmāṃsā was composed in the form of sūtras by Śrī Vedavyāsa.
तद्व्याख्यानानि च नानारूपाणि अनेककृतानि सन्ति ।
And its commentaries are manifold, written by many authors.
तथापि भगवत्पूज्यचरणश्रीशङ्कराचार्यकृतं भाष्यात्मकं व्याख्यानमेव वेदानुसारि वर्तते ।
Even so, the commentary in the form of Bhāṣya written by the revered Śrī Śaṅkarācārya alone conforms fully to the Veda.
नेतराणि ।
The others do not.
पञ्चमतरङ्गे चैतदुक्तम् ।
And this has already been stated in the fifth wave.
तस्माच्छास्त्रान्तराणि सर्वाण्यपि पञ्च अप्रमाणान्येव ।
Therefore, all the other five philosophical treatises are strictly unauthoritative.
531
शास्त्रान्तराणि अप्रमाणानि इति अतः हेयानि, तत्र दृष्टान्तः हेतुः च कथ्यते ।
Other systems of thought are not valid authorities (for liberation) and are therefore to be abandoned; an illustration and the underlying reason are now explained.
अस्मिन् तरङ्गे पूर्वम् शास्त्राणाम् सर्वेषाम् मोक्षोपयोगिता तर्कदृष्टि-सारग्राहि-विवेकवशात् अभिहिता ।
Earlier in this chapter, the auxiliary usefulness of all śāstras towards liberation was stated from the viewpoint of an essence-extracting discernment guided by logic.
यथा कश्चित् शत्रुः असिना रुग्णम् कञ्चित् अच्छिनत् ।
Just as an enemy struck a certain diseased man with a sword,
तदा बहिः रुधिरागमनात् दैवगत्या तद्रोगनिवृत्तिः अभूत् ।
and then, through the outward draining of bad blood by providential chance, his disease was cured;
तत्र सारग्राही पुरुषः स्वशत्रुम् हन्तारम् असिपाणिम् अपि उपकारकत्वेन एव मन्यते ।
in that situation, an essence-discerning person considers even his sword-wielding enemy (who intended to kill him) as a benefactor.
तथा शास्त्रान्तरेण अपि येन केन अपि प्रकारेण अन्तःकरणशुद्धि-नैश्चल्योत्पत्ति-वशात् संसारात् विनिवृत्तस्य पुरुषस्य वेदानुसारि-निश्चय-करणात् मोक्षः जायेत इति न एव अत्र आग्रहः सर्वथा अपि कर्तुम् शक्यते ।
Likewise, if for a person who turns away from worldly life through purity and stillness of mind brought about somehow by other systems, liberation should arise from attaining conviction in accord with the Veda — still, one cannot dogmatically insist that other scriptures are the direct cause.
अन्धगोलाङ्गूलन्यायेन अनर्थप्राप्तिप्रसङ्गात् ।
Because (relying directly on non-Vedāntic śāstras for mokṣa) entails the danger of ruin, just as in the maxim of the blind man holding the cow's tail.
तस्मात् विहाय शास्त्रान्तराणि अपि सकलानि शुद्ध-अद्वैत-व्याख्यान-रीत्या शारीरक-उत्तरमीमांसा एव ग्राह्या ।
Therefore, setting aside all other doctrinal systems, the Śārīraka-Uttaramīmāṃsā alone is to be embraced, in accordance with the exposition of pure Advaita.
532 · अन्धगोलाङ्गूलन्यायः
कस्यचिद्धनिकस्य पुत्रं सर्वाभरणभूषितं चोरा वनमानीयाभरणान्यपि सर्वाण्यपहृत्य तन्नेत्रे बद्ध्वा विजने विसृज्य जग्मुः ।
Thieves brought the son of a wealthy man, who was adorned with all ornaments, into a forest, stole all his ornaments, blindfolded his eyes, abandoned him in a desolate place, and left.
तदा तत्र रुदन्तं तं बालं निर्दयः कश्चिदतिवञ्चकोऽतिबलिष्ठमुन्मत्तं कञ्चिद्बलीवर्दं लाङ्गूले तद्धस्तेन ग्राहयित्वा मा त्यजास्य लाङ्गूलम् , शीघ्रं स्वग्राममनेन प्राप्नोषि इत्यवोचत् ।
Then, to that boy weeping there, a merciless and highly fraudulent person made his hand grasp an extremely strong, mad bull by its tail and said, 'Do not let go of this bull's tail; through this you will reach your village quickly.'
स च दुःखी बालस्तद्वचनं विश्वस्य तदुक्तमनुष्ठाय ततोऽपि महत् दुःखमनुभूय विनष्टोऽभूत् ।
And that suffering boy, believing his words and doing as told, experienced even greater misery and perished.
तद्वद्विषयरूपाश्चोरा विवेकाख्यं नेत्रं पिधाय संसारवने मुमुक्षुं सन्त्यजन्ति ।
In the same way, the thieves in the form of sense-objects cover the eye called discrimination (*viveka*) and abandon the seeker (*mumukṣu*) in the forest of *saṃsāra*.
तदा भेदवादी मतान्तरस्थो निर्दयवञ्चकोऽन्यशास्त्रसिद्धान्ते तस्य विश्वासं जनयित्वा अस्मदुपदेश एव तव परमसुखप्राप्तिहेतुः , मा त्यजैनम् इति उपदिशति ।
Then, a merciless deceiver upholding duality and belonging to an erroneous school creates faith in him towards the doctrine of other systems and instructs: 'Our teaching alone is the cause of attaining supreme bliss; do not abandon this!'
मन्दतमो ह्यधिकारी तद्वाक्यमेव विश्वस्य तदुक्तमाचरन् परमपुरुषार्थसुखरहितो जननमरणरूपं महद्दुःखमनुभवेत् ।
Indeed, the dullest aspirant, believing his words alone and practicing what he prescribed, becomes deprived of the bliss of the supreme goal of human life (*parama-puruṣārtha*) and suffers the great misery of birth and death.
अतः शास्त्रान्तराणि मुमुक्षुणा म्लेच्छशास्त्रवद्दूरतस्त्याज्यान्येव ।
Therefore, non-Vedic / rival treatises must certainly be discarded from afar by the seeker of liberation, just like the teachings of barbarians.
533 · राज्ञो मरणानन्तरं ब्रह्मलोकप्राप्तिः
इत्थं शुभसन्ततिर्नाम राजा तर्कदृष्टेः स्वपुत्रस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वसंशयान् समस्तमनःशोकांश्च सन्त्यज्य पूर्णानन्दमवाप ।
Thus the king named Śubhasantati, having heard the words of his son Tarkadṛṣṭi, cast aside all doubts and all mental sorrow, and attained complete bliss.
कारणब्रह्मोपसानायां बहुशश्चित्तलयं चकार ।
He repeatedly absorbed his mind in meditation upon the causal Brahman.
तर्कदृष्टिमेव स्वगुरुत्वेन भावयित्वा विशिष्टं राज्यं तस्मा अदात् ।
Regarding Tarkadṛṣṭi as his very Guru, he bestowed his distinguished kingdom upon him.
पुत्रोऽपि तर्कदृष्टिरुत्तमोपदेशकर्तृत्वाद्गुरुपदवीं भेजे ।
The son Tarkadṛṣṭi, on account of being the dispenser of sublime instruction, assumed the rank of a Guru.
तदेतत् सर्वं ब्रह्मविद्याया माहात्म्यमेव ।
All this is solely the glory of Brahmavidyā.
534 · शुभसन्ततिमरणम्
कतिपयदिवसानन्तरं राजा प्राणान् सञ्जहौ ।
After a few days, the king gave up his life-breaths.
सनकादिमुनिगणप्राप्यं ब्रह्मलोकं च जगाम ।
And he attained *Brahmaloka*, which is attained by the hosts of sages such as Sanaka.
न हि राज्ञो मरणे देशकालादिनियमोक्तिरस्ति ।
Indeed, there is no statement specifying restrictions of place, time, etc., regarding the king's death.
अस्यायमभिप्रायः — उपासकमरणविषये न देशकालादिव्यपेक्षास्ति ।
The purport of this is: in the case of a meditator's death, there is no dependence on place, time, and so forth.
अहनि वा रात्रौ वा दक्षिणायने वा उत्तरायणे वा शुद्धे वाप्यशुद्धे देशे मृतोऽप्युपासनाबलात् स सर्वथापि देवयानेन पथा ब्रह्मलोकमेव गच्छति ।
Whether dying by day or by night, in *dakṣiṇāyana* or in *uttarāyaṇa*, in a pure place or in an impure place, by the power of his *upāsanā* he definitely goes only to *Brahmaloka* along the path of the gods (*devayāna*).
अदृष्टिप्रसङ्गे पूर्वं देशकालाद्यपेक्षा स्यादिति यदुक्तं तदयोगसहितोपासकविषयम् ।
What was stated earlier in the episode of Adṛṣṭi — that there is a dependence on place, time, etc. — applied only to a meditator lacking complete yoga.
केवलेश्वरैकशरणतां गतस्योपसकस्य नैवास्ति देशकालाद्यपेक्षा ।
For a meditator who has surrendered completely to Īśvara alone, there is absolutely no dependence on place, time, and so forth.
प्रतिपादितश्चायमर्थः सूत्रभाष्यकारादिभिः ।
